definition_zh: 蛹的；蛹期的；蛹壳的；蛹室的；蛹体发育的；蛹期蜕皮的；蛰伏静止的（比喻）；寄生于蛹的
definition_en: relating to a pupa or to the stage between larva and adult, when an insect stops feeding and its body is rebuilt inside a case
core_image: 土室里裂开一枚蛹壳，旁边还留着幼虫蜕下的干皮，翅已在壳内折好
scene: 土室中，一枚蛹壳裂开，旁边留着幼虫蜕下的干皮。 A pupal case lies split in the soil chamber beside the larva's shed skin.
sceneCN: 这里 pupal 指「与蛹、蛹壳有关的」（第 3 个义项：蛹壳的）；句意为土室中的蛹壳裂开，旁边留着幼虫蜕下的皮。可辨识物件：裂开的蛹壳、干皮、土室壁、折好的翅。

pos.zh: 蛹的；蛹期的；蛹状的

senses.title: Of or belonging to a pupa
senses.definition: relating to a pupa, the stage between larva and adult in complete metamorphosis
senses.definitionCN: 与蛹有关，即完全变态中幼虫与成虫之间的阶段
senses.example: The pupal skin hardens within a day of formation.
senses.exampleCN: 蛹的皮在形成后一天之内变硬。
senses.why: The suffix -al makes a plain relational adjective, so pupal answers the question 'which stage?' rather than describing a quality.
senses.whyCN: 后缀 -al 构成纯粹的关系形容词，因此 pupal 回答的是「哪个阶段」，而非描述某种性质。

senses.title: The interval before adulthood
senses.titleCN: 化蛹到羽化之间的时段
senses.definition: the period during which the insect does not feed and its tissues are reorganised
senses.definitionCN: 昆虫不取食、组织被重组的那段时间
senses.example: Pupal duration depends strongly on temperature.
senses.exampleCN: 蛹期的长短高度依赖温度。
senses.why: This sense measures time, and in rearing records it is a number of days rather than a description.
senses.whyCN: 这一义度量时间，在饲养记录中是一串天数而非描述。

senses.title: The hardened case
senses.definition: the protective outer case of the pupa, including the hardened last larval skin of many flies
senses.definitionCN: 蛹的保护性外壳，包括许多蝇类硬化后的末龄幼虫皮
senses.example: A pupal case lies split in the soil chamber beside the larva's shed skin.
senses.exampleCN: 土室中的蛹壳裂开，旁边留着幼虫蜕下的皮。
senses.why: The case is not the animal; distinguishing them matters because fly puparia are modified larval skins.
senses.whyCN: 壳不是动物本身；区分两者很重要，因为蝇类的蛹壳是改造过的幼虫皮。

senses.title: The chamber built for pupation
senses.definition: the cavity or cell an insect prepares for pupation, in soil, wood or a silk shelter
senses.definitionCN: 昆虫为化蛹准备的腔室或巢房，可在土中、木内或丝质庇护所里
senses.example: The beetle excavated a pupal chamber beneath the bark.
senses.exampleCN: 甲虫在树皮下挖出一个蛹室。
senses.why: This sense attaches the adjective to a place, a common pattern in ecology and behaviour studies.
senses.whyCN: 这一义把形容词挂到地点上，是生态与行为研究中常见的模式。

senses.title: Development inside the case
senses.definition: the internal growth and differentiation that turns larval tissue into adult structures
senses.definitionCN: 把幼虫组织转变为成虫结构的内部生长与分化
senses.example: Pupal development reconstructs the wings and eyes entirely.
senses.exampleCN: 蛹期发育把翅与眼完全重建。
senses.why: The phrase pupal development names a process, not an object, and it is the sense used in physiology.
senses.whyCN: 「pupal development」指一个过程而非物件，是生理学中使用的义。

senses.title: The pupal moult
senses.definition: the shedding of the last larval skin that produces the pupa, or the moult that releases the adult
senses.definitionCN: 产生蛹时蜕去末龄幼虫皮，或羽化时进行的那次蜕皮
senses.example: The pupal moult leaves a dry skin beside the case.
senses.exampleCN: 蛹期蜕皮在壳旁留下了一张干皮。
senses.why: Moulting bookends the stage, so the adjective can mark either the entry or the exit.
senses.whyCN: 蜕皮在这一阶段的两端，因此形容词既可指进入也可指离开。

senses.title: A dormant, waiting state
senses.definition: used figuratively for a quiet interval in which something is being remade before it reappears
senses.definitionCN: 比喻用法，指某物在重新出现之前被改造的安静间歇
senses.example: The old factory spent a pupal winter and reopened as a studio.
senses.exampleCN: 那座旧工厂度过了一个「蛹期」的冬天，重新开张时成了工作室。
senses.why: The metaphor keeps the stillness and the promise of emergence, which is why it suits institutions as well as insects.
senses.whyCN: 比喻保留了静止与将要羽化的许诺，因此既适用于机构也适用于昆虫。

senses.title: Living on a pupa
senses.definition: describing a parasitoid that attacks the pupal stage and emerges from it
senses.definitionCN: 描述攻击蛹期并从蛹中出来的寄生蜂或寄生昆虫
senses.example: A pupal parasitoid emerged from the moth's case in spring.
senses.exampleCN: 一只蛹寄生蜂在春天从蛾蛹壳中钻出。
senses.why: This technical sense narrows the adjective to a host stage, a standard usage in biological control.
senses.whyCN: 这一技术义把形容词收窄到寄主阶段，是生物防治中的标准用法。

intro.en: Pupal is pupa plus the relational suffix -al. The base noun is Latin pupa 'girl, doll', which Linnaeus reused for the insect stage.
intro.cn: pupal 由 pupa 加关系后缀 -al 构成。基名词是拉丁 pupa「女孩、玩偶」，林奈改用于昆虫阶段。

items.en: Latin pupa meant a doll or a girl; the entomological sense came only in the eighteenth century.
items.cn: 拉丁 pupa 指玩偶或女孩；昆虫学义到 18 世纪才出现。

items.en: Latin -alis became English -al and forms relational adjectives from nouns, as in fate and fatal or nation and national.
items.cn: 拉丁 -alis 变成英语 -al，从名词构成关系形容词，如 fate 与 fatal、nation 与 national。

items.en: Pupal was coined in English on this pattern inside natural-history writing, not borrowed as a whole word from Latin.
items.cn: pupal 是英语在自然史写作中按这一模式新造的，并非整词借自拉丁。

items.en: Entomology uses pupal for stage, case, chamber and development, so one adjective covers time, object, place and process.
items.cn: 昆虫学把 pupal 用于阶段、壳、室与发育，一个形容词覆盖时间、物件、地点与过程。

items.en: Biological control writes of pupal parasitoids, and laboratory protocols write of pupal duration, extending the word beyond description.
items.cn: 生物防治写「pupal parasitoid」，实验室方案写「pupal duration」，把词扩展到描述之外。

items.en: Source uncertain (detail and first date): the deeper origin and the exact first citation are not settled, so any pre-Latin form offered here is a reconstruction and competing hypotheses are left side by side.
items.cn: 来源不确定（细节与首见年代）：更深的来源与确切最早书证均无定论，此处给出的拉丁语之前形式属重构形式，并列假说一并保留、不作定论。

note.en: Group one separates pupal from the noun and from look-alike words; group two lists adjectives for neighbouring stages.
note.cn: 第一组把 pupal 与名词及形近词分开；第二组列出相邻阶段的形容词。

entries.definition: Pupa names the animal; pupal describes it, so the two are not interchangeable.
entries.definitionCN: pupa 指动物；pupal 描述它，两者不能互换。

entries.definition: Pupae is a plural noun, not an adjective, and cannot modify stage or case.
entries.definitionCN: pupae 是复数名词，不是形容词，不能修饰 stage 或 case。

entries.definition: Pupil sounds identical but means a student or the eye's opening, from a different branch of the same Latin family.
entries.definitionCN: pupil 读音相同，却指学生或瞳孔，出自同一拉丁词族的另一分支。

entries.definition: Puppet shares the doll ancestor but has no biological sense at all.
entries.definitionCN: puppet 共享玩偶这一祖先，却完全没有生物学义。

entries.definition: Larval marks the feeding, growing stage that precedes the pupa.
entries.definitionCN: larval 标出蛹之前取食、生长的阶段。

entries.definition: Nymphal describes the young of insects that have no pupal stage at all.
entries.definitionCN: nymphal 描述完全没有蛹期的不完全变态昆虫幼期。

entries.definition: Chrysalid is a rare adjective for the butterfly's uncovered pupal case.
entries.definitionCN: chrysalid 是描述蝴蝶裸露蛹壳的罕见形容词。

entries.definition: Dormant is the general word for an inactive period, which pupal only implies.
entries.definitionCN: dormant 是一般的「不活动」说法，pupal 只暗含这一层。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real collocations and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: Pupa plus -al gives the relational adjective, the same pattern as fate and fatal.
normal.cn: pupa 加 -al 构成关系形容词，与 fate / fatal 同一模式。

normal.en: The family runs pupa, pupae, pupal, pupate, pupation and puparium.
normal.cn: 词族包括 pupa、pupae、pupal、pupate、pupation 与 puparium。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark the senses: pupal stage, pupal case, pupal chamber.
normal.cn: 固定搭配标出各义项：蛹期、蛹壳、蛹室。

normal.en: The adjective covers time, shell, place and process, four different questions.
normal.cn: 这个形容词覆盖时间、外壳、地点与过程四类不同问题。

normal.en: Do not confuse pupal with pupil: one is a stage, the other a student or an eye.
normal.cn: 别把 pupal 与 pupil 混淆：一个是阶段，一个是学生或瞳孔。

abstract.en: Picture a sealed workshop where the old body is taken apart.
abstract.cn: 想象一间封闭的工场，旧身体正在被拆开。

abstract.en: Picture a dry skin left on the floor like a receipt for the change.
abstract.cn: 想象一张干皮留在地上，像这场变化的收据。

abstract.en: Picture a factory that goes quiet for one winter and reopens as something else.
abstract.cn: 想象一座工厂静默一个冬天，再开时已换了个模样。

examples.en: Pupal colour often matches the bark so the case is hard to see.
examples.cn: 蛹的颜色常与树皮一致，使蛹壳很难被发现。

examples.en: The wasp searches for a pupal host beneath the leaf litter.
examples.cn: 这种蜂在落叶层下寻找蛹期寄主。

examples.en: Pupal duration fell by three days when the rearing room was warmed.
examples.cn: 饲养室升温后，蛹期缩短了三天。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「pupal（普泡）」——泡在壳里不动的阶段 → 蛹的

root: pupa（拉丁「女孩、玩偶」，林奈改用为蛹）+ 关系后缀 -al（拉丁 -alis）。属英语在拉丁词基上构成的形容词。pupa 的更早来源不确定。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses apply the adjective to the animal, the interval, the shell, the chamber, the inner development, the moult, a metaphor of dormancy and a parasitoid's host stage.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项把形容词用于动物、时段、外壳、蛹室、内部发育、蜕皮、蛰伏比喻，以及寄生者的寄主阶段。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a split case in a soil chamber, a shed larval skin beside it and folded wings inside.
core.cn: 核心意象：土室中裂开的蛹壳，旁边是蜕下的幼虫皮，壳内是折好的翅。

branches.en: PLAIN RELATION: the suffix asks only which stage is meant.
branches.cn: 纯粹关系：后缀只问指的是哪个阶段。

branches.en: TIME AND PROCESS: duration, inner rebuilding and the moult all describe a remaking that takes time.
branches.cn: 时间与过程：时长、内部重建与蜕皮都描述一段耗时的改造。

branches.en: CASE AND PLACE: the shell protects and the chamber hides.
branches.cn: 壳与地点：外壳保护，蛹室隐藏。

branches.en: DORMANCY: the quiet interval becomes a metaphor for reinvention.
branches.cn: 蛰伏：安静的间歇成为再造的比喻。

branches.en: HOST STAGE: another insect uses the pupa as food.
branches.cn: 寄主阶段：另一种昆虫把蛹当作食物。

intro.en: Pupal is the relational adjective of pupa; the family's other members add -ate, -ation, -arium and -parous to the same stem.
intro.cn: pupal 是 pupa 的关系形容词；词族其它成员在同一词干上加 -ate、-ation、-arium 与 -parous。

latinIntro.en: Latin pupa and its plural pupae supply pup-, which English extends with -al, -ate, -ation, -arium and -gerous.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 pupa 及其复数 pupae 提供词干 pup-，英语用 -al、-ate、-ation、-arium、-gerous 扩展。

items.example: The pupal case is hard and dry.
The puparium split along its top.
Pupiparous flies avoid the larval stage.
items.exampleCN: 蛹生蝇类跳过幼虫阶段。

definition_zh: 学习；通过学习获得知识与技能的过程，也可指所获得的学问
definition_en: the process of gaining knowledge or skill, or the knowledge so gained
core_image: 一个人把反复试错的结果留在手上，下一次动作更稳
scene: 琴房里，孩子一遍遍纠正指法，几周后同一段曲子终于不再出错。 The child corrects her fingering again and again until the passage comes out right, and that slow change is learning.
sceneCN: 这里 learning 指「通过反复练习获得技能的过程」（第 1 个义项：练习带来行为上的稳定改变）；句意为孩子一遍遍纠正指法，直到同一段曲子不再出错。图中可辨识物件：琴键、节拍器、翻开的乐谱、反复移动的手。

pos.zh: 学习；学问；学习活动（不可数）

derivatives.zh: 有学问的（另作「学习」的过去式）
忘掉（已学的东西）；改掉旧习

senses.title: The process of acquiring knowledge or skill
senses.titleCN: 获得知识与技能的过程
senses.definition: the process by which a person or animal gains knowledge, understanding or skill
senses.definitionCN: 人或动物获得知识、理解或技能的过程
senses.example: The child corrects her fingering until the passage comes out right.
senses.exampleCN: 孩子不断纠正指法，直到这段曲子不再出错。
senses.why: the -ing form names the activity itself, not one finished result: learning is what happens while the skill is still being built.
senses.whyCN: -ing 形式命名活动本身，而不是某个完成的结果：learning 是技能仍在形成时发生的事。

senses.title: Knowledge that has been gained
senses.definition: the body of knowledge a person has acquired through study
senses.definitionCN: 一个人通过学习积累起来的知识总体
senses.example: Her learning was obvious in the range of sources she cited.
senses.exampleCN: 她引用的资料范围之广，显露出她的学识。
senses.why: an activity can also name its product; what has been learned stays as a store that others can recognize.
senses.whyCN: 活动也可以命名其产物；学到的东西留成一份储备，旁人能够辨认。

senses.title: Change of behavior through experience
senses.definition: a lasting change in behavior produced by experience rather than by instinct or maturation
senses.definitionCN: 由经验而非本能或成熟带来的持久行为改变
senses.example: The rat avoids the gate after one mild shock.
senses.exampleCN: 老鼠被轻微电击一次后就避开那道门。
senses.why: psychology defined learning operationally: if experience changes what an animal does, learning has occurred, whatever the inner state.
senses.whyCN: 心理学从操作上定义学习：只要经验改变了动物的行为，就算发生了学习，不论内部状态如何。

senses.title: Machine learning
senses.definition: the field in which computer systems improve their performance by finding patterns in data
senses.definitionCN: 计算机系统通过从数据中发现模式而改进性能的领域
senses.example: The model improves its predictions after seeing more examples.
senses.exampleCN: 模型看过更多样本后，预测变得更准。
senses.why: the metaphor is exact enough to be technical: a machine adjusts its internal parameters from experience, as an animal adjusts behavior.
senses.whyCN: 这个比喻精确到足以成为术语：机器像动物调整行为那样，从经验中调整内部参数。

senses.title: School study and instruction
senses.definition: organized study within a course, curriculum or training programme
senses.definitionCN: 课程、教学大纲或培训项目中的有组织学习
senses.example: The school measures learning through projects, not only tests.
senses.exampleCN: 这所学校通过项目而不只是考试来衡量学习。
senses.why: institutions need a countable domain, so the general process is narrowed to what happens inside a programme.
senses.whyCN: 机构需要一个可管理的领域，于是把一般过程收窄为课程之内发生的事。

senses.title: Memorization by repetition
senses.definition: the act of fixing facts in memory through repeated study or recitation
senses.definitionCN: 通过反复学习或背诵把事实固定在记忆中
senses.example: Learning the dates took three evenings of repetition.
senses.exampleCN: 记住这些年代花了三个晚上的反复背诵。
senses.why: repetition is the oldest method of learning, and in ordinary speech the word often narrows to this visible, countable effort.
senses.whyCN: 重复是最古老的学习方法；在日常说法中，这个词常收窄为这种看得见、可计数的努力。

senses.title: Learning ability or difficulty
senses.definition: the capacity to learn, or a diagnosed obstacle to it, as in learning disability
senses.definitionCN: 学习的能力，或被诊断出的学习障碍，如学习障碍症
senses.example: The assessment distinguishes a language barrier from a learning difficulty.
senses.exampleCN: 这项评估把语言障碍与学习困难区分开来。
senses.why: when used attributively, learning names the capacity being measured, which is why learning disability is about ability, not about effort.
senses.whyCN: 作定语时，learning 指被测量的能力，因此「学习障碍」这一说法关乎能力，而非努力程度。

senses.title: A lesson drawn from experience
senses.definition: the understanding gained from an event, especially a mistake
senses.definitionCN: 从事件、尤指错误中获得的认识
senses.example: The failed launch taught the team a costly lesson.
senses.exampleCN: 那次失败的发射给团队上了昂贵的一课。
senses.why: experience can teach without a teacher; the word extends to any change in understanding that comes from what happened.
senses.whyCN: 经验可以没有老师也教人；这个词扩展到因发生的事情而产生的任何认识改变。

intro.en: Learning is native English: Old English leornung 'study' from leornian 'to learn', with no Latin cognate. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: learning 是英语本族词：古英语 leornung「学习」来自 leornian「学」，没有拉丁同族词。年代为约数。

items.en: Leornian meant 'to get knowledge, study, read, think about'; the noun leornung named the activity and its result.
items.cn: leornian 意为「获得知识、学习、阅读、思考」；名词 leornung 指这项活动及其结果。

items.en: The verb goes back to a reconstructed Proto-Germanic form usually written *liznojan, also the source of German lernen and Dutch leren.
items.cn: 这个动词可追溯到原始日耳曼语的重构形式，通常写作 *liznojan，也是德语 lernen 与荷兰语 leren 的来源。

items.en: The deeper root is reconstructed as *leis- 'track, furrow'; learning would then be pictured as following a track until it is known.
items.cn: 更早的词根被重构为 *leis-「痕迹、犁沟」；按此设想，学习就是循着痕迹走到熟悉为止。

items.en: Middle English kept learning for study and also for the knowledge gained; the modern gerund simply continues the same noun.
items.cn: 中古英语用 learning 既指学习也指所得的学问；现代英语的动名词只是延续同一个名词。

items.en: The technical sense dates from the mid-twentieth century, when programmers began to speak of machines that improve from data.
items.cn: 技术义形成于 20 世纪中期，当时程序员开始谈论能从数据中改进的机器。

items.en: Source uncertain (first dates): the exact transition from 'the act of studying' to 'the knowledge possessed' is not dated, and the pre-Germanic reconstruction *leis- remains a hypothesis.
items.cn: 来源不确定（首见年代）：从「学习这一动作」到「拥有的学问」的确切转变没有年代记录；印欧语前的 *leis- 重构仍属假说。

note.en: Group one holds forms of the same verb that are easily confused; group two holds words about gaining knowledge with different emphases.
note.cn: 第一组是同一动词的易混形式；第二组是同样关于获取知识、但侧重不同的词。

entries.definition: To gain knowledge or skill; learning is the noun made from it, so the two cannot replace each other in a sentence.
entries.definitionCN: 获得知识或技能；learning 是由它构成的名词，二者在句中不能互换。

entries.definition: As an adjective, 'having much knowledge', pronounced with two syllables; as a participle, 'having learned', pronounced as one.
entries.definitionCN: 作形容词意为「有学问的」，读两个音节；作分词意为「已学会的」，读一个音节。

entries.definition: A person who is learning; the -er suffix names the agent, while -ing names the activity.
entries.definitionCN: 正在学习的人；-er 后缀命名施动者，-ing 命名活动。

entries.definition: A period of teaching or a piece of instruction; historically from Latin lectio 'a reading', not from learn.
entries.definitionCN: 一堂课或一段教学内容；历史上来自拉丁 lectio「诵读」，并非由 learn 派生。

entries.definition: The whole process and system of teaching, usually formal; learning can happen without any system.
entries.definitionCN: 教学的全过程与制度，通常指正规教育；learning 可以在没有任何制度的情况下发生。

entries.definition: The activity of reading and working to learn; it names the effort, while learning names the change that results.
entries.definitionCN: 阅读与用功以求得知识的活动；指付出的努力，而 learning 指由此产生的改变。

entries.definition: Instruction aimed at a specific skill or job; it is narrower and more practical than learning.
entries.definitionCN: 针对某项技能或工作的训练；比 learning 更窄、更实用。

entries.definition: The information and understanding a person holds; learning is the process or the acquired body of it.
entries.definitionCN: 一个人掌握的信息与理解；learning 是过程或所获得的那部分学问。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real collocations and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: learn + -ing: the suffix turns the verb into the ongoing activity and its accumulated result.
normal.cn: learn + -ing：后缀把动词变成正在进行的活动及其积累的结果。

normal.en: The family runs learn, learner, learned, learnable and unlearn.
normal.cn: 同族词包括 learn、learner、learned、learnable 与 unlearn。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark the range: learning process, learning environment, lifelong learning, machine learning.
normal.cn: 固定搭配标出范围：学习过程、学习环境、终身学习、机器学习。

normal.en: Old English leornian is unrelated to Latin, so do not look for a Latin root.
normal.cn: 古英语 leornian 与拉丁语无关，因此不要去找拉丁词根。

normal.en: Learned as an adjective has two syllables; as a past participle it has one.
normal.cn: learned 作形容词时读两个音节，作过去分词时读一个音节。

abstract.en: Picture a path worn into grass by feet that keep taking the same route.
abstract.cn: 想象一条被反复踩出的草径，脚总走同一条路线。

abstract.en: Picture a hand that fumbles a knot ten times and then ties it without looking.
abstract.cn: 想象一只手打了十次都打不好的结，后来不看也能系上。

abstract.en: Picture a machine that adjusts one number after every mistake.
abstract.cn: 想象一台机器，每犯一次错就调整一个数字。

examples.en: Learning a language takes regular contact, not one long session.
examples.cn: 学一门语言需要经常接触，而不是一次长时间的苦学。

examples.en: The programme measures learning through real tasks.
examples.cn: 该项目通过真实任务来衡量学习。

examples.en: Machine learning models improve as they see more data.
examples.cn: 机器学习模型随着看到更多数据而改进。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「勒宁」——把知识勒进脑子里，留下痕迹 → 学习、学问

root: 古英语 leornung「学习」源自 leornian「学」，属日耳曼语族；更早可重构为原始日耳曼语 *liznojan，无拉丁同族词。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses move from the activity to its product: studying, the knowledge stored, the behavior changed, the machine that improves, the classroom, the repetition, the ability and the lesson.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项从活动走向产物：学习、积累的学问、被改变的行为、会改进的机器、课堂、重复、能力，以及教训。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a repeated attempt that leaves a trace, so the next attempt is steadier.
core.cn: 核心意象：反复的尝试留下痕迹，于是下一次尝试更稳。

branches.en: THE LOOP: trying, noticing and repeating is the minimal unit of learning.
branches.cn: 循环：尝试、察觉与重复构成学习的最小单位。

branches.en: THE STORE: what remains after the loop becomes knowledge one can show.
branches.cn: 储备：循环之后留下的东西，成为可以展示的学问。

branches.en: BEHAVIOR AND REPETITION: psychology measures the change; recitation is its oldest method.
branches.cn: 行为与重复：心理学测量改变，背诵是最古老的方法。

branches.en: TRANSFER: the same loop is given to machines and to classrooms.
branches.cn: 迁移：同一条循环被交给机器，也被交给课堂。

branches.en: CAPACITY AND LESSON: learning can be measured as ability or remembered as a warning.
branches.cn: 能力与教训：学习既可作为能力被测量，也可作为警示被记住。

intro.en: Learning is a Germanic root plus the productive -ing suffix; because the root has no Latin relative, the borrowed side of the family is empty.
intro.cn: learning 是日耳曼语词根加能产的 -ing 后缀；由于该词根没有拉丁同族词，借词一侧的词族为空。

latinIntro.en: There is no reliable Latin cognate for learn, so latinEntries is left empty. Latin discere 'to learn' and studere 'to strive' belong to different families.
latinIntro.cn: learn 没有可靠的拉丁同族词，因此拉丁词条留空。拉丁 discere「学习」与 studere「努力」属于不同词族。

items.example: Children learn by copying and correcting.
items.exampleCN: 孩子通过模仿与纠正来学习。

items.meaning: the act, process or result of an action
items.example: The suffix turns learn into a name for the activity.
items.exampleCN: 这个后缀把 learn 变成活动的名称。

items.example: A learner needs feedback, not only input.
items.exampleCN: 学习者需要反馈，而不只是输入。

items.example: A learned judge cites many sources.
items.exampleCN: 博学的法官会引用许多资料。

items.example: Most skills are learnable with practice.
items.exampleCN: 大多数技能都能通过练习学会。

items.meaning: to discard a learned habit or belief
items.meaningCN: 忘掉已学的东西；改掉旧习
items.example: Drivers must unlearn the old habit.

items.meaning: traditional knowledge passed by word of mouth
items.example: Folk lore preserves what schools do not teach.
items.exampleCN: 民间传说保存了学校不教的东西。

items.example: Leornian is the direct ancestor of learn.
items.exampleCN: leornian 是 learn 的直接祖词。

definition_zh: 相互依赖；相互依存；（生态、经济、政治上的）互赖关系
definition_en: the condition in which two or more people, groups, species, or systems depend on each other for survival, support, or normal functioning
core_image: 两个人各扶住同一架梯子的一端：谁松手，两人都会摔下来
scene: 全球经济课上，教授指着供应链图说，一处缺货就能波及全世界。 Global supply chains show how deep the interdependence of nations has become.
sceneCN: 这里 interdependence 是「相互依赖」（第 1 个义项：双方彼此需要才能运转）；句意：全球供应链显示出各国之间的相互依赖有多深。

pos.zh: 相互依赖；相互依存（不可数，指状态；可数时指一种具体的互赖关系）
（专业）互赖：经济、生态、国际政治等领域的术语（常带修饰语）

collocations.zh: A 与 B 之间的相互依赖
复合相互依存（国际关系术语）

senses.title: Mutual reliance in general
senses.titleCN: 一般意义上的相互依赖
senses.definition: a situation in which each of two or more parties needs the others in order to function or succeed
senses.definitionCN: 两个或更多方中，每一方都需要其他方才能运转或成功的情形
senses.example: The partnership rests on a genuine interdependence rather than one-sided need.
senses.exampleCN: 这种伙伴关系建立在真正的相互依赖之上，而不是单方面的需要。
senses.why: Interdependence adds inter- 'between' to dependence, from Latin dependere 'hang from', built on de- 'down' and pendere 'hang'. The image is a weight hanging from a hook: each side is a support for the other, so neither can simply let go.
senses.whyCN: interdependence 在 dependence 上加 inter-“在……之间”，而 dependence 源自拉丁语 dependere“悬挂于”，由 de-“向下”与 pendere“悬挂”构成。意象是重物挂在钩上：每一方都是对方的支点，谁都不能随便松手。

senses.title: Economic interdependence
senses.definition: the condition in which economies rely on each other for trade, investment, and supply
senses.definitionCN: 各经济体在贸易、投资与供应上彼此依赖的状态
senses.example: Trade data show how quickly economic interdependence transmits a local shortage.
senses.exampleCN: 贸易数据表明，经济互赖会让局部短缺迅速传导。
senses.why: Economics adopted the noun to describe gains and risks of the same fact: specialisation raises output but also exposes each country to shocks elsewhere. The word names a two-sided vulnerability, not merely cooperation.
senses.whyCN: 经济学采用这个名词来描述同一事实的两面：专业化提高产量，也让每个国家暴露在他处的冲击之下。这个词命名的是双向的脆弱性，而不只是合作。

senses.title: Ecological interdependence
senses.definition: the reliance of species and habitats on one another within an ecosystem
senses.definitionCN: 生态系统内物种与栖息地彼此依赖的关系
senses.example: Pollinators and flowering plants show a clear interdependence.
senses.exampleCN: 传粉昆虫与开花植物表现出明显的相互依存。
senses.why: Ecology generalised the word to food webs: a predator depends on prey, and prey numbers depend on predators. Removal of one node is felt elsewhere, which is exactly what the hanging image predicts.
senses.whyCN: 生态学把这个词推广到食物网：捕食者依赖猎物，猎物的数量又取决于捕食者。移除一个节点，别处就会感到，这正是悬挂意象所预示的。

senses.title: Psychological or social reliance
senses.titleCN: 心理与社会层面的互赖
senses.definition: a relationship in which people rely on one another for emotional support, care, or daily tasks
senses.definitionCN: 人们彼此依赖以获得情感支持、照料或完成日常事务的关系
senses.example: Healthy families balance interdependence with personal autonomy.
senses.exampleCN: 健康的家庭在相互依赖与个人自主之间取得平衡。
senses.why: Psychology uses the noun for mature reliance: needing others without losing oneself. It is contrasted with 'dependence' as a pathology, because inter- makes the reliance reciprocal and therefore non-exploitative.
senses.whyCN: 心理学用这个名词指成熟的依赖：需要他人而不失去自我。它与作为病态的 dependence 相对，因为 inter- 使依赖成为相互的，因而没有剥削性。

senses.title: Complex interdependence in politics
senses.titleCN: 国际政治中的复合相互依存
senses.definition: the condition in which states are linked through many channels so that force becomes costly and less useful
senses.definitionCN: 各国通过多种渠道相连，以致使用武力代价高昂且效用下降的状态
senses.example: The theory of complex interdependence explains why trade disputes rarely become wars.
senses.exampleCN: 复合相互依存理论解释了贸易争端为何很少演变为战争。
senses.why: Robert Keohane and Joseph Nye made the phrase a term of international relations in the 1970s. The word carries their argument: multiple channels of contact change the calculus of power.
senses.whyCN: 罗伯特·基欧汉与约瑟夫·奈在 1970 年代把这个说法变成国际关系术语。这个词承载着他们的论点：多渠道的接触改变了权力的计算方式。

senses.title: Interdependence of technical systems
senses.definition: the coupling of infrastructures such that a failure in one propagates into another
senses.definitionCN: 基础设施彼此耦合，一处故障会传播到另一处
senses.example: Engineers map the interdependence of power and water systems before planning outages.
senses.exampleCN: 工程师在规划停运前先绘制电力与供水系统的互赖关系。
senses.why: Infrastructure studies borrowed the term for cascading failure: water pumps need electricity, and power plants need water. The word describes a shared fate that operators cannot ignore.
senses.whyCN: 基础设施研究借用这个术语来描述级联失效：水泵需要电力，电厂需要水。这个词描述一种运营者无法忽视的共同命运。

senses.title: Interdependence among organizations
senses.definition: the reliance of firms or institutions on one another for resources, information, or legitimacy
senses.definitionCN: 企业或机构在资源、信息或合法性上彼此依赖
senses.example: Suppliers and manufacturers develop a long-term interdependence.
senses.exampleCN: 供应商与制造商形成长期的相互依赖。
senses.why: Organization theory uses the noun to explain why firms cooperate without merging: each controls resources the other needs, so the link holds without ownership.
senses.whyCN: 组织理论用这个名词解释企业为何合作而不合并：各自掌握对方需要的资源，因此连接在没有所有权的情况下也能维持。

senses.title: Biological mutual dependence
senses.definition: a close association in which two organisms depend on each other for survival
senses.definitionCN: 两种生物彼此依赖才能存活的紧密关系
senses.example: Lichens are a textbook case of interdependence between fungus and alga.
senses.exampleCN: 地衣是真菌与藻类相互依存的教科书案例。
senses.why: Biology applies the noun to symbiosis, where the partnership is not optional. Here the hanging image is literal: neither organism can live detached from the other.
senses.whyCN: 生物学把这个名词用于共生，那里的伙伴关系并非可选。这里的悬挂意象是字面的：两种生物都无法脱离对方存活。

intro.en: Interdependence is inter- 'between' plus dependence, from Latin dependere 'to hang from', built on de- 'down' and pendere 'hang'. The word pictures each party as a support from which the other hangs.
intro.cn: interdependence 是 inter-“在……之间”加 dependence，后者源自拉丁语 dependere“悬挂于”，由 de-“向下”与 pendere“悬挂”构成。这个词把每一方都画成对方悬挂其上的支点。

items.en: Latin pendere meant 'to hang, weigh'. With de- 'down from' it formed dependere, 'to hang from, be dependent on'. The image was physical before it became social.
items.cn: 拉丁语 pendere 意为“悬挂、称重”。加 de-“从……向下”构成 dependere“悬挂于、依赖于”。这个意象在变成社会义之前是物理的。

items.en: English depend and dependence entered through French. Dependence described both physical hanging and the relation of a person or thing controlled by another.
items.cn: 英语 depend 与 dependence 经法语进入。dependence 既描述物理悬挂，也描述人或物受另一人控制的关系。

items.en: Interdependence is recorded in the early nineteenth century as 'mutual dependence'. It answered a new need: describing relationships in which no side is simply the master.
items.cn: interdependence 于 19 世纪初被记录，义为“相互依赖”。它回应了一种新需要：描述没有哪一方只是主人的关系。

items.en: Biology applied it to symbiosis, and economics to trade between specialised nations. In both fields the word named a shared fate that could help or hurt.
items.cn: 生物学把它用于共生，经济学把它用于专业化国家之间的贸易。两个领域里，这个词都命名一种既能造福也能致害的共同命运。

items.en: Keohane and Nye's theory of complex interdependence made the noun a standard term for states linked through many channels. The word then implied that force had lost some of its usefulness.
items.cn: 基欧汉与奈的复合相互依存理论使这个名词成为描述多渠道相连国家的标准术语。这个词由此暗示武力已部分失去效用。

items.en: Modern usage covers supply chains, infrastructure, ecosystems, and families. In every case the test is the same: does the withdrawal of one party hurt the other?
items.cn: 现代用法覆盖供应链、基础设施、生态系统与家庭。无论哪种情况，检验标准都一样：一方退出是否会伤及另一方？

note.en: The look-alike group separates nouns built on the same pendere root with different prefixes; the near-meaning group separates words of reliance and linkage.
note.cn: 形近组区分以同一 pendere 词根但前缀不同的名词；近义组区分表示“依赖”与“连接”的词。

entries.definition: freedom from control by others. Here in- negates dependence entirely, so the word is the opposite of the sense at issue.
entries.definitionCN: 不受他人控制的自由。这里 in- 完全否定 dependence，因此这个词与前文所论的义项相反。

entries.definition: reliance on someone or something. It can be one-sided and is often used of addiction or burden, unlike reciprocal interdependence.
entries.definitionCN: 对某人或某物的依赖。它可以是单方面的，常用于成瘾或负担，与相互的 interdependence 不同。

entries.definition: the state of relying on something, or a territory controlled by another state. The -cy form often names a concrete territory or a political relation.
entries.definitionCN: 依赖状态，或受他国控制的属地。-cy 形式常命名具体属地或政治关系。

entries.definition: the act of depending on someone or something. It usually describes one party's trust; interdependence requires the reliance to run both ways.
entries.definitionCN: 依赖某人或某物的行为。它通常描述一方的信赖；interdependence 要求依赖是双向的。

entries.definition: the state of being linked. It describes the channel itself, while interdependence describes the need that makes the channel necessary.
entries.definitionCN: 相互连接的状态。它描述通道本身，而 interdependence 描述使通道成为必要的需要。

entries.definition: an ecological relationship that benefits both species. It is a specific biological category, narrower than general interdependence.
entries.definitionCN: 对两种物种都有益的生态关系。它是一个具体的生物类别，比一般的相互依赖更窄。

normalIntro.en: Real associations: depend from de- 'down' + pendere 'hang', the reciprocal inter-, and the international-relations phrase complex interdependence.
normalIntro.cn: 真实联想：depend 来自 de-“向下”+ pendere“悬挂”、相互的 inter-，以及国际关系术语 complex interdependence。

normal.en: pendere means 'hang': to depend is to hang from something, and interdependence means both sides hang from each other.
normal.cn: pendere 意为“悬挂”：depend 是挂在某物上，而 interdependence 是双方互相挂在对方上。

normal.en: A pendulum and a pendant share the same root; so does the idea of being suspended.
normal.cn: 钟摆（pendulum）与吊坠（pendant）同根，被悬置的概念也同根。

normal.en: In trade, one country's shortage becomes everyone's shortage — that is economic interdependence.
normal.cn: 在贸易中，一国的短缺会变成所有人的短缺——这就是经济互赖。

normal.en: Lichens are the classic case: fungus and alga cannot live apart.
normal.cn: 地衣是经典案例：真菌与藻类无法分离而活。

normal.en: Complex interdependence is the political version: many channels make force expensive.
normal.cn: 复合相互依存是政治版本：渠道众多使动武代价高昂。

abstract.en: The word is not about weakness; it says that support is mutual, so both sides hold a hook.
abstract.cn: 这个词不是讲软弱；它说支撑是相互的，因此双方都握着一个钩子。

abstract.en: Every interdependence cuts both ways: the same link that shares growth also shares shock.
abstract.cn: 每一种相互依赖都是双刃的：分享增长的同一连接，也分享冲击。

abstract.en: Independence removes the hook; interdependence keeps it but makes it symmetrical.
abstract.cn: 独立拆掉了钩子；相互依赖保留钩子，但让它变得对称。

examples.en: Economic interdependence means that a factory closure in one country is felt in another.
examples.cn: 经济上的相互依存意味着，一国工厂关闭会在另一国被感受到。

examples.en: The ecosystem's interdependence became clear when one pollinator disappeared.
examples.cn: 当一种传粉昆虫消失时，生态系统的相互依存就变得清晰。

examples.en: Complex interdependence theory explains cooperation among trading democracies.
examples.cn: 复合相互依存理论解释了贸易民主国家之间的合作。

dict_mnemonic.text: “因它来低盆等死”——它一来，两边的盆都低低地吊着，谁离开谁都不行 → interdependence 相互依赖

root: inter-（在……之间）+ de-（向下）+ 拉丁语 pendere“悬挂”+ -ence；字面义“彼此悬挂在对方身上”，核心是“双方互为支点、无法单方松手”。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses of interdependence all describe support that runs both ways: people, economies, species, systems, states, firms, and organisms. The word never means simple weakness; it means that each side is a hook for the other.
sensesIntro.cn: interdependence 的八个义项都描述双向的支撑：人、经济体、物种、系统、国家、企业与生物。这个词从不表示单纯的软弱；它表示每一方都是对方的挂钩。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: two people each holding one end of the same ladder; if either lets go, both fall.
core.cn: 核心意象：两人各扶同一架梯子的一端；任一方松手，两人都会倒下。

branches.en: PERSONAL: people need each other for care and autonomy, without one side owning the other.
branches.cn: 个人：人们在照料与自主上彼此需要，而没有一方占有另一方。

branches.en: ECONOMIC: trade and supply chains make firms and countries share both growth and shortage.
branches.cn: 经济：贸易与供应链让企业与国家共享增长，也共享短缺。

branches.en: ECOLOGICAL: food webs and symbioses make survival a joint condition.
branches.cn: 生态：食物网与共生使生存成为共同条件。

branches.en: POLITICAL: many channels of contact make force costly and cooperation rational.
branches.cn: 政治：多渠道接触使武力代价高昂、合作变得理性。

branches.en: TECHNICAL: coupled infrastructures carry failure from one system into the next.
branches.cn: 技术：耦合的基础设施把故障从一个系统带进下一个。

intro.en: Interdependence is inter- + dependence, and dependence is depend + -ence from Latin dependere. The family turns on the verb pendere 'hang', with prefixes changing who hangs from whom.
intro.cn: interdependence 是 inter- + dependence，而 dependence 是 depend + -ence，源自拉丁语 dependere。这个家族围绕动词 pendere“悬挂”，前缀改变的是谁挂在谁身上。

latinIntro.en: Latin pendere 'to hang, weigh' yields pendulus 'hanging', pendulum 'a hanging weight', and dependere 'hang from'. The same root also gives expensive and pension, where the idea is weighing out money.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 pendere“悬挂、称重”给出 pendulus“悬挂的”、pendulum“摆”、dependere“悬挂于”。同一词根还给出 expensive 与 pension，那里的意思是“称出钱来”。

items.example: The two industries show close interdependence.
items.exampleCN: 这两个行业表现出紧密的相互依赖。

items.meaningCN: 相互依赖的（-ent 构成形容词）
items.exampleCN: 这些地区在经济上相互依赖。

items.meaningCN: 以相互依赖的方式（-ly 构成副词）
items.exampleCN: 这些物种相互依赖地演化。

definition_zh: 竞争优势
definition_en: a condition or resource that lets a firm outperform its rivals in a market
core_image: 同一场比赛里，一名选手脚下多了一双带钉的跑鞋，起跑线却没有变
scene: 两家工厂的成品并排摆在展台上，其中一家的产品更薄、更省电，价签却相同。 A durable competitive advantage usually rests on resources rivals cannot copy.
sceneCN: 这里 competitive advantage 指「企业胜过对手的有利条件」（第 1 个义项：使企业在市场中表现优于对手的条件或资源）；句意为持久的竞争优势通常建立在对手无法复制的资源上。图中可辨识物件：并排展台、更薄更省电的产品、相同价签、对手的产品。

pos.zh: 竞争优势

senses.title: A general edge over rivals
senses.definition: any condition that lets a firm serve buyers better or more cheaply than its rivals
senses.definitionCN: 使企业比对手更好或更便宜地服务买主的任何条件
senses.example: A reliable supply chain gave the retailer a competitive advantage.
senses.exampleCN: 可靠的供应链给了这家零售商竞争优势。
senses.why: advantage comes from avant 'before', so the phrase names a position ahead of rivals rather than a fixed property.
senses.whyCN: advantage 来自 avant「在前」，因此这个短语指相对对手靠前的位置，而非固定属性。

senses.title: Cost advantage
senses.definition: the ability to produce or deliver at a lower cost than competitors
senses.definitionCN: 以低于竞争对手的成本生产或交付的能力
senses.example: Low labour costs were its original competitive advantage.
senses.exampleCN: 低劳动成本是它最初的竞争优势。
senses.why: cost is the easiest edge to measure, so the phrase often takes this narrow reading in industry reports.
senses.whyCN: 成本是最容易测量的优势，因此在产业报告中这个短语常取这一窄义。

senses.title: Differentiation advantage
senses.definition: an edge from offering something buyers value that rivals do not offer
senses.definitionCN: 通过提供买主看重而对手不提供的东西取得的优势
senses.example: Design became the brand's competitive advantage.
senses.exampleCN: 设计成了这个品牌的竞争优势。
senses.why: when price cannot be lowered further, the edge must come from a difference buyers are willing to pay for.
senses.whyCN: 当价格无法再降，优势就只能来自买主愿意为之付费的差异。

senses.title: A durable advantage
senses.definition: an edge that survives imitation and market change for a long period
senses.definitionCN: 长期经受住模仿与市场变化的优势
senses.example: A patent-protected process is a sustainable competitive advantage.
senses.exampleCN: 受专利保护的工艺是一种可持续的竞争优势。
senses.why: strategy writing added durable because most edges are copied quickly and stop being advantages.
senses.whyCN: 战略写作加上「持久」一词，因为多数优势很快被复制，就不再是优势。

senses.title: An advantage rooted in resources
senses.definition: an edge that comes from resources a firm owns that are rare and hard to imitate
senses.definitionCN: 来自企业拥有的稀缺且难以模仿的资源
senses.example: Rare earth deposits are a resource-based competitive advantage.
senses.exampleCN: 稀土矿藏是一种基于资源的竞争优势。
senses.why: the resource-based view asks what the firm owns, not what it does, so the phrase shifts to stocks rather than actions.
senses.whyCN: 资源基础观问企业拥有什么而非做什么，因此这个短语转向「存量」而非「动作」。

senses.title: A locational advantage
senses.definition: an edge from being close to markets, suppliers, ports or skilled labour
senses.definitionCN: 因靠近市场、供应商、港口或熟练劳动力而获得的优势
senses.example: Proximity to the port is a locational competitive advantage.
senses.exampleCN: 靠近港口是一种区位竞争优势。
senses.why: advantage can attach to a place, because distance still costs money even in a digital economy.
senses.whyCN: 优势可以附着在地点上，因为即使在数字经济中，距离仍然要花钱。

senses.title: First-mover advantage
senses.definition: an edge gained by entering a market before rivals and locking in customers or standards
senses.definitionCN: 先于对手进入市场并锁定顾客或标准而取得的优势
senses.example: Being first to the market gave the startup a competitive advantage.
senses.exampleCN: 率先进入市场给了这家初创企业竞争优势。
senses.why: the phrase covers timing as well as resources, since an early position can itself be the asset.
senses.whyCN: 这个短语也涵盖时机，因为靠前的位置本身就可以是资产。

senses.title: An edge for any organization
senses.titleCN: 任何组织相对对手的有利条件
senses.definition: the same idea applied to a team, university or charity rather than a business
senses.definitionCN: 同一观念被用于队伍、大学或慈善机构而非企业
senses.example: A well-drilled team can turn a competitive advantage into a win.
senses.exampleCN: 训练有素的队伍能把竞争优势转化为胜利。
senses.why: once rivals are anywhere, advantage follows them beyond commercial markets.
senses.whyCN: 一旦对手无处不在，优势就跟着越出商业市场。

intro.en: Competitive comes from Latin competere 'to strive together'. Advantage comes through Old French avantage from avant 'before', ultimately from Latin ab ante 'from before'. The phrase is twentieth-century strategy vocabulary. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: competitive 来自拉丁 competere「一起力争」。advantage 经古法语 avantage 上溯 avant「在前」，最终来自拉丁 ab ante「从前面」。整个短语是 20 世纪战略词汇。年代均为约数。

items.en: The phrase ab ante meant 'from before, in front of'. Its shortened form ante 'before' is the seed of the whole advantage family.
items.cn: ab ante 意为「从前面、在……之前」，其简式 ante「在前」是整族 advantage 词的种子。

items.en: Avant 'before' plus the noun suffix -age produced avantage, a position ahead of others or a profit gained from it.
items.cn: avant「在前」加名词后缀 -age 构成 avantage，指领先于他人的位置或由此得到的利益。

items.en: English borrowed advantage in the fourteenth century, first as a favourable position, then as a benefit or profit.
items.cn: 英语在 14 世纪借入 advantage，先指有利位置，后指好处或利益。

items.en: Competere joins com- 'together' to petere 'seek'; competitive entered English as an adjective for anything able to contend.
items.cn: competere 把 com-「共同」接在 petere「寻求」上；competitive 作为形容词进入英语，形容能够相争的事物。

items.en: Competitive advantage became central to business strategy writing in the 1980s, when analysts asked why some firms consistently outperform others.
items.cn: 20 世纪 80 年代，当分析者追问为何某些企业持续胜过其他企业时，competitive advantage 成为企业战略写作的核心。

items.en: The exact first printed use of the full phrase is not recorded; earlier economics used advantage and competitive separately. The Latin and French steps are documented.
items.cn: 完整短语的最早印刷用例没有确切记录；更早的经济学写作分开使用 advantage 与 competitive。拉丁与法语环节有据可查。

note.en: Group one holds look-alike words from the advantage family, including one that is a doublet rather than a derivative; group two holds near terms for an edge that are not identical to it.
note.cn: 第一组是 advantage 词族中易混的词，其中一个是对偶词而非派生词；第二组是表示「优势」的近义说法，与它并不完全等同。

entries.definition: From the same avant 'before' line, but it means to move forward in space or time, not to hold a favourable position.
entries.definitionCN: 同出 avant「在前」这条线，但意为在空间或时间上向前移动，而非占据有利位置。

entries.definition: Dis- added to advantage in English, naming an unfavourable position; it is not a Latin word.
entries.definitionCN: dis- 在英语中加在 advantage 上，指不利位置；它不是拉丁词。

entries.definition: The adjective meaning favourable; a competitive advantage is the noun, while advantageous describes the condition.
entries.definitionCN: 表示「有利的」形容词；competitive advantage 是名词，而 advantageous 描述该条件。

entries.definition: The rival itself; an advantage exists only in relation to a competitor, but the two words name different things.
entries.definitionCN: 指对手本身；优势只在与竞争者相对时存在，但这两个词指称不同事物。

entries.definition: A small lead or sharpness over rivals; it is the everyday word for what competitive advantage states formally.
entries.definitionCN: 对对手的微小领先或锋利之处；它是竞争优势正式说法的日常版本。

entries.definition: A capability a firm possesses; a strength becomes an advantage only when buyers or rivals make it valuable.
entries.definitionCN: 企业拥有的能力；只有当买主或对手使其有价值时，能力才成为优势。

entries.definition: A resource with value; assets can support an advantage, but an asset by itself may be neither rare nor useful.
entries.definitionCN: 有价值的资源；资产可以支撑优势，但一项资产本身未必稀缺或有用。

entries.definition: The state of being better than another; it is a verdict, while competitive advantage is a market condition.
entries.definitionCN: 优于他者的状态；它是一种评判，而竞争优势是一种市场条件。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real fixed phrases and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: avant 'before' + -age: advantage is literally a position in front.
normal.cn: avant「在前」+ -age：advantage 字面上就是「靠前的位置」。

normal.en: The family runs advantage, advantageous, disadvantage, disadvantaged, competitive, competitor.
normal.cn: 同族词包括 advantage、advantageous、disadvantage、disadvantaged、competitive、competitor。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark the strategy sense: sustainable competitive advantage, source of competitive advantage.
normal.cn: 固定搭配标出战略义：可持续竞争优势、竞争优势的来源。

normal.en: Strategy writing pairs it with three sources: cost, differentiation and focus.
normal.cn: 战略写作把它与三种来源配对：成本、差异化与聚焦。

normal.en: The everyday twin is competitive edge, used in speech more than in reports.
normal.cn: 日常的对应说法是 competitive edge，多用于口语而非报告。

abstract.en: Picture a runner with better shoes on the same starting line.
abstract.cn: 想象一名跑者站在同一条起跑线上，脚上却是一双更好的鞋。

abstract.en: Picture two stalls side by side, one with a shorter queue.
abstract.cn: 想象并排的两个摊位，其中一个队伍更短。

abstract.en: Picture a map where one warehouse sits closer to every road.
abstract.cn: 想象一张地图，其中一座仓库离每条路都更近。

examples.en: The firm's competitive advantage disappeared once the patent expired.
examples.cn: 专利一到期，这家企业的竞争优势就消失了。

examples.en: Training staff well can create a competitive advantage that rivals cannot buy.
examples.cn: 把员工培训好，可以创造对手买不到的竞争优势。

examples.en: Analysts asked which competitive advantage would survive the next price war.
examples.cn: 分析者追问哪一项竞争优势能挺过下一场价格战。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「competitive（竞争的）+ advantage（靠前的位置）」——在竞争中站得更靠前 → 竞争优势

root: competitive 来自拉丁 competere「一起力争」（com- + petere「寻求」）；advantage 经古法语 avantage 上溯 avant「在前」，最终来自拉丁 ab ante「从前面」。整个短语为 20 世纪战略用语。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one lead: a firm stands ahead of its rivals, and that lead is then located in cost, in difference, in durability, in owned resources, in a place, in timing, and finally in any organization that has rivals.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项沿同一个「靠前」展开：企业站在对手前面，这个靠前再依次落在成本、差异、持久性、自有资源、地点、时机，最后落在任何有对手的组织上。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a runner on the same starting line with better shoes.
core.cn: 核心意象：同一条起跑线上，一名跑者穿着更好的鞋。

branches.en: THE PLAIN LEAD: any condition that puts a firm ahead.
branches.cn: 朴素的领先：任何使企业靠前的条件。

branches.en: TWO ROUTES: charge less, or offer what rivals do not.
branches.cn: 两条路径：收得更少，或提供对手没有的东西。

branches.en: DURABILITY AND OWNERSHIP: an edge that survives imitation, and one rooted in what the firm owns.
branches.cn: 持久与所有：经得住模仿的优势，以及扎根于企业自有资源的优势。

branches.en: PLACE AND TIMING: proximity to roads and ports, and the advantage of arriving first.
branches.cn: 地点与时机：靠近道路与港口，以及先到一步的好处。

branches.en: BEYOND BUSINESS: the same lead sought by a team, a school or a charity.
branches.cn: 越出商业：队伍、学校或慈善机构追求的同一个领先。

intro.en: The phrase combines a Latin-derived adjective of striving with a French-derived noun of being in front; neither half is a bare root.
intro.cn: 这个短语把拉丁来源的「相争」形容词与法语来源的「在前」名词组合起来；两半都不是光秃的词根。

latinIntro.en: Latin petere and com- supply competitive and competitor; Latin ante, through French avant, supplies advantage, advantageous and disadvantage.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 petere 与 com- 提供 competitive 与 competitor；拉丁 ante 经法语 avant 提供 advantage、advantageous 与 disadvantage。

items.structure: Latin preposition ante (before, in front of)
items.example: The Latin word survives inside advantage and advance.
items.exampleCN: 这个拉丁词留在 advantage 与 advance 之中。

items.example: Height is an advantage in basketball.
The early train is advantageous for commuters.
Distance is a disadvantage for the shop.
items.exampleCN: 距离远是这家店的不利条件。
该项目服务处境不利的学生。

items.example: Four firms compete for the tender.
items.exampleCN: 四家企业争夺这项招标。
这项服务定价有竞争力。

items.example: A rival copied the design within a year.
items.exampleCN: 一家对手在一年内复制了设计。

items.example: The extra staff gave them an edge.
items.exampleCN: 多出的员工给了他们一点优势。

items.example: The land was bought advantageously before prices rose.
items.exampleCN: 这块地在涨价前被有利地买下。

definition_zh: v. 渐渐康复，疗养
definition_en: to recover slowly after illness or injury
core_image: 病人在窗边慢慢站起，阳光落在毯子上
scene: 手术后她在乡下静养，慢慢康复。 After surgery she stayed in the country to convalesce.
sceneCN: 第 1 个义项：convalesce 指渐渐康复；句意是她术后在乡下静养康复。

pos.zh: 康复；疗养

senses.title: Recover gradually
senses.definition: to grow stronger again after illness
senses.definitionCN: 病后慢慢恢复力气
senses.example: She convalesced for a month.
senses.exampleCN: 她康复了一个月。
senses.why: Strength returning a little each day.
senses.whyCN: 力气一天天回来。

senses.title: Rest while recovering
senses.definition: to rest in a quiet place while healing
senses.definitionCN: 在安静处休息以待痊愈
senses.example: He convalesced in the country.
senses.exampleCN: 他在乡下疗养。
senses.why: A chair by a sunny window.
senses.whyCN: 阳光窗边的一把椅子。

senses.title: Regain strength
senses.definition: to build back the strength illness took
senses.definitionCN: 把病耗掉的体力补回来
senses.example: The patient convalesced slowly.
senses.exampleCN: 病人慢慢恢复体力。
senses.why: A short walk lengthening week by week.
senses.whyCN: 一周比一周走得远。

intro.en: Convalesce comes from Latin convalescere, to grow strong again.
intro.cn: convalesce 来自拉丁语 convalescere，意为重新变强。

items.en: Valere means to be strong or well.
items.cn: valere 意为强壮、健康。

items.en: Convalescere means to grow strong again.
items.cn: convalescere 意为重新恢复强壮。

items.en: Convalescentia names the recovery period.
items.cn: convalescentia 指康复期。

items.en: English used convalesce of the sick.
items.cn: 十五世纪英语用它描述病人康复。

items.en: Medicine named the wards convalescent.
items.cn: 十九世纪医学把病房称作康复病房。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the conval- stem; the near-meaning group names getting well.
note.cn: 形近组共享 conval- 词干；近义组都是「恢复健康」。

entries.definition: The period of recovery.
entries.definitionCN: 康复期。

entries.definition: Recovering from illness.
entries.definitionCN: 康复中的。

entries.definition: The state of being easy to use.
entries.definitionCN: 方便。

entries.definition: To become healthy again.
entries.definitionCN: 痊愈。

entries.definition: To recover health and strength.
entries.definitionCN: 恢复。

entries.definition: To become sound again.
entries.definitionCN: 愈合。

entries.definition: To improve after injury.
entries.definitionCN: 好转。

normalIntro.en: Convalesce is strength creeping back day by day.
normalIntro.cn: convalesce 就是力气一天天爬回来。

normal.en: Valere means to be strong.
normal.cn: valere 意为强壮。

normal.en: Con- adds again to the growing strong.
normal.cn: con- 给「变强」加上「重新」。

normal.en: -esce marks a process beginning.
normal.cn: -esce 表示过程开始。

normal.en: A convalescent walks a little farther each day.
normal.cn: 康复者每天多走一点路。

normal.en: Convalescence is the slow middle of healing.
normal.cn: 康复期是痊愈过程中缓慢的一段。

abstract.en: A chair by a sunny window.
abstract.cn: 阳光窗边的一把椅子。

abstract.en: A cane left further from the bed.
abstract.cn: 越放越远的一根拐杖。

abstract.en: A blanket folded and put away.
abstract.cn: 叠好收起的毯子。

examples.en: She convalesced at home for a month.
examples.cn: 她在家康复了一个月。

examples.en: He is convalescing after surgery.
examples.cn: 他手术后正在疗养。

examples.en: A convalescent home stood by the sea.
examples.cn: 海边有一座疗养院。

dict_mnemonic.text: con（重新）+ val（强壮）+ esce（开始）→ 重新变强，即渐渐康复。

root: 拉丁 con（重新）+ valere（强壮）+ -scere（开始）→ convalescere → 英语 convalesce

sensesIntro.en: Illness fading and strength coming back.
sensesIntro.cn: 病渐渐退去，力气慢慢回来。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: strength returning a little each day
core.cn: 核心意象：力气一天天回来

branches.en: A month of slow recovery.
branches.cn: 一个月的缓慢康复。

branches.en: A chair by a country window.
branches.cn: 乡下窗边的一把椅子。

branches.en: Short walks growing longer.
branches.cn: 越走越长的短途散步。

branches.en: A body building itself back.
branches.cn: 把身体重新建起来。

branches.en: A quiet place chosen for healing.
branches.cn: 为养病挑的安静处。

intro.en: Convalesce joins con- to valere, to be strong, with the inceptive suffix -esce.
intro.cn: convalesce 把 con- 与表「强壮」的 valere 相连，再加表开始的 -esce。

latinIntro.en: Latin convalescere means to grow strong again.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 convalescere 意为重新变强。

definition_zh: n. 勇敢，勇气；勇敢的行为
definition_en: the quality of facing danger, pain or fear without giving way; also a brave act
core_image: 火警响起，人群往外跑，只有一个人往里冲
scene: 火警响起时所有人都往外跑，只有他转身冲回了楼里。 When the alarm sounded, everyone ran for the door, and only he turned back into the building, an act of plain bravery.
sceneCN: 第 1 个义项：bravery 指面对危险的勇气；句意是火警响起时大家往外跑，只有他转身冲回楼里。

pos.zh: 勇敢；勇气

forms.label: 不可数名词（无屈折变化）

senses.title: The quality of facing danger
senses.definition: the willingness to face danger or pain without backing away
senses.definitionCN: 愿意直面危险或痛苦而不退缩
senses.example: She was given a medal for bravery.
senses.exampleCN: 她因勇敢而获得一枚奖章。
senses.why: Brave is the adjective, and -ery names the quality behind it.
senses.whyCN: brave 是形容词，-ery 表示其背后的品质。

senses.title: A brave act
senses.definition: one particular action that shows courage
senses.definitionCN: 一次体现勇气的具体行为
senses.example: His bravery that night saved two lives.
senses.exampleCN: 他那一晚的勇敢救了两条命。
senses.why: The uncountable quality can be counted when it appears as single acts.
senses.whyCN: 这种不可数的品质，落到具体行为上就可数了。

intro.en: Bravery is brave plus -ery; brave first meant wild or bold in Italian and Spanish.
intro.cn: bravery 是 brave 加 -ery；brave 最初在意大利语与西班牙语中意为狂野、大胆。

items.en: Bravo means bold, wild, or splendid.

entries.definition: Great bravery, especially in battle.

entries.definition: Calm confidence in a hard moment.

entries.definition: The readiness to take risks.

abstract.cn: 看一个兜帽身影在黑暗中仓皇逃窜。

definition_en: to refuse to proceed or stop short abruptly; also, to hinder, and a baseball illegal motion
core_image: 马匹走到沟边前蹄一收，说什么也不肯再迈
scene: 缰绳拉了三次，马打了个响鼻停在栅栏前。 The horse balked at the narrow bridge.
sceneCN: 这里 balk 指「（马等）突然止步不前」（第 1 个义项：拒绝继续）；句意：那匹马在窄桥前停住不肯走。

pos.zh: 畏缩不前；拒绝继续
阻止；使受挫；（棒球）做牵制犯规
障碍；失误；（木材）大方料

derivatives.zh: 倔强止步的；不听使唤的（balk + -y）

senses.title: Of animals, to stop and refuse
senses.definition: of a horse or mule, to stop abruptly and refuse to go on
senses.definitionCN: 指马、骡等突然停步、拒绝前进
senses.example: The mule balked a mile from the mine.
senses.exampleCN: 离矿一英里处，骡子说什么也不走了。
senses.why: The ridge of unplowed earth stopped the plow and the team alike.
senses.whyCN: 田垄间未犁的土埂既挡犁，也挡牲口。

senses.title: Of people, to hesitate or refuse
senses.definition: to recoil from or refuse to accept something proposed
senses.definitionCN: 对所提之事退缩、不愿接受
senses.example: The board balked at the price.
senses.exampleCN: 董事会嫌价格太高，不肯点头。
senses.why: Human stubbornness borrowed the mule's motion.
senses.whyCN: 人的固执借用了骡子那一停。

senses.title: To thwart or get in the way
senses.definition: to block or frustrate someone's plan or progress
senses.definitionCN: 阻挠某人的计划或进展
senses.example: Rain balked the harvest for a week.
senses.exampleCN: 阴雨使收割耽搁了一周。
senses.why: What stops the animal stops the plan; the obstacle verb followed.
senses.whyCN: 能让牲口停步者亦能令计划搁浅，障碍动词随之而生。

senses.title: The unplowed ridge, the original noun
senses.definition: a ridge of land left unplowed between furrows
senses.definitionCN: 犁沟之间留下的未耕土埂
senses.example: The field still showed its old balks under the grass.
senses.exampleCN: 草皮之下仍可见旧日田埂。
senses.why: This is the word's first sense, the ridge that stops the plow.
senses.whyCN: 这是词的本义：挡住犁头的土埂。

senses.title: A baseball illegal motion
senses.definition: an illegal pitcher's motion that lets runners advance
senses.definitionCN: 投手违规动作，跑者可乘机进垒
senses.example: The umpire called a balk and the runner took second.
senses.exampleCN: 裁判判牵制犯规，跑者上二垒。
senses.why: American baseball froze the hindering sense into a rule.
senses.whyCN: 美式棒球把「妨碍」义冻结成了一条规则。

senses.title: A timber square
senses.definition: a thick beam or square-sawn length of wood
senses.definitionCN: 厚木梁或方锯木料
senses.example: Oak balks framed the new barn.
senses.exampleCN: 橡木大方料搭起新谷仓的骨架。
senses.why: A ridge and a beam share the same long, blocking shape.
senses.whyCN: 田埂与木梁同属「横亘的长条」。

senses.title: A check in games
senses.definition: in billiards and older games, a missed stroke or a marking line
senses.definitionCN: 台球及旧游戏中指失误一击或界线标记
senses.example: He left the red on the balk line.
senses.exampleCN: 他把红球留在了开球线上。
senses.why: Games adopted the stopping line as a boundary.
senses.whyCN: 游戏把「停顿之线」借作界线。

senses.title: Balky, the stubborn habit
senses.definition: in balky, given to stopping without cause
senses.definitionCN: 形容词 balky，指动辄无故停步
senses.example: The balky printer jammed every Monday.
senses.exampleCN: 那台倔打印机每逢周一必卡纸。
senses.why: The mule's temperament became a machine's too.
senses.whyCN: 骡子的脾气，机器也学了去。

intro.en: Balk comes from Old English balca, a ridge or beam, from Proto-Germanic balkon, a dividing piece; the verb grew in the fourteenth century from the ridge that stops the plow, and baseball fixed the legal sense in the nineteenth century.
intro.cn: balk 出自古英语 balca「田埂、横梁」，源自原始日耳曼语 balkon「分隔物」；动词义于 14 世纪从「挡犁之埂」发展而来；棒球「牵制犯规」义则定型于 19 世纪的美国。

items.en: The root balkon meant a dividing beam or ridge.
items.cn: 词根 balkon 意为分隔的梁木或田埂。

items.en: balca named both the ridge in the field and the beam in the roof.
items.cn: 古英语 balca 兼指田间土埂与屋顶横梁。

items.en: Old Norse bálkr and modern Swedish balk keep the beam sense in Scandinavia.
items.cn: 古诺斯语 bálkr 与瑞典语 balk 在北欧保留梁木义。

items.en: To balk arose from the stopping-ridge: to check the plow, then any plan.
items.cn: 动词 balk 从「停顿之埂」产生：先挡犁，后挡一切计划。

items.en: Settlers carried balk to America, where a sawmill is still a balk mill.
items.cn: 移民把 balk 带到美洲，锯木厂至今称大方料为 balk。

items.en: The rulebook sense, the pitcher's balk, entered official baseball in the nineteenth century.
items.cn: 19 世纪棒球规则正式写入投手牵制犯规（balk）。

note.en: Group one gathers the beam family and sound-alikes; group two gathers refusal and hindrance words.
note.cn: 第一组收梁木词族与音近词；第二组收拒绝与阻碍义场的词。

entries.definition: mass or size; shares the Old English family but a different vowel and sense.

entries.definition: a platform outside a window; from Italian balcone, not the ridge.

entries.definition: the boundary line on a billiard table.

entries.definition: to raise polite objection; the formal cousin.
entries.definitionCN: 婉言异议；正式语域的同族。

entries.definition: to pause from doubt.

entries.definition: to defeat a plan by active opposition.
entries.definitionCN: 以对抗挫败计划。

entries.definition: to delay or (of an engine) stop from lack of power.
entries.definitionCN: 拖延；（发动机）熄火停转。

entries.definition: to go forward; the direct antonym of balk at.
entries.definitionCN: 继续前进；balk at 的直接反义。

normalIntro.en: Picture a balk in the field: the ridge no plow and no mule will cross.

abstract.en: Feel the harness go slack as the animal plants its feet.

abstract.en: Balk is the body's veto, cast without a word.

root: 出自古英语 balca「田埂、横梁」，源自原始日耳曼语 balkon「分隔物」，与古诺斯语 bálkr、瑞典语 balk 同源；本义为田间挡犁的土埂，14 世纪引申出动词「（牲口）止步」「（人）畏缩」「阻挠」；19 世纪美式棒球将名词义定为「牵制犯规」；方木义与田埂义同源并峙。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses grow from one ridge: the animal that stops, the person who refuses, the plan that is blocked, the beam, the billiard line, the baseball rule, and the adjective for all things stubborn.

branches.en: THE HINDRANCE SIDE: plans balked by weather or men.
branches.cn: 妨碍一面：被天或人搅黄的计划。

branches.en: THE TIMBER SIDE: ridge and beam, one shape twice named.

branches.en: THE GAMES SIDE: the baseball rule and the billiard line.
branches.cn: 游戏一面：棒球规则与台球界线。

branches.en: THE TEMPER SIDE: balky machines and mules.
