intro.en: Balk is a bare Germanic root; its family wears only plain English endings.
intro.cn: balk 是裸的日耳曼词根，其词族只穿平实的英语词尾。

latinIntro.en: No Latin enters: the line runs straight from Proto-Germanic balkon through Old English balca.
latinIntro.cn: 无拉丁成分：词线从原始日耳曼语 balkon 直贯古英语 balca。

items.exampleCN: 动不动就熄火的发动机

definition_zh: 顾问；提供专业建议的人；（大学的）指导教师；（政府的）高级幕僚
definition_en: a person whose job is to give expert advice; a teacher who guides a student’s course choices; a senior official who advises a government
core_image: 站在你旁边、替你把眼前局面看清楚的那个人
scene: 选课表摊在桌上，学生拿不定主意，于是敲开了那扇门。 She asked her advisor which course to take first.
sceneCN: 这里 advisor 是「指导教师」（第 2 个义项：在学校里指导学生选课与学业安排的人）；句意为她问导师该先修哪门课。核心画面是有人替你把局面看清楚，再告诉你往哪走。

pos.zh: 顾问；指导教师；幕僚

collocations.phrase: on the advice of an advisor

derivatives.zh: 由同一词根构成，义为「建议；劝告」，是 advisor 所做的事
加 -ory 构成，义为「顾问的；咨询的；劝告的」
加 -able 构成，义为「明智的；可取的」
同族名词，义为「建议；忠告」，不可数

senses.title: A person paid to give expert advice
senses.definition: a person whose job is to give professional advice on money, law, business or policy
senses.definitionCN: 以提供理财、法律、商业或政策方面的专业意见为职业的人
senses.example: The company hired a financial advisor before the merger.
senses.exampleCN: 公司在并购前聘请了一位理财顾问。
senses.why: The root means to cause someone to see, so an advisor is literally the person who makes the situation visible to you.
senses.whyCN: 词根的意思是「使人看见」，所以 advisor 字面上就是那个让你看清局面的人——你看不到的风险，他替你看。

senses.title: A teacher who guides a student’s studies
senses.definition: a teacher at a school or college who helps students choose courses and plan their studies
senses.definitionCN: 在学校或大学里帮助学生选课、规划学业的教师
senses.example: My advisor suggested I take statistics in the second year.
senses.exampleCN: 我的导师建议我第二年修统计学。
senses.why: The same seeing image narrows to one field: the advisor sees the whole curriculum and points out the path a student cannot yet see.
senses.whyCN: 同一个「看清」的意象收窄到学业这一域：导师看得见整张课程地图，于是指出学生自己还看不见的那条路。

senses.title: A senior official who advises a government
senses.definition: a senior official who gives advice to a government or a head of state, often in a titled post
senses.definitionCN: 向政府或国家元首提供意见的高级官员，常带正式头衔
senses.example: He served as national security advisor for four years.
senses.exampleCN: 他担任了四年国家安全顾问。
senses.why: Here the seeing is done for a whole state: the advisor is the extra pair of eyes attached to power, which is why the spelling advisor is preferred in official titles.
senses.whyCN: 这里是替整个国家「看」：顾问是接在权力旁边的另一双眼睛，也正因这种正式色彩，官方头衔更偏爱 advisor 这一拼写。

intro.en: Advisor is built on the Latin verb for seeing: advice began as making something visible to another person.
intro.cn: advisor 建立在拉丁语表示「看」的动词上：建议最初就是把事情让别人看见。

items.en: Videre meant to see, and its past participle visum supplied the stem for vision, visible and advise.
items.cn: videre 意为「看」，其过去分词 visum 提供了 vision、visible 与 advise 的词干。

items.en: Vulgar Latin advisare combined ad-, toward, with visum, giving the sense to cause to see or to consider.
items.cn: 通俗拉丁语 advisare 由 ad-「向」与 visum 组合，义为「使看见、使考虑」。

items.en: Old French aviser meant to perceive, to consider and to give an opinion, and it carried the word north.
items.cn: 古法语 aviser 意为「察觉、考虑、发表意见」，并把这个词向北传播。

items.en: Middle English avisen meant to consider or to counsel, and the noun advice grew beside it.
items.cn: 中古英语 avisen 意为「考虑、劝告」，名词 advice 随之产生。

items.en: Adviser is advise plus the agent suffix -er; advisor is a later variant spelling, now common in American official titles.
items.cn: adviser 由 advise 加施事后缀 -er 构成；advisor 是后起的异形拼写，如今常见于美式官方头衔。

note.en: The look-alike group stays inside the see family; the near-meaning group lists other people you pay to think for you.
note.cn: 形近组留在「看」这一词族内；近义组列出其他受聘替你思考的人。

entries.definition: The usual British spelling of the same noun.
entries.definitionCN: 同一名词的英式常用拼写。

entries.definition: To give someone an opinion about what they should do.
entries.definitionCN: 就某人该怎么做给出意见。

entries.definition: Worth doing; sensible under the circumstances.
entries.definitionCN: 值得做的；在当时情况下明智的。

entries.definition: An expert paid to give professional advice, often from outside the organization.
entries.definitionCN: 受聘提供专业意见的专家，常来自机构外部。

entries.definition: A person trained to give guidance, especially on personal or legal matters.
entries.definitionCN: 受过训练、提供指导的人，尤指个人或法律事务。

entries.definition: An experienced person who guides a less experienced one over time.
entries.definitionCN: 长期指导经验较少者的资深人士。

normalIntro.en: Remember advisor through advise: the advisor is the one who does the advising.
normalIntro.cn: 用 advise 记 advisor：advisor 就是做 advise 这件事的人。

normal.en: Advise plus -er equals the person who advises, exactly like teach plus -er gives teacher.
normal.cn: advise 加 -er 就是提建议的人，正如 teach 加 -er 得到 teacher。

normal.en: The vis inside advisor is the same vis in vision and visible: an advisor gives you vision.
normal.cn: advisor 里的 vis 与 vision、visible 中的 vis 相同：顾问给你视野。

normal.en: Split it as ad plus visor: a visor is what you look through, and an advisor is who you look through.
normal.cn: 拆成 ad 加 visor：visor 是你透过它看的东西，advisor 是你透过他看的人。

normal.en: Advisor ends in -or like doctor and professor, which is why official titles prefer it.
normal.cn: advisor 以 -or 结尾，像 doctor、professor，所以正式头衔偏爱这种拼写。

normal.en: Advice is the thing, advisor is the person; one is uncountable, the other can be counted.
normal.cn: advice 是东西，advisor 是人；前者不可数，后者可数。

abstract.en: Picture a foggy road and a person walking beside you holding a lamp: that lamp is the advice.
abstract.cn: 想象一条雾中的路，旁边有人提着一盏灯：那盏灯就是建议。

abstract.en: Imagine a map you cannot read, and a finger tracing the route for you.
abstract.cn: 想象一张你读不懂的地图，一根手指替你描出路线。

abstract.en: Think of a second pair of eyes borrowed for a decision you must make alone.
abstract.cn: 想象为一个必须独自做出的决定借来的第二双眼睛。

examples.en: Every freshman is assigned an advisor at the start of the term.
examples.cn: 每位新生在学期开始时都会被分配一位指导教师。

examples.en: The advisor warned that the investment carried serious risks.
examples.cn: 顾问警告说这项投资带有严重风险。

examples.en: She works as a legal advisor to several small charities.
examples.cn: 她担任几家小型慈善机构的法律顾问。

dict_mnemonic.text: 谐音「额的歪泽」——额（ad）头一歪，泽（visor）出一双眼睛替你看路，这人就是顾问。

root: 拉丁语 ad-「向」加 visum（videre「看」的过去分词）构成通俗拉丁语 advisare「使看见、使考虑」，经古法语 aviser 进入英语 advise，再加施事后缀 -er／-or 构成「出主意的人」。

sensesIntro.en: All three senses keep one image: someone else sees the situation clearly and tells you what to do, whether about money, courses or state affairs.
sensesIntro.cn: 三个义项保留同一意象：别人把局面看清，再告诉你怎么做——无论是钱、课程还是国家大事。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a second pair of eyes that makes the situation visible
core.cn: 核心意象：让局面变得可见的第二双眼睛

branches.en: Seeing done as a paid profession.
branches.cn: 把「看清」当成受聘的职业。

branches.en: Seeing narrowed to a curriculum.
branches.cn: 把「看清」收窄到课程地图。

branches.en: Seeing attached to state power.
branches.cn: 把「看清」接到国家权力旁边。

branches.en: Both give a recommendation, not an order.
branches.cn: 两者给的都是建议，不是命令。

branches.en: Both are formal posts with a title.
branches.cn: 两者都是带正式头衔的职位。

intro.en: Advisor is a transparent Latin build: a prefix of direction, a root of sight, and a suffix that turns an action into a person.
intro.cn: advisor 是透明的拉丁语构词：一个方向前缀、一个视觉词根，再加一个把动作变成人的后缀。

latinIntro.en: Latin ad- plus visum produced advisare; English kept the verb advise and built the agent noun on top of it.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 ad- 加 visum 产生 advisare；英语保留动词 advise，并在其上构成施事名词。

latinEntries.example: Videre is the source of vis-.
latinEntries.exampleCN: videre 是 vis- 的来源。

latinEntries.example: Visum supplied the stem of advisare.
latinEntries.exampleCN: visum 提供了 advisare 的词干。

latinEntries.meaning: to cause to see, to consider

definition_zh: 阳极；正极
definition_en: the positively charged electrode by which electrons leave a device, or the electrode where oxidation occurs
core_image: 电流进出的门柱之一：阳极这边，电子动身离开
scene: 化学老师把铜片和锌片插进液体。 Electrons flow from the anode through the wire to the cathode.
sceneCN: 这里 anode 是「阳极」（第 1 个义项：电流所经的电极之一）；句意为：电子从阳极经导线流向阴极。

pos.zh: 阳极；正极（电解中为发生氧化的一极）

derivatives.zh: anode + -ize，义为「对……作阳极氧化处理」
与 anode 相对造出的词，义为「阴极」，同 -ode 后缀

senses.title: The positive terminal of a cell or battery
senses.definition: the electrode through which conventional current enters a battery from outside
senses.definitionCN: 电流从外部进入电池所经的电极
senses.example: Connect the red wire to the anode of the battery.
senses.exampleCN: 把红线接到电池的正极。
senses.why: Faraday coined the word for the way up in a circuit, and the positive pole took it.
senses.whyCN: 法拉第为电路中的「上行之路」造了此词，正极获得了这个名字。

senses.title: The electrode where oxidation occurs in electrolysis
senses.definition: in electrolysis, the electrode at which negative ions discharge and oxidation happens
senses.definitionCN: 电解时负离子放电、发生氧化反应的电极
senses.example: Chlorine gas bubbles off at the anode.
senses.exampleCN: 氯气在阳极冒出气泡。
senses.why: Ions travel up toward the anode, the road named for ascending.
senses.whyCN: 离子向上行进至阳极，正如其名所示的「上行之路」。

senses.title: The electron-emitting electrode in a vacuum tube
senses.definition: in a vacuum tube, the plate that collects electrons emitted by the cathode
senses.definitionCN: 真空管中收集阴极发射电子的板极
senses.example: Old radios failed when the anode burned out.
senses.exampleCN: 旧收音机常因板极烧毁而失灵。
senses.why: The ascending road is where the electron journey ends.
senses.whyCN: 这条「上行之路」正是电子旅程的终点。

senses.title: An electrode in an X-ray tube
senses.definition: the metal target in an X-ray tube that the electron beam strikes
senses.definitionCN: X 射线管中电子束轰击的金属靶
senses.example: The rotating anode keeps the X-ray tube from melting.
senses.exampleCN: 旋转阳极防止 X 射线管过热熔化。
senses.why: Where the ascending electrons land, light is born.
senses.whyCN: 上行电子的落点，正是光产生之处。

senses.title: A sacrificial anode protecting metal from corrosion
senses.definition: a reactive metal electrode that corrodes instead of the protected structure
senses.definitionCN: 代替被保护结构发生腐蚀的活泼金属电极
senses.example: Sacrificial anodes protect the ship's hull underwater.
senses.exampleCN: 牺牲阳极在水下保护船体。
senses.why: One electrode gives itself up so the whole may last.
senses.whyCN: 一个电极自我牺牲，使整体得以长存。

senses.title: The positive electrode of an electrolytic cell in industry
senses.definition: the electrode used in industrial processes such as electroplating or smelting
senses.definitionCN: 电镀、冶炼等工业过程中使用的电极
senses.example: Aluminum smelting consumes carbon anodes steadily.
senses.exampleCN: 炼铝过程持续消耗碳阳极。
senses.why: Industry scales the laboratory cell to factory size, keeping the same poles.
senses.whyCN: 工业把实验室电解槽放大到工厂规模，而极的名称不变。

senses.title: Anode in diodes and semiconductors
senses.definition: the terminal of a diode at which forward current enters
senses.definitionCN: 二极管上正向电流流入的一端
senses.example: The LED lights only when wired anode to positive.
senses.exampleCN: 只有阳极接正极，LED 才会亮。
senses.why: Semiconductors inherit the battery's vocabulary for their two doors.
senses.whyCN: 半导体沿用了电池给它的两扇「门」所起的名称。

senses.title: Anode in welding and plasma work
senses.definition: the workpiece or electrode that acts as the positive pole in arc processes
senses.definitionCN: 电弧工艺中充当正极的工件或电极
senses.example: In this torch setup the workpiece is the anode.
senses.exampleCN: 在这种焊枪配置中，工件即为阳极。
senses.why: Every arc needs an up road and a down road for its charge.
senses.whyCN: 每条电弧都需要一上一下两条电荷之路。

intro.en: Anode is one of Michael Faraday's own coinages, built from Greek for a way up, chosen with the help of a classical scholar.
intro.cn: anode 是迈克尔·法拉第亲自创造的词，源自希腊语「上行之路」，是在一位古典学者的帮助下选定的。

items.en: The roots *h₁ed- (to go) and *upo- (up from under) are generally reconstructed behind Greek hodos and ana-.
items.cn: 一般认为希腊语 hodos 出自印欧词根 *h₁ed-（行走），ana- 出自 *upo-（自下而上），均为重构形式。

items.en: Anos meant up, and hodos meant way; the phrase pointed to a rising road.
items.cn: 希腊语 anos 意为「向上」，hodos 意为「路」，合指「上行之路」。

items.en: In 1834 Faraday, advised by William Whewell, coined anode and cathode for his electrochemistry papers.
items.cn: 1834 年，法拉第在威廉·休厄尔建议下，为其电化学论文创造了 anode 与 cathode。

items.en: The words spread through battery, electrolysis, and vacuum-tube technology.
items.cn: 这两个词随之进入电池、电解与真空管技术的语汇。

items.en: Anode now names the positive pole in batteries and the oxidation site in cells, with an established verb anodize.
items.cn: 如今 anode 既指电池正极，也指电解中发生氧化的一极，并衍生出动词 anodize。

note.en: Grouped by the shared -ode road-roots Faraday coined and by electrode neighbors.
note.cn: 按法拉第所造的同后缀「路」词与电极近义词分组。

entries.definition: the opposite electrode, the way down
entries.definitionCN: 阴极，与 anode 相对造出、共享 -ode 后缀

entries.definition: a conductor through which current enters or leaves
entries.definitionCN: 电极，anode 与 cathode 的上位词，同含 -ode

entries.definition: a negatively charged ion that travels to the anode
entries.definitionCN: 阴离子，因向阳极迁移而得名，拼写相近且同源于 ana-

entries.definition: the plus pole of a battery, the everyday phrase
entries.definitionCN: 电池正极的日常说法，与 anode 在电池语境中同指

entries.definition: the anode of a vacuum tube, in trade jargon
entries.definitionCN: 板极，真空管行业对阳极的称呼

entries.definition: either end point of a circuit element
entries.definitionCN: 端子；接线端，泛指电路元件的两端

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the real Greek roots Faraday built on.
normalIntro.cn: 以下记忆钩子基于法拉第所用的真实希腊词根。

normal.en: ana- (up) + hodos (way) = the way up: anode.
normal.cn: ana-（向上）+ hodos（路）= 上行之路：即 anode。

normal.en: Cathode is the matching way down, kata- meaning down.
normal.cn: cathode 是对应的下行之路，kata- 意为「向下」。

normal.en: Anions (negative ions) walk up to the anode in electrolysis.
normal.cn: 电解时阴离子「上行」走向阳极。

normal.en: Remember PANiC: Positive Anode, Negative Cathode, for batteries.
normal.cn: 电池口诀：正极阳极（PANiC 的 PA），负极阴极。

normal.en: Anodize means to treat metal as if at the anode, building an oxide layer.
normal.cn: anodize 指像在阳极那样对金属作氧化处理。

abstract.en: Picture an escalator for charges, going up through the anode door.
abstract.cn: 想象一道为电荷准备的自动扶梯，向上穿过阳极之门。

abstract.en: See a dull zinc block dissolving slowly beside a shiny ship's hull.
abstract.cn: 想象一块黯淡的锌块在闪亮的船体旁缓缓溶解。

abstract.en: Feel one pole pulling and the other pushing, the circuit breathing between them.
abstract.cn: 感受一极拉、一极推，电路在其间呼吸。

examples.en: Corrosion was stopped by fitting a magnesium anode.
examples.cn: 安装镁制阳极后腐蚀停止了。

examples.en: The anode of the diode must face the positive supply.
examples.cn: 二极管的阳极必须朝向电源正极。

examples.en: Aluminum parts are anodized at the anode to resist scratching.
examples.cn: 铝件在阳极作氧化处理以抗刮擦。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「俺诺得」——俺承诺得到电流进来的一极，正是 anode（阳极）。

root: 希腊语 ana-（向上）+ hodos（路，一般认为出自印欧词根 *h₁ed-「行走」）→ 1834 年法拉第（经休厄尔建议）据希腊语复合创造 anode「上行之路」，与 cathode（下行之路）相对。

sensesIntro.en: From Faraday's way up, the word assigns poles in batteries, electrolysis tanks, vacuum tubes, and welding arcs alike.
sensesIntro.cn: 从法拉第的「上行之路」出发，该词为电池、电解槽、真空管与焊接电弧指派极名。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: the rising road that charge takes out of a device
core.cn: 核心意象：电荷离开设备所走的上行之路

branches.en: the plus door of batteries and diodes
branches.cn: 电池与二极管的正门

branches.en: the oxidation site in cells
branches.cn: 电解槽中的氧化之地

branches.en: the landing place of electrons in tubes
branches.cn: 真空管与 X 射线管中电子的落点

branches.en: the electrode that gives itself up
branches.cn: 自我牺牲的电极

branches.en: the positive pole of the working arc
branches.cn: 工作电弧的正极

intro.en: Faraday's pair of coinages share one Greek suffix, and a small family grew around them.
intro.cn: 法拉第的一对造词共享一个希腊后缀，周围又长出了一个小词族。

latinIntro.en: Though coined in English, the parts are pure Greek and the family stays regular.
latinIntro.cn: 虽在英语中创造，部件却是纯希腊语，词族也很规整。

items.example: Analysis means a loosening up into parts.
Method is the way after, the following of a road.
Electrode means the amber way, the path of electricity.
Cathode rays stream toward the screen.

items.meaning: the ion going up to the anode

items.example: They anodize bicycle frames for color and strength.
items.exampleCN: 他们对自行车车架作阳极氧化以着色并增强。

derivatives.zh: anodize 的名词形式，义为「阳极氧化」

definition_zh: 断言；主张；陈述；对权利或权威的维护；程序中的断言检查
definition_en: a confident and forceful statement of fact or belief, or the act of stating or defending something
core_image: 一个人把一枚印章重重按在文件上，抬手时印痕已经固定，再难悄悄收回
scene: 审稿人指出，论文里那句强硬的判断并没有数据支撑，只能算是一种声明。 The claim remained an assertion until the data arrived.
sceneCN: 这里指没有数据支撑的强硬判断（第 1 个义项：自信的断言）；句意为在数据到手之前，那个说法始终只是一句断言。

pos.zh: 断言；主张；维护；断言语句

derivatives.zh: 由同一拉丁词干构成的动词，义为「断言；维护」
由动词加表示「倾向」的形容词尾构成，义为「自信的；坚定主张的」
加表示性质的名词尾，义为「自信果断」
加已然词尾，义为「已断言的；被主张的」

senses.title: A confident statement of fact
senses.definition: a firm statement that something is true, made without hesitation
senses.definitionCN: 毫不迟疑地断定某事为真的陈述
senses.example: Her assertion that the test had failed was later confirmed.
senses.exampleCN: 她关于测试失败的那句断言后来得到证实。
senses.why: The Latin verb meant to claim as one's own, and a claim made firmly becomes a statement of fact.
senses.whyCN: 这个拉丁动词意为「认作自己的」，坚定地认领就成了一种事实陈述。

senses.title: A claim open to challenge
senses.definition: a statement put forward as true that others may reasonably dispute
senses.definitionCN: 被提出为真、但他人可以合理反驳的陈述
senses.example: The report's central assertion has no data behind it.
senses.exampleCN: 报告的核心主张背后没有数据。
senses.why: Anything asserted invites a counter-statement, so the word often marks a claim still awaiting proof.
senses.whyCN: 凡是断言都会招来反陈述，因此这个词常标出尚待证明的主张。

senses.title: A declaration of rights
senses.definition: the act of stating or defending a right, title or claim
senses.definitionCN: 声明或维护某项权利、名分或主张的行为
senses.example: The march was an assertion of the right to assemble.
senses.exampleCN: 那场游行是对集会权利的一次声明。
senses.why: Rights are claimed before they are used, and the word covers that public claiming.
senses.whyCN: 权利在被使用之前先被主张，这个词覆盖这种公开主张。

senses.title: A proposition affirmed in logic
senses.definition: a proposition that is put forward as true and from which inferences may follow
senses.definitionCN: 被提出为真、并可据以推出结论的命题
senses.example: In the proof, each assertion must follow from the one before.
senses.exampleCN: 在证明中，每个命题都必须由前一个推出。
senses.why: Logic treats an assertion as a statement with a truth value, which is a formal version of claiming.
senses.whyCN: 逻辑学把断言看作有真值的陈述，这是「主张」的形式化版本。

senses.title: An assertion in a program
senses.definition: a statement in code that declares a condition which must be true at that point
senses.definitionCN: 代码中声明某条件在该处必须为真的语句
senses.example: The developer added an assertion to catch empty input.
senses.exampleCN: 开发者在代码里加了一个断言，用来捕获空输入。
senses.why: Programming borrowed the word because a check asserts that a condition holds, and fails loudly if it does not.
senses.whyCN: 编程借用这个词，因为检查是在断言某条件成立，不成立就大声报错。

senses.title: A forceful expression of opinion
senses.definition: a confident way of saying what one thinks, often in speech
senses.definitionCN: 以自信的方式说出自己的想法，常见于口头表达
senses.example: His assertion that the plan was hopeless silenced the room.
senses.exampleCN: 他那句计划毫无希望的说法让全场安静下来。
senses.why: Tone matters here: the noun can name the force of a statement as much as its content.
senses.whyCN: 语气在这里很关键：这个名词既指内容，也指说话的力度。

senses.title: An assertion of authority
senses.definition: the act of showing or enforcing one's power or control
senses.definitionCN: 展示或强行施加自身权力与控制的行为
senses.example: The new manager's first meeting was an assertion of control.
senses.exampleCN: 新任经理的第一次会议是一次掌控权的宣示。
senses.why: Power is often claimed before it is obeyed, and the word names that claim.
senses.whyCN: 权力常在被服从之前先被主张，这个词就指那种主张。

senses.title: A statement made without proof
senses.definition: a statement offered as true although no evidence has been supplied
senses.definitionCN: 虽无证据却作为真实提出的陈述
senses.example: The essay opens with an assertion rather than a finding.
senses.exampleCN: 这篇文章以一个断言而不是发现开头。
senses.why: Because the word does not itself guarantee proof, it can politely name something unproven.
senses.whyCN: 因为这个词本身不保证有证明，它可以客气地指称未经证实的东西。

intro.en: Assertion comes from Latin asserere, to claim or maintain, literally to join something to oneself. The noun entered English through French and kept both the sense of a firm statement and the sense of defending a right.
intro.cn: 这个词来自拉丁语 asserere「主张、维护」，字面意为「把某物接到自己身上」。名词经法语进入英语，既保留「坚定陈述」的意思，也保留「维护权利」的意思。

items.en: Serere meant to join or arrange in a row, and it also gave the words for series and insert.
items.cn: 这个词根意为「连接、排成行」，也表示「系列」与「插入」的词也出自它。

items.en: With the prefix ad-, the verb meant to join to oneself, hence to claim a thing as one's own and defend it.
items.cn: 加上表示「朝向」的前缀后，动词意为「接到自己身上」，因而指把某物认作自己的并加以维护。

items.en: Roman law used the verb for asserting freedom or a right, and English kept that public, declarative force.
items.cn: 罗马法用这个动词表示主张自由或权利，英语保留了这种公开宣告的力量。

items.en: The noun assertion appeared in English writing on logic and law; its exact first record is uncertain.
items.cn: 名词「断言」在十五世纪的逻辑与法律写作中出现；确切最早记录不确定。

items.en: Grammar calls a positive statement an assertive sentence, and logic treats assertions as propositions with truth values.
items.cn: 语法学把肯定陈述称为断言句，逻辑学把断言当作有真值的命题。

items.en: Programming languages adopted assertion for a condition the program declares must hold at a given point.
items.cn: 编程语言采用这个词，指程序声明在某处必须成立的条件。

note.en: The first group shares the joining root or looks similar; the second group names statements and claims of other strengths.
note.cn: 第一组共享「连接」词根或形近；第二组指力度不同的陈述与主张。

entries.definition: The verb meaning to state firmly or to defend a right.
entries.definitionCN: 指坚定陈述或维护权利的动词。

entries.definition: Confident and direct in stating one's views.
entries.definitionCN: 指陈述观点时自信直接的。

entries.definition: The quality of standing up for oneself calmly and directly.
entries.definitionCN: 指平静而直接地维护自身立场的品质。

entries.definition: To put something inside; same joining root, inward prefix.
entries.definitionCN: 指把某物放入；与断言共享「连接」词根，前缀向内。

entries.definition: To abandon; the prefix means apart, so the joining is undone.
entries.definitionCN: 指抛弃；前缀意为「分开」，即把连接解开。

entries.definition: Capable of being asserted as true.
entries.definitionCN: 指可以被断言为真的。

entries.definition: A statement that something is true, often one not yet proved.
entries.definitionCN: 指声称某事为真，常指尚未证明的说法。

entries.definition: A formal public statement, stronger in official weight than in proof.
entries.definitionCN: 指正式的公开声明，官方分量重于证明。

entries.definition: The neutral word for something said or written.
entries.definitionCN: 指说出或写下的内容，是中性的说法。

entries.definition: A point argued in a debate or essay.
entries.definitionCN: 指辩论或文章中提出的论点。

entries.definition: A positive statement that something is true, often in law or religion.
entries.definitionCN: 指肯定某事为真的陈述，常用于法律或宗教。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations use the stamp picture, the legal claim of a right and the programming statement.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想使用盖章的画面、对权利的法律主张以及程序中的断言语句。

normal.en: To assert is to claim something as one's own, which is why the word can mean both saying and defending.
normal.cn: 断言就是把某物认作自己的，所以这个词既能指说出，也能指维护。

normal.en: An assertion is a stamp pressed down: the mark is made before anyone can argue with it.
normal.cn: 断言是按下的一枚印章：印痕在别人反驳之前就已经留下。

normal.en: Assertive speech is confident speech, and assertiveness training teaches people to state needs plainly.
normal.cn: 断言式说话就是自信的说话，「自信训练」教人把需求讲清楚。

normal.en: In code, an assertion is a promise that a condition holds, and a failed assertion stops the program.
normal.cn: 在代码里，断言是「某条件成立」的承诺，断言失败会中止程序。

normal.en: Assertion of rights is a fixed legal phrase, showing that the word kept its declarative legal force.
normal.cn: 「权利的主张」是固定法律说法，说明这个词保留了宣告式的法律力量。

abstract.en: An assertion is a claim wearing the clothes of a fact, and the clothes are what listeners must see through.
abstract.cn: 断言是一个穿着事实外衣的主张，而听众要做的正是看穿这件外衣。

abstract.en: Every field has its own way of stamping: logic stamps truth values, law stamps rights, code stamps conditions.
abstract.cn: 每个领域都有自己的盖章方式：逻辑盖真值，法律盖权利，代码盖条件。

abstract.en: The word reminds us that before evidence arrives, all we have is someone standing behind a sentence.
abstract.cn: 这个词提醒我们，在证据到来之前，我们只有某个人站在一句话后面。

examples.en: The author's assertion about rising costs is supported by three surveys.
examples.cn: 作者关于成本上升的断言得到三项调查的支持。

examples.en: No one could disprove his assertion that the method was safe.
examples.cn: 没有人能反驳他关于该方法安全的断言。

examples.en: The code contains an assertion that the list is never empty.
examples.cn: 这段代码里有一个断言，声明该列表永不为空。

dict_mnemonic.text: 读作「阿瑟申」——把话「申」明得像盖了章，一口咬定，就是断言

root: 拉丁语 asserere「主张、维护」= ad-「朝向」+ serere「连接、排成行」，字面为「接到自己身上」。罗马法用它表示主张自由或权利；名词经法语于十五世纪进入英语，兼指坚定陈述与权利维护；二十世纪编程语言又借它指断言语句。最早记录年代不确定。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses run from speech act to code: a confident statement, a challengeable claim, a declaration of rights, a logical proposition, a program assertion, a forceful opinion, a show of authority, and an unproved statement.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项从言语行为延伸到代码：自信陈述、可质疑的主张、权利声明、逻辑命题、程序断言、有力的意见、权威的彰显、无证明的陈述。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a seal is pressed hard onto paper, and the mark stays after the hand lifts.
core.cn: 核心意象：印章重重压上纸面，手抬起后印痕仍在。

branches.en: THE STAMPED SENTENCE: a firm statement that may or may not have proof behind it.
branches.cn: 盖章的句子：坚定的陈述，背后未必有证明。

branches.en: THE OPEN CLAIM: a statement that invites others to dispute it.
branches.cn: 敞开的主张：招来他人反驳的陈述。

branches.en: THE CLAIMED RIGHT: a right declared in public, and power shown by assertion.
branches.cn: 被主张的权利：公开宣告的权利，以及以断言彰显的权力。

branches.en: THE LOGICAL PROPOSITION: a statement carrying a truth value.
branches.cn: 逻辑命题：带有真值的陈述。

branches.en: THE CODE CHECK AND THE FORCEFUL TONE: a condition declared in code, and the weight of confident speech.
branches.cn: 代码检查与有力语气：在代码中声明的条件，以及自信说话的重量。

intro.en: Assertion is a Latin verb turned noun whose root of joining still appears in English words of insertion and series.
intro.cn: 这个词是拉丁语动词转成的名词，其「连接」词根至今仍出现在表示插入与系列的英语词中。

latinIntro.en: Latin supplies serere and asserere; the noun came through French and kept the legal flavour of claiming a right.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语提供了「连接」与「主张」两词；名词经法语而来，保留了「主张权利」的法律意味。

items.example: It turns joining into joining to oneself.
items.exampleCN: 它把「连接」变成「接到自己身上」。

items.meaning: to join, arrange in a row
items.example: The root of insert and series.
items.exampleCN: 这是「插入」与「系列」的词根。

items.example: The direct source of the English noun.
items.exampleCN: 这是英语名词的直接来源。

items.example: It forms assertion from the verb stem.
items.exampleCN: 它由动词词干构成「断言」。

items.example: The form ad- takes before s.
items.exampleCN: 这是「朝向」前缀在 s 前的变体。

items.example: It forms assertive from the verb.
items.exampleCN: 它由动词构成形容词「自信主张的」。
它构成「自信果断」这一名词。
它构成形容词「被主张的」。

加倾向形容词尾，义为「自信坚定的」
加性质名词尾，义为「自信果断」
加已然词尾，义为「被主张的」

definition_zh: 冬眠；越冬休眠；（计算机）休眠
definition_en: to pass the winter in a dormant state with lowered body temperature and metabolism
core_image: 秋末一只动物把自己塞进洞穴，呼吸与心跳慢下来，直到春天的暖意把它唤醒
scene: 秋末，一只蝙蝠钻进废弃矿井的深处，体温降到接近洞壁的温度。 Some bats hibernate in caves where the temperature stays above freezing.
sceneCN: 这里 hibernate 指「以低代谢状态度过冬天」（第 1 个义项：动物越冬休眠）；句意为有些蝙蝠在温度保持在冰点以上的洞穴里冬眠。图中可辨识物件：矿井支架、倒挂的蝙蝠、岩壁水痕、洞口霜花。

pos.zh: 冬眠；越冬休眠（不及物；主语为动物）
（计算机）休眠（不及物；主语为设备或系统）

derivatives.zh: hibernate + -ion（拉丁 -atio 动作名词后缀）→ 冬眠这一状态
hibernate + -or（施动者后缀）→ 进行冬眠的动物
hibernare + -aculum（场所后缀）→ 越冬的巢穴或越冬芽
hibernus（冬天的）+ -al（形容词后缀）→ 冬季的
hibernate + -ing（分词形容词）→ 正处于冬眠中的

senses.title: Pass the winter in dormancy
senses.definition: to spend the winter with body temperature, breathing and metabolism greatly reduced
senses.definitionCN: 在体温、呼吸与代谢大幅降低的状态下度过冬天
senses.example: Some bats hibernate in caves where the temperature stays above freezing.
senses.exampleCN: 有些蝙蝠在温度保持在冰点以上的洞穴里冬眠。
senses.why: The Latin verb hibernare simply meant 'to winter'; science narrowed it to wintering in torpor.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁动词 hibernare 本只表示「过冬」；科学用法把它收窄为「在昏睡中过冬」。

senses.title: Survive the cold season
senses.titleCN: 活过寒冷季节（较宽泛的用法）
senses.definition: to get through the winter, whether by torpor or by some other quiet strategy
senses.definitionCN: 度过冬天，无论靠昏睡还是别的安静策略
senses.example: The colony hibernates through the coldest eight weeks of the year.
senses.exampleCN: 这个群体在一年中最冷的八周里越冬休眠。
senses.why: Because the verb names the season itself, it can still carry the older, looser sense of simply lasting until spring.
senses.whyCN: 因为这个动词本指季节本身，所以仍保留较宽松的旧义：只是撑到春天。

senses.title: Put a computer into its disk-saved sleep
senses.titleCN: 让计算机进入把内存存入磁盘的休眠
senses.definition: to switch a computer into the state that writes memory to disk and cuts all power
senses.definitionCN: 把计算机切换到写入内存到磁盘并完全断电的状态
senses.example: Set the laptop to hibernate when the lid has been closed for an hour.
senses.exampleCN: 把笔记本设为合盖一小时后休眠。
senses.why: The machine is said to hibernate because it too stops, stores its contents and waits to be woken.
senses.whyCN: 机器也被说成 hibernate，因为它同样停下、存放内容、等待被唤醒。

senses.title: Withdraw from activity for a long stretch
senses.titleCN: 长期退出活动（人或组织的比喻用法）
senses.definition: to stop working, publishing or competing for a long period and then return
senses.definitionCN: 长时间停止工作、发表或竞争，然后再回来
senses.example: The author hibernated for three years and then published a short, sharp book.
senses.exampleCN: 这位作者蛰伏三年，然后出版了一本短而锐利的书。
senses.why: Withdrawal plus preserved capacity is the same shape as torpor, so the verb transfers easily to people and careers.
senses.whyCN: 退出加上保有能力，与昏睡同形，因此这个动词很容易转到人和事业上。

senses.title: Stay indoors through the cold months
senses.definition: to leave the house as little as possible during winter, in informal speech
senses.definitionCN: 口语中指冬天尽量不出门
senses.example: We hibernate at home from December to March, baking and watching old films.
senses.exampleCN: 我们从十二月到三月都窝在家里，烤点心、看老电影。
senses.why: The humorous human use keeps only the shell of the word: warm shelter, low activity, no travel.
senses.whyCN: 人的幽默用法只保留这个词的外壳：温暖的住处、低活动、不出行。

senses.title: Overwinter in a particular animal group
senses.titleCN: 某类动物特有的越冬方式
senses.definition: to adopt the winter rest characteristic of bats, insects, snakes or another named group
senses.definitionCN: 采用蝙蝠、昆虫、蛇等特定类群所具有的越冬休眠方式
senses.example: Certain insects hibernate as larvae buried below the frost line.
senses.exampleCN: 某些昆虫以幼虫形态在冻线以下休眠越冬。
senses.why: Group names add information because the physiological pattern differs sharply from species to species.
senses.whyCN: 加上类群名能补充信息，因为不同物种的生理模式差别很大。

senses.title: Fall into a long idle state
senses.titleCN: 设备或账户长期闲置后自动停用
senses.definition: to become inactive after a long period without use, as an account, service or machine does
senses.definitionCN: 长时间无人使用后进入不活跃状态，如账户、服务或机器
senses.example: Dormant accounts hibernate after two years and need a fresh login.
senses.exampleCN: 休眠账户两年后会停用，需要重新登录。
senses.why: This technical use borrows only the pause, not the metabolism: nothing is stored except state.
senses.whyCN: 这一技术用法只借用「暂停」，不涉及代谢：除了状态之外没有东西被保存。

senses.title: Lie low and revive later
senses.definition: to remain inactive as a project or plan until conditions allow it to start again
senses.definitionCN: 作为项目或计划保持不活跃，直到条件允许重新启动
senses.example: The plan hibernated during the funding freeze and revived last spring.
senses.exampleCN: 这项计划在资金冻结期间停摆，去年春天又复苏了。
senses.why: The word promises revival: hibernation is a pause, not an ending, which is why it suits stalled projects.
senses.whyCN: 这个词承诺复苏：冬眠只是暂停而非终结，因此适合形容停滞的项目。

intro.en: Hibernate is a seventeenth-century English verb from Latin hibernare 'to pass the winter', itself from hibernus 'wintry' and hiems 'winter'. The Latin verb first described soldiers and animals wintering in place.
intro.cn: hibernate 是十七世纪英语动词，来自拉丁 hibernare「过冬」，后者又由 hibernus「冬季的」与 hiems「冬天」构成。该拉丁动词最初描述士兵与动物在原地越冬。

items.en: Hiems was the standard noun for winter. Its earlier history is usually traced to a reconstructed Indo-European root for snow, a form marked with an asterisk because it is rebuilt rather than recorded.
items.cn: hiems 是表示「冬天」的标准拉丁名词。其更早历史一般追溯到原始印欧语中表示雪的重构词根，该形式带星号，表示是重建而非有记录。

items.en: From hiems came hibernus 'wintry', which survives in the English adjective hibernal and in the name of the winter months.
items.cn: 由 hiems 生出 hibernus「冬季的」，它留在英语形容词 hibernal 中，也留在冬季月份的名称里。

items.en: Hibernare meant 'to winter, to spend the winter'. Classical writers used it of troops in winter camp, not yet of animals in torpor.
items.cn: hibernare 意为「过冬、度过冬天」。古典作家用它指部队在冬营驻扎，尚未用于动物的昏睡。

items.en: The English verb appears in the seventeenth century. Sources differ on the exact first record, so the date should be treated as approximate.
items.cn: 英语动词出现于十七世纪。各家对确切首见记载说法不一，因此年代应视为约数。

items.en: Nineteenth- and twentieth-century physiology fixed the verb to the measurable state of low temperature, slow pulse and reduced oxygen use.
items.cn: 十九至二十世纪的生理学把这个动词固定为体温低、脉搏慢、耗氧少这一可测量状态。

items.en: Late twentieth-century computing extended the verb to a machine state, keeping the metaphor of a body saved and asleep.
items.cn: 二十世纪后期的计算技术把这个动词扩展到机器状态，保留了「身体被保存并睡着」的比喻。

note.en: Group one holds members of the same winter family that differ only by suffix; group two holds other verbs for resting through a hard season.
note.cn: 第一组是同一「冬天」词族中仅后缀不同的成员；第二组是其他表示在艰难季节中休息的动词。

entries.definition: The noun of the same verb, naming the state rather than the act; swapping the two changes the grammar of the sentence.
entries.definitionCN: 同一动词的名词形式，指状态而非动作；两者互换会改变句子的语法结构。

entries.definition: An adjective for 'of winter', from hibernus; it describes weather or light, never an animal's behaviour.
entries.definitionCN: 由 hibernus 来的「冬季的」形容词，描述天气或光线，绝不描述动物行为。

entries.definition: The place or bud in which an organism overwinters; it is a noun of location, not an action.
entries.definitionCN: 生物越冬所在的处所或越冬芽；是表示地点的名词，不是动作。

entries.definition: The animal that performs the action, formed with the agent suffix -or.
entries.definitionCN: 执行这一动作的动物，由施动后缀 -or 构成。

entries.definition: To live through the winter by whatever strategy, including staying active; hibernate names one specific strategy.
entries.definitionCN: 以任何策略活过冬天，包括保持活动；hibernate 只指其中一种特定策略。

entries.definition: To pass the hot or dry season in dormancy; it is the seasonal mirror image of hibernate.
entries.definitionCN: 在炎热或干旱季节休眠；是 hibernate 在季节上的镜像对应词。

entries.definition: Ordinary nightly rest with quick waking and normal body temperature; it is far shallower than hibernation.
entries.definitionCN: 普通的夜间休息，容易唤醒且体温正常；比冬眠浅得多。

entries.definition: A phrase for being inactive and waiting, often used of ideas, seeds or diseases; it lacks the seasonal winter frame.
entries.definitionCN: 表示不活动并等待的短语，常用于想法、种子或疾病；没有冬季这一季节框架。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real collocations and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: Hibernare is 'to winter': the verb is winter turned into an action.
normal.cn: hibernare 就是「过冬」：这个动词是把冬天变成动作。

normal.en: The family runs hibernate, hibernation, hibernator, hibernaculum, hibernal, hibernating.
normal.cn: 同族词包括 hibernate、hibernation、hibernator、hibernaculum、hibernal、hibernating。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark the use: hibernate through the winter, hibernate in a cave, hibernate until spring.
normal.cn: 固定搭配标出用法：整个冬天冬眠、在洞穴里冬眠、冬眠到春天。

normal.en: The computer menu item hibernate keeps the same metaphor of a saved body and a stopped clock.
normal.cn: 电脑菜单里的休眠项保留了「保存身体、停下时钟」的同一比喻。

normal.en: The stress falls on the first syllable: HIB-er-nate, like HIB-ernal.
normal.cn: 重音落在第一音节：HIB-er-nate，与 HIB-ernal 一致。

abstract.en: Picture an animal folding itself into a drawer and pulling the drawer shut.
abstract.cn: 想象一只动物把自己折进抽屉，再把抽屉推上。

abstract.en: Picture a machine saving its whole mind onto a disk before going dark.
abstract.cn: 想象一台机器在熄灭前把整个「心思」存进磁盘。

abstract.en: Picture a writer who disappears, then returns with a finished book.
abstract.cn: 想象一位作家消失一段时间，再带着写完的书回来。

examples.en: Some bats hibernate in caves where the temperature stays above freezing.
examples.cn: 有些蝙蝠在温度保持在冰点以上的洞穴里冬眠。

examples.en: Certain insects hibernate as larvae buried below the frost line.
examples.cn: 某些昆虫以幼虫形态在冻线以下休眠越冬。

examples.en: Set the laptop to hibernate when the lid has been closed for an hour.
examples.cn: 把笔记本设为合盖一小时后休眠。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「嗨，被窝里头」——钻进被窝把头一蒙，睡过整个冬天 → 冬眠

root: 拉丁 hibernare「过冬」，由 hibernus「冬天的」构成，源于 hiems「冬天」；更早形式一般追溯到原始印欧语表示雪与冬天的重构词根（星号形式为重构，非实录），确切音形存疑。英语 hibernate。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one gesture: activity is switched off and kept off. Biology owns the gesture; people, machines and projects borrow it.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项沿同一个动作展开：把活动关掉并保持关着。生物学拥有这个动作；人、机器与项目借用它。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a body tucked into a cold hole, its pulse slowed to a whisper, waiting for warmth.
core.cn: 核心意象：一具身体缩进寒冷的洞穴，脉搏慢成耳语，等待暖意。

branches.en: SEASONAL REST: the core act is wintering, with torpor as its technical and its looser reading.
branches.cn: 季节性休息：核心动作是越冬，既可读作昏睡，也可读作较宽松的撑过冬天。

branches.en: SWITCHED-OFF MACHINE: equipment copies the pause but stores only its state.
branches.cn: 关掉的机器：设备复制了暂停，但只保存状态。

branches.en: HUMAN AND PROJECT WITHDRAWAL: a person or plan lies low with capacity intact, then returns.
branches.cn: 人与项目的退隐：人或计划带着完整能力潜伏，然后回来。

branches.en: HOMELY SHELTER: the everyday sense keeps only warmth, food and no travel.
branches.cn: 居家的庇护：日常义只保留温暖、食物与不出行。

branches.en: GROUP PATTERN: different animals perform the same act in sharply different ways.
branches.cn: 类群模式：不同动物以差别很大的方式完成同一动作。

intro.en: Hibernate is the bare Latin verb adapted to English, and every family member adds a different suffix to the same winter root.
intro.cn: hibernate 是把拉丁动词直接改成英语，词族每个成员都是在同一「冬天」词根上加不同后缀。

latinIntro.en: Hiems 'winter' gives hibernus 'wintry' and hibernare 'to winter'; -atio makes the state noun, -or the agent, -aculum the place, -al the adjective.
latinIntro.cn: hiems「冬天」生出 hibernus「冬季的」与 hibernare「过冬」；-atio 构成状态名词，-or 表施动者，-aculum 表场所，-al 构成形容词。

items.example: The frogs hibernate under the mud.
Hibernation begins with the first frost.
Bats are the most familiar hibernators.
items.exampleCN: 蝙蝠是最为人熟知的冬眠动物。

items.example: The pupa rests in a silk hibernaculum.
items.exampleCN: 蛹在丝质越冬室里休息。

items.meaning: in the act of winter dormancy
items.example: A hibernating animal should not be disturbed.
items.exampleCN: 不应打扰冬眠中的动物。

items.example: Pre-hibernation fat is laid down in autumn.
items.exampleCN: 冬眠前的脂肪在秋季囤积。

definition_zh: n. 勤勉；勤奋；细致用心；（商务）尽职（due diligence）
definition_en: steady, careful and persistent effort in doing something
core_image: 台灯下摊开的练习册，草稿纸写满一张又一张；墙上的日历被一格格划掉
scene: 他靠勤勉补上了落下的功课。 He caught up through sheer diligence.
sceneCN: 这里 diligence 是「勤勉」（第 1 个义项：长期、持续、用心地做事）；句意是他靠勤勉补上了落下的功课。图中可辨识物件：台灯下摊开的练习册、写满的草稿纸、墙上一格格划掉的日历。

pos.zh: 勤勉；勤奋；细致用心；（商务）尽职

senses.title: Steady careful effort
senses.definition: persistent, attentive work kept up over time
senses.definitionCN: （名词）长期保持的专注努力
senses.example: He caught up through sheer diligence.
senses.exampleCN: 他靠勤勉补上了落下的功课。
senses.why: A lamp-lit workbook with draft sheets filled one after another.
senses.whyCN: 台灯下摊开的练习册，草稿纸一张接一张写满。

senses.title: The care owed to a task
senses.definition: the careful checking expected before a decision, as in due diligence
senses.definitionCN: （名词）决策前应做的细致核查，如尽职调查
senses.example: The buyers completed their due diligence in March.
senses.exampleCN: 买方在三月完成了尽职调查。
senses.why: A folder of contracts ticked twice in different coloured pens.
senses.whyCN: 一夹合同被两种颜色的笔各打了一遍勾。

senses.title: A public stagecoach
senses.definition: a fast public horse-drawn coach, from the French diligence
senses.definitionCN: （名词）一种快捷的公共马车，来自法语 diligence
senses.example: The travellers booked seats on the Paris diligence.
senses.exampleCN: 旅客订了去巴黎的驿站马车座位。
senses.why: A four-horse coach waiting outside a posting inn.
senses.whyCN: 一辆四马马车停在驿站旅店外。

intro.en: Diligence comes from Latin diligentia, from diligere, to single out and value highly, itself from dis- apart and legere, to choose.
intro.cn: diligence 来自拉丁语 diligentia，源自 diligere（挑出来并看重），而 diligere 由 dis-（分开）与 legere（挑选）构成。

items.en: Legere meant to choose or gather.
items.cn: legere 意为挑选、收集。

items.en: Dis- meant apart.
items.cn: dis- 意为分开。

items.en: Diligere meant to pick out and value highly.
items.cn: diligere 意为挑出来并看重。

items.en: Diligentia named careful attention.
items.cn: diligentia 指细致的用心。

items.en: Diligence entered English for steady care.
items.cn: 十四世纪 diligence 以「持续用心」义进入英语。

items.en: A fast French coach was called a diligence for its speed.
items.cn: 十八世纪法国一种快捷马车因速度被称作 diligence。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the lig- choose root; the near-meaning group names other kinds of steady work.
note.cn: 形近组共享 lig-（挑选）词根；近义组是其他表示「持续用功」的词。

entries.definition: Showing steady careful effort.
entries.definitionCN: 表现出持续用心的。

entries.definition: Failure to take proper care.
entries.definitionCN: 未能给予应有的注意。

entries.definition: The ability to learn and understand, also from legere.
entries.definitionCN: 学习与理解的能力；同样来自 legere。

entries.definition: Steady, energetic work.
entries.definitionCN: 持续而有劲头的工作。

entries.definition: Continuing despite difficulty.
entries.definitionCN: 不顾困难坚持下去。

entries.definition: Care that covers every detail.
entries.definitionCN: 覆盖每个细节的细致。

normalIntro.en: Diligence is di- apart plus lig- choose: pick out what matters and keep working at it.
normalIntro.cn: diligence 就是 di-（分开）加 lig-（挑）：挑出要紧的事，一直做下去。

normal.en: Di- apart plus lig- choose means pick out and keep at it.
normal.cn: di-（分开）加 lig-（挑）就是挑出来一直做。

normal.en: Diligent is the adjective, diligently the adverb.
normal.cn: diligent 是形容词，diligently 是副词。

normal.en: Due diligence is the check before you buy.
normal.cn: due diligence 是买入前的核查。

normal.en: Negligence is the same root turned negative.
normal.cn: negligence 是同根变否定。

normal.en: A French stagecoach was also called a diligence.
normal.cn: 法国的一种驿站马车也叫 diligence。

abstract.en: A lamp-lit workbook with draft sheets filled one after another.
abstract.cn: 台灯下摊开的练习册，草稿纸一张接一张写满。

abstract.en: A folder of contracts ticked twice in different coloured pens.
abstract.cn: 一夹合同被两种颜色的笔各打了一遍勾。

abstract.en: A four-horse coach waiting outside a posting inn.
abstract.cn: 一辆四马马车停在驿站旅店外。

examples.en: He caught up through sheer diligence.
examples.cn: 他靠勤勉补上了落下的功课。

examples.en: The buyers completed their due diligence in March.
examples.cn: 买方在三月完成了尽职调查。

examples.en: Her diligence was rewarded with a scholarship.
examples.cn: 她的勤勉换来了奖学金。

dict_mnemonic.text: diligence ＝ di-（分开）＋ lig-（拉丁语 legere「挑选、收集」，同根 elegant、intelligence）＋ -ence（名词后缀）＝把要紧的事挑出来、一直用心做，「勤勉」。商务里的 due diligence 就是「该做的用心」＝尽职调查。

root: 拉丁语 dis-（分开）＋ legere（挑选）→ diligere（挑出来并看重）→ diligentia（用心）→ 古法语 diligence → 英语 diligence

sensesIntro.en: Care that keeps going: a lamp-lit workbook, a folder checked twice and a coach that never stopped.
sensesIntro.cn: 一直不停的用心：台灯下的练习册、查了两遍的文件夹，以及一辆从不停歇的马车。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a lamp-lit workbook open on a desk while draft sheets pile up beside it night after night
core.cn: 核心意象：台灯下的练习册摊在桌上，草稿纸一夜又一夜在旁边堆高

branches.en: A lamp-lit workbook with draft sheets filled one after another.
branches.cn: 台灯下摊开的练习册，草稿纸一张接一张写满。

branches.en: A folder of contracts ticked twice in different coloured pens.
branches.cn: 一夹合同被两种颜色的笔各打了一遍勾。

branches.en: A four-horse coach waiting outside a posting inn.
branches.cn: 一辆四马马车停在驿站旅店外。

branches.en: Both keep attention on the work until it is right.
branches.cn: 两者都把注意力放在工作上直到做对。

branches.en: Both were named for speed that does not slacken.
branches.cn: 两者都因不肯松劲的速度而得名。

intro.en: Diligence is di- plus lig- plus -ence; the choose root also builds elegant, eligible and intelligence.
intro.cn: diligence 由 di- 加 lig- 加 -ence 构成；挑选这个词根也造出 elegant、eligible 与 intelligence。

latinIntro.en: Latin legere means to choose or gather, diligere to value highly and severus strict.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 legere 意为挑选、收集，diligere 意为看重，severus 意为严格的。

definition_zh: 监管的；规章的；调节性的
definition_en: relating to the rules and agencies that control an activity, or to the parts that control a biological process
core_image: 一块写满条款的告示牌立在工厂大门前，旁边站着检查员
scene: 这里指「监管的」。 The regulatory agency approved the drug after two years of review.
sceneCN: 这里 regulatory 指「监管性质的」（第 2 个义项：与监管机构及其审查有关）；句意：监管机构经两年审查后批准了该药物。图中可辨识物件：告示牌、条款、检查员证件、工厂大门。

pos.zh: 监管的；规章的；与监管机构有关的；（生物学）调节性的

senses.title: Relating to rules
senses.titleCN: 规章性的：与规则体系有关
senses.definition: connected with the making or applying of rules that govern an activity
senses.definitionCN: 与制定或适用管理某项活动的规则有关
senses.example: The regulatory system for food additives is complex.
senses.exampleCN: 食品添加剂的规章体系很复杂。
senses.why: The adjective adds -ory to regulator, so it describes whatever belongs to the work of ruling by rules.
senses.whyCN: 形容词由 regulator 加 -ory 构成，描述属于「依规则治理」工作的事物。

senses.title: Of an oversight body
senses.titleCN: 监管机构的：指负责监督的机关
senses.definition: describing an official body whose job is to supervise and enforce rules in a sector
senses.definitionCN: 形容负责监督并执行某行业规则的官方机构
senses.example: The regulatory agency approved the drug after two years.
senses.exampleCN: 监管机构经两年审查后批准了该药物。
senses.why: Institutions need a label for themselves: an agency that regulates is regulatory, and the adjective becomes part of its name.
senses.whyCN: 机构需要给自身一个标签：负责监管的机关就是 regulatory，形容词成了机构名称的一部分。

senses.title: Compliance with rules
senses.definition: describing the state of meeting the rules set by authorities
senses.definitionCN: 形容满足主管机关所设规则的状态
senses.example: Regulatory compliance costs the firm about a million dollars a year.
senses.exampleCN: 监管合规每年花掉这家公司约一百万美元。
senses.why: The adjective marks the boundary between permitted and forbidden conduct, and compliance is living inside that boundary.
senses.whyCN: 形容词标记允许与禁止行为之间的边界，而合规就是生活在这条边界之内。

senses.title: Framework and approval
senses.titleCN: 框架与审批：规则体系及放行程序
senses.definition: describing the structure of rules and the formal permissions required before an activity may proceed
senses.definitionCN: 形容规则的整体结构，以及活动开始前所需的正式许可
senses.example: No product reaches the market without regulatory approval.
senses.exampleCN: 没有产品能在未获监管审批的情况下进入市场。
senses.why: A framework is the architecture of rules; approval is the gate, and the same adjective covers both.
senses.whyCN: 框架是规则的建筑结构，审批是闸门，同一个形容词涵盖两者。

senses.title: The cost of oversight
senses.titleCN: 监管负担：合规带来的成本
senses.definition: describing the time, money and staff that rules impose on those they govern
senses.definitionCN: 形容规则对被监管者施加的时间、金钱与人力成本
senses.example: Small firms complain about the regulatory burden.
senses.exampleCN: 小公司抱怨监管负担。
senses.why: The adjective can turn critical: what began as protection is also measured as a weight carried by business.
senses.whyCN: 这个形容词可以转为批评：原本的保护措施也被计为企业的负担。

senses.title: Biological control elements
senses.titleCN: 生物调控元件：控制基因开关的片段
senses.definition: in genetics, describing DNA sequences or molecules that control when a gene is expressed
senses.definitionCN: 遗传学中形容控制基因何时表达的 DNA 序列或分子
senses.example: A regulatory sequence upstream of the gene binds a repressor.
senses.exampleCN: 基因上游的调控序列会结合阻遏蛋白。
senses.why: Biology uses the same adjective for the parts that regulate: the controlling function, not the rule-making institution.
senses.whyCN: 生物学用同一个形容词指执行调控的部件：是控制功能，而非制定规则的机构。

senses.title: Regulatory capture
senses.titleCN: 监管俘获：监管者被被监管者影响
senses.definition: describing the situation in which an agency comes to serve the industry it is meant to oversee
senses.definitionCN: 形容监管机构转而服务于本应被其监督的行业的情形
senses.example: Regulatory capture can turn a watchdog into a partner.
senses.exampleCN: 监管俘获可能把看门狗变成伙伴。
senses.why: The phrase names a failure of the adjective's purpose: the regulator still regulates, but in the industry's interest.
senses.whyCN: 该短语命名形容词所指目的的失败：监管者仍在监管，却是按行业利益监管。

senses.title: Cross-border coordination
senses.titleCN: 跨境监管协调：不同辖区规则对接
senses.definition: describing cooperation among countries or jurisdictions to align their rules and standards
senses.definitionCN: 形容国家或辖区之间为统一规则与标准而进行的合作
senses.example: Regulatory cooperation reduced duplicate inspections.
senses.exampleCN: 监管合作减少了重复检查。
senses.why: As trade crosses borders, the adjective extends from one agency to the relations among many.
senses.whyCN: 当贸易跨越国界，形容词便从单一机构扩展到许多机构之间的关系。

intro.en: Regulatory is an English adjective: regulator plus the ending -ory, which comes from Latin -orius. Regulator itself is regulare 'to rule' plus -or 'one who'.
intro.cn: regulatory 是英语形容词：regulator 加词尾 -ory，后者出自拉丁 -orius。regulator 本身则是 regulare「管理」加 -or「做某事的人」。

items.en: Regula 'rule, straight stick' is the base. It is generally connected with regere 'to guide straight'.
items.cn: 词基是 regula「规则、直木条」，一般认为与 regere「引直、治理」相关。

items.en: Regulare meant 'to rule, regulate'; adding -or produced regulator, 'one who regulates', used for officials and later for devices.
items.cn: regulare 意为「管理、调节」；加 -or 构成 regulator「调节者」，先用于官员，后用于装置。

items.en: The adjective suffix -orius formed words meaning 'belonging to or serving' a person or function; English -ory descends from it.
items.cn: 形容词后缀 -orius 构成意为「属于或服务于某人/某功能」的词；英语 -ory 由此而来。

items.en: Regulatory appears in English in the eighteenth and nineteenth centuries, first in legal and administrative writing.
items.cn: regulatory 于 18 至 19 世纪出现在英语中，最早见于法律与行政文本。

items.en: The twentieth century extended it to independent agencies, compliance departments, and gene regulatory sequences.
items.cn: 20 世纪把它扩展到独立监管机构、合规部门与基因调控序列。

items.en: The exact first English citation is uncertain, and the relationship of regula to regere is accepted rather than fully documented.
items.cn: 来源不确定（派生路径）：英语最早书证确切年代存疑；regula 与 regere 的关系属于「一般认为」，并非完全有文献可证。

note.en: The first group separates the regulate family; the second gives near-synonyms for rule-making and for control.
note.cn: 第一组区分 regulate 词族；第二组给出关于规则制定与控制的近义词。

entries.definition: The rule or the act. Regulatory is the adjective placed before agency, framework or compliance.
entries.definitionCN: 指规则或动作；regulatory 是放在 agency、framework、compliance 前的形容词。

entries.definition: The institution or mechanism that regulates. Regulatory describes such a body's character.
entries.definitionCN: 指进行监管的机构或装置；regulatory 描述这类机构的性质。

entries.definition: To make or apply rules. Regulatory never functions as a verb.
entries.definitionCN: 指制定或适用规则；regulatory 从不用作动词。

entries.definition: Organized with rigid discipline. It is critical and has nothing to do with formal agencies.
entries.definitionCN: 指以严格纪律组织起来，带批评意味，与正式监管机构无关。

entries.definition: Relating to the running of an organization. Regulatory work is one kind of administration, focused on rules.
entries.definitionCN: 指与组织运作有关；监管工作是行政管理的一种，聚焦于规则。

entries.definition: Created or required by a formal law. Regulatory bodies are often statutory, but the words answer different questions.
entries.definitionCN: 指由正式法律创设或要求；监管机构常为法定机构，但两词回答的问题不同。

entries.definition: Relating to oversight of people or work. Supervision may be internal, while regulatory usually implies public authority.
entries.definitionCN: 指对人员或工作的监督；监督可以是内部的，而 regulatory 通常暗示公共权威。

entries.definition: Having power over something. It is broader and more forceful than regulatory, which works through rules.
entries.definitionCN: 指对某物拥有控制权，范围更广、语气更强；regulatory 则通过规则运作。

entries.definition: The activity of enforcing order. It stresses detection and enforcement more than rule design.
entries.definitionCN: 指维持秩序的执法活动，更强调发现与执行，而非规则设计。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real collocations and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: regulator + -ory: belonging to the work of ruling by rules.
normal.cn: regulator + -ory：属于「依规则治理」的工作。

normal.en: The family runs regulate, regulation, regulator, deregulation, self-regulatory.
normal.cn: 同族词包括 regulate、regulation、regulator、deregulation、self-regulatory。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark the field: regulatory agency, regulatory framework, regulatory compliance, regulatory burden.
normal.cn: 固定搭配标出领域：监管机构、监管框架、监管合规、监管负担。

normal.en: regulatory capture names the watchdog that ends up serving the industry.
normal.cn: 监管俘获指看门狗最终反过来服务行业。

normal.en: In genetics, a regulatory sequence switches a gene on or off.
normal.cn: 遗传学中，调控序列开关基因。

abstract.en: Picture a gate with a clipboard beside it, where every truck must show its papers.
abstract.cn: 想象一道大门旁放着记录板，每辆卡车都要出示文件。

abstract.en: Picture a switch upstream of a lamp, deciding whether the lamp can light at all.
abstract.cn: 想象灯的上游有个开关，决定灯能否亮起。

abstract.en: Picture a watchdog slowly being fed by the same hand it was meant to guard against.
abstract.cn: 想象一条看门狗慢慢被它本该防着的那只手喂养。

examples.en: Regulatory approval for the new aircraft took four years.
examples.cn: 新飞机的监管审批用了四年。

examples.en: The company hired a regulatory affairs team before launch.
examples.cn: 公司在上市前组建了监管事务团队。

examples.en: A regulatory sequence can silence a gene without changing its code.
examples.cn: 调控序列可以在不改变基因编码的情况下使其沉默。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「regulator（监管者）+ y」——带着规章来管 → regulatory 监管的

root: 拉丁 regula「规则」→ regulare「管理」→ regulator「监管者」+ -ory（形容词后缀）→ regulatory。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses show the adjective spreading from a rule, to an agency, to compliance, approval, cost, genes, capture and cross-border cooperation.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项展示该形容词的扩展：从一条规则，到机构、合规、审批、成本、基因、俘获与跨境合作。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a clipboard gate where every truck must show papers.
core.cn: 核心意象：记录板旁的大门，每辆卡车都要出示文件。

branches.en: RULES AND BODIES: the rule system itself, and the agency that administers it.
branches.cn: 规则与机构：规则体系本身，以及执行它的机构。

branches.en: THE GATE: compliance inside the boundary, and approval before entry.
branches.cn: 闸门：边界之内的合规，以及进入之前的审批。

branches.en: THE WEIGHT: the same protection is also a cost carried by the regulated.
branches.cn: 负担：同一保护措施也成为被监管者承担的成本。

branches.en: BIOLOGY: the controlling part of a gene, not a controlling institution.
branches.cn: 生物学：基因的调控部件，而非监管机构。

branches.en: FAILURE AND SCALE: the watchdog may be captured, and rules must meet across borders.
branches.cn: 失败与尺度：看门狗可能被俘获，规则还须跨境对接。

intro.en: Regulatory stacks an agent noun and an adjective ending: regulate, regulator, then -ory, from Latin -orius.
intro.cn: regulatory 叠加了施动名词与形容词词尾：regulate、regulator，再加出自拉丁 -orius 的 -ory。

latinIntro.en: The regula family supplies rule, regular, regulate, regulator, regulation, regime and regiment; each keeps the image of a straight line or a fixed order.
latinIntro.cn: regula 词族提供 rule、regular、regulate、regulator、regulation、regime、regiment，每个词都保留直线或固定秩序的意象。

items.meaningCN: 属于规则制定或控制的
items.example: Regulatory oversight increased after the accident.
items.exampleCN: 事故之后监管监督加强了。

items.example: The state regulates the sale of alcohol.

items.meaning: a rule; the act of regulating
items.example: The regulation limits sulfur in fuel.
items.exampleCN: 该规章限制燃料中的硫含量。

items.meaning: an official body or device that regulates
items.meaningCN: 进行监管的机构或装置
items.exampleCN: 监管机构公布了调查结果。

items.example: Regular inspections keep the plant safe.
items.exampleCN: 定期检查保障工厂安全。

items.example: The press adopted a self-regulatory code.
items.exampleCN: 新闻界通过了自我监管守则。
放松监管方案轻松通过。

items.example: The tax regime favours small firms.

definition_zh: 通信系统；信息从发送者传到接收者的一整套通道与规则；（引申）一个社会或组织维持联络的整体安排
definition_en: the whole set of channels, codes and rules by which messages travel from a sender to a receiver
core_image: 深谷两侧各立一座铁塔，话音被拆成电码沿铁塔与光缆传过去，到对岸再拼回人声
scene: 山两侧的村落隔着深谷，人们把话交给铁塔与光缆，话音在对岸重新拼回原声。 The communication system carried a greeting across the valley faster than a runner could walk it.
sceneCN: 这里 communication system 指信息从发送者传到接收者的一整套通道与规则（第 1 个义项：作为整体安排）；句意为这套通信系统把一句问候送过山谷，比人跑过去还快。

pos.zh: 通信系统；信息传递体系（可数，指一套通道与规则）
（生物学）动物的信号传递系统（可数）

derivatives.zh: 交流；传递（由拉丁 communicare 直接借入，核心是「使信息成为共同所有」，侧重动作）
交流；通信（由基础动词加表过程或结果的名词后缀而来，由动作转指过程与内容，是本词组的基础名词）
乐于交流的；传达性的（由基础动词加表性质的形容词后缀而来，由动作转指性质）
传讯者；善于表达的人（由基础动词加表施事者的名词后缀而来，由动作转指施事的人）
系统性的；全身的（由基础名词加表属性的形容词后缀而来，由「整体」转指「属于整体结构」）

senses.title: The whole arrangement
senses.definition: the complete set of channels, codes and rules that lets messages pass from sender to receiver
senses.definitionCN: 让信息从发送者抵达接收者的全部通道、编码与规则
senses.example: A reliable communication system is the first need of any remote field station.
senses.exampleCN: 对任何偏远野外观测站来说，一套可靠的通信系统是首要需求。
senses.why: The two words name a circuit, not a device: system supplies the idea of parts standing together as one working whole.
senses.whyCN: 这两个词命名的是一条回路，而不是一台设备：后一个词提供「多个部分合成一个运作整体」的意思。

senses.title: The hardware network
senses.definition: the physical infrastructure of cables, towers, satellites and switches that carries signals
senses.definitionCN: 由电缆、铁塔、卫星与交换机等实体设施构成的信号承载网络
senses.example: The storm disabled the region's communication system for two days.
senses.exampleCN: 风暴让该地区的通信系统瘫痪了两天。
senses.why: Once messages travel by wire, the arrangement becomes visible as hardware, and the word shifts from rules to machinery.
senses.whyCN: 一旦信息靠线路传输，这套安排就以硬件的形式显形，词义也从规则转向机器。

senses.title: Signalling in the body
senses.definition: the ways animals exchange information by sound, scent, gesture or dance
senses.definitionCN: 动物用声音、气味、姿态或舞蹈交换信息的方式
senses.example: Bees rely on a chemical communication system inside the hive.
senses.exampleCN: 蜜蜂在蜂巢内依靠一套化学通信系统。
senses.why: The same circuit exists without any technology: a sender, a signal, a channel and a receiver can all be organic.
senses.whyCN: 同一条回路不需要技术也能存在：发送者、信号、通道与接收者都可以是生物体。

senses.title: A society's media order
senses.definition: the mix of speech, print and broadcast through which a whole population shares news
senses.definitionCN: 一个全体人口借以共享消息的言谈、印刷与广播的组合
senses.example: Print created a national communication system out of scattered local dialects.
senses.exampleCN: 印刷把零散的地方方言编织成一套全国性的通信体系。
senses.why: A society also sends messages to itself; its media form a system with its own reach, speed and blind spots.
senses.whyCN: 社会也在给自己发消息；它的媒介构成一个有特定覆盖、速度与盲区的系统。

senses.title: Information flow in an organization
senses.definition: the fixed routes and routines by which orders, reports and records move inside a body
senses.definitionCN: 命令、报告与档案在一个机构内部流动的固定路线与惯例
senses.example: The army rebuilt its communication system after the radio failure.
senses.exampleCN: 无线电故障之后，部队重建了它的通信体系。
senses.why: An organization is held together by messages going up and down; the routes themselves are what the phrase names here.
senses.whyCN: 组织靠上下流动的消息维持一体；这里命名的正是那些路线本身。

senses.title: A shared protocol
senses.definition: a standard format and set of rules that two devices must follow to exchange data
senses.definitionCN: 两台设备交换数据时必须遵循的标准格式与规则
senses.example: The two devices share a common communication system, so they pair at once.
senses.exampleCN: 两台设备共用一套通信协议，所以立刻就能配对。
senses.why: Compatibility is a code agreement; the smallest system two machines can share is one common way of formatting a signal.
senses.whyCN: 兼容性就是一种编码约定；两台机器能共用的最小系统，就是一套共同的信号格式。

senses.title: One person's means of contact
senses.definition: the informal set of tools a person uses to stay in touch with others
senses.definitionCN: 一个人用来与他人保持联系的非正式工具组合
senses.example: Her only communication system is a phone and two messaging apps.
senses.exampleCN: 她唯一的联络手段是一部手机和两个聊天软件。
senses.why: Everyday use shrinks the system to whatever sits in one pocket: the word stretches from institutions down to a personal kit.
senses.whyCN: 日常用法把系统缩小到口袋里那点东西：词义从制度一路延伸到个人的工具包。

senses.title: The model in communication theory
senses.definition: a formal model of sender, message, channel, noise and receiver used to measure information
senses.definitionCN: 由发送者、消息、通道、噪声与接收者构成、用于度量信息的正式模型
senses.example: Shannon modelled the communication system as a sender, a channel and a receiver.
senses.exampleCN: 香农把通信系统建模为发送者、通道与接收者。
senses.why: Theory strips away people and wires and keeps only the boxes and arrows, turning the phrase into an abstract object of study.
senses.whyCN: 理论剥去人与线路，只留下方框与箭头，于是这个词组变成了抽象的研究对象。

intro.en: The phrase joins communication, from Latin communicatio 'a making common', and system, from Greek systema 'a whole compounded of parts'. It became a technical term with telegraphy and was formalized in information theory. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: 这个词组由 communication（来自拉丁 communicatio「使共同」）与 system（来自希腊 systema「由多部分合成的整体」）组合而成。它随电报技术成为术语，又在信息论中被形式化。年代均为约数。

items.en: Communicare 'to share, impart' comes from communis 'common, shared'. The usual analysis is com- 'together' plus munus 'duty, gift, office'; the deeper origin of munus is not established.
items.cn: communicare「分享、传达」来自 communis「共同的、共享的」。通行分析是前缀表「共同」加 munus「职责、赠礼、公务」；munus 更深的来源未得到证明。

items.en: Communicatio was the noun of action for 'a making common, an imparting', already used for sharing speech and goods.
items.cn: communicatio 是表示「使共同、传达」的动作名词，早已用于分享言谈与财物。

items.en: Systema meant 'an organized body, a whole of several parts', built on syn- 'together' and histanai 'to cause to stand'.
items.cn: systema 意为「有组织的整体、由若干部分合成的整体」，由表示「一起」的成分与 histanai「使站立」构成。

items.en: Late Latin borrowed systema as 'a whole, an organized body'; English system followed through French in the sixteenth century.
items.cn: 晚期拉丁语借入 systema，义为「整体、有组织的身体」；英语 system 在十六世纪经法语进入。

items.en: In the nineteenth century communication system became a practical term for the wires, stations and codes that carried messages over distance.
items.cn: 十九世纪，communication system 成为实用术语，指远距离传递消息的线路、站点与电码。

items.en: Shannon's 1948 model fixed the modern technical reading: a source, a transmitter, a channel with noise, and a receiver. The phrase was thereby turned into a measurable object.
items.cn: 香农在一九四八年的模型确定了现代技术读法：信源、发送器、带噪声的通道与接收者。这个词组由此变成可度量的对象。

note.en: Group one contains words built from the same two roots; group two holds near neighbours for networks and information flow.
note.cn: 第一组是由同样两个词根构成的词；第二组是网络与信息流方面的近邻词。

entries.definition: The act or process of exchanging information; it lacks the system's emphasis on connected parts.
entries.definitionCN: 交换信息的动作或过程；它没有 system 那种「各部分连成整体」的重点。

entries.definition: A group of people sharing something; it comes from the same 'common' root but names people, not channels.
entries.definitionCN: 共享某物的一群人；同出「共同」词根，却指人，不指通道。

entries.definition: Shared participation, often religious; it names the sharing itself, not a technical network.
entries.definitionCN: 共同的参与，常用于宗教；它指共享本身，而非技术网络。

entries.definition: Any set of connected parts; alone it says nothing about messages or signals.
entries.definitionCN: 任何由相连部分构成的整体；单用时与消息或信号无关。

entries.definition: The linked nodes themselves; a communication system adds the codes and rules that make the links carry meaning.
entries.definitionCN: 相互连接的节点本身；通信系统还要加上使连接能承载意义的编码与规则。

entries.definition: The physical facilities a society needs; it is broader and says nothing about messages.
entries.definitionCN: 社会所需的实体设施；范围更宽，且不涉及消息。

entries.definition: A system of signals, common for railways and cells; it stresses the signs rather than the whole organisation.
entries.definitionCN: 信号构成的系统，常用于铁路与细胞；它强调信号本身，而非整个组织。

entries.definition: A system for storing and processing data; it foregrounds records and computation rather than transmission.
entries.definitionCN: 用于存储与处理数据的系统；它突出记录与计算，而非传输。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real compounds and real technical phrases, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实的复合词与真实的技术说法，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: Communication carries 'common': a message becomes common property once it arrives.
normal.cn: communication 含着「共同」：消息一到，就成了双方共同拥有的东西。

normal.en: System means parts standing together, so the phrase is literally 'the standing-together of shared messages'.
normal.cn: system 意为各部分站在一起，所以这个词组字面上就是「共享消息的一体化」。

normal.en: The telegraph gave the phrase its modern body: wires, stations and codes.
normal.cn: 电报给了这个词组现代的身体：线路、站点与电码。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark the scale: a modern communication system, the global communication system, communication system design.
normal.cn: 固定说法标出尺度：现代通信系统、全球通信系统、通信系统设计。

normal.en: The plural communication systems and the unchanged attributive form are both standard.
normal.cn: 复数 communication systems 与作定语时不变形，都是标准用法。

abstract.en: Picture two towers facing each other across a valley, each one repeating what it hears.
abstract.cn: 想象两座塔隔着山谷相对，各自把听到的东西复述出去。

abstract.en: Picture the body as a network of nerves where a signal is never stored, only passed on.
abstract.cn: 想象身体是一张神经网络，信号从不被储存，只被传递。

abstract.en: Picture a society as a single ear listening to its own broadcast, deciding what counts as news.
abstract.cn: 想象一个社会是一只耳朵，听着自己的广播，并决定什么才算新闻。

examples.en: Engineers extended the communication system to the last village in the valley.
examples.cn: 工程师把通信系统延伸到了山谷里最后一个村庄。

examples.en: Ants use a chemical communication system that no satellite can intercept.
examples.cn: 蚂蚁使用一套化学通信系统，任何卫星都无法截获。

examples.en: A company's communication system fails when bad news travels slower than good news.
examples.cn: 当一个公司的坏消息比好消息传得慢，它的通信体系就失灵了。

dict_mnemonic.text: communication（使共同）+ system（各部分站在一起）＝ 让消息在各方之间成为共同财产的那套安排；记「有发有收，中间有路」。

root: communication 源自拉丁 communicare「使共同、传达」，其词根 communis 意为「共同的」，一般分析为前缀表「共同」加 mūnus「职责、赠礼」，mūnus 更深的来源不确定；system 源自希腊 systema「由多部分合成的整体」，由前缀表「一起」加 histanai「使站立」构成，更早形式属重构。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one circuit at different scales: the whole arrangement, its hardware, a body's signals, a society's media, an organisation's routes, a shared protocol, one person's kit, and the theorist's model.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项是同一回路在不同尺度上的取景：整体安排、硬件网络、生物信号、社会媒介、组织路线、共用协议、个人工具，以及理论家的模型。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a message leaves one mouth, passes through towers and codes, and arrives whole at another ear.
core.cn: 核心意象：消息离开一张嘴，穿过铁塔与编码，完整地抵达另一只耳朵。

branches.en: ARRANGEMENT AND HARDWARE: first the whole set of rules, then the metal and glass that carry them.
branches.cn: 安排与硬件：先是整套规则，再是承载规则的金属与玻璃。

branches.en: THE BODY AS NETWORK: animals run the same circuit with scent and dance instead of wire.
branches.cn: 身体即网络：动物用气味与舞蹈代替线路，跑着同一条回路。

branches.en: SOCIETY AND ORGANISATION: a population and a staff each need routes for news and orders.
branches.cn: 社会与组织：一个全体人口与一个工作班子，都需要消息与命令的路线。

branches.en: PROTOCOL AND POCKET: compatibility between machines, then the few tools one person carries.
branches.cn: 协议与口袋：机器之间的兼容，然后再缩小到一个人随身带的几件工具。

branches.en: THE THEORIST'S BOXES: people and wires drop out, leaving sender, channel and receiver.
branches.cn: 理论家的方框：人与线路退场，只剩发送者、通道与接收者。

intro.en: The phrase is built from two borrowings whose parts still recur in English: a Latin root for 'common' and a Greek root for 'standing together'.
intro.cn: 这个词组由两个借词构成，它们的构件在英语中仍然反复出现：一个拉丁词根表示「共同」，一个希腊词根表示「站在一起」。

latinIntro.en: Latin communis and communicare supply the first half; Greek systema, borrowed into Late Latin, supplies the second. The two families never merged in Latin, so the English phrase is a modern assembly.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 communis 与 communicare 提供前半部分；借入晚期拉丁语的希腊 systema 提供后半部分。这两个词族在拉丁语中从未合并，因此英语这个词组是现代的拼装。

items.meaning: to share information, thoughts or feelings
items.meaningCN: 交流；传达（信息、想法或感受）
items.example: They communicate by radio every morning.
items.exampleCN: 他们每天早上用无线电联络。

items.meaning: the process or content of exchanging messages
items.meaningCN: 交流；通信（交换消息的过程或内容）
items.exampleCN: 清晰的沟通能避免大多数延误。

items.example: She is unusually communicative about her work.

definition_en: the legal status of being a member of a state, together with its rights and duties, or the practice of taking part responsibly in a community

sceneCN: 入籍仪式的大厅里，一排人举右手跟着念誓词，桌上摊开一本深色封面的小册；句中这个词指「依法取得的国家成员身份」（第 1 个义项：个人与国家之间的法定成员关系，附带权利与义务）。句意为她在这个国家住满十年后，终于宣誓取得公民身份。可辨识物件：誓词卡、举起的右手、深色小册、桌上的旗。

senses.title: Legal membership of a state
senses.titleCN: 依法属于某个国家的成员身份
senses.definition: the legal status of belonging to a country, which brings a passport, protection and a permanent right to return
senses.definitionCN: 依法属于某个国家的身份，附带护照、领事保护与永久回国权
senses.example: After ten years in the country, she finally took the oath of citizenship.
senses.exampleCN: 她在这个国家住满十年后，终于宣誓取得公民身份。
senses.why: The native suffix -ship turns a person-word into a state-word, exactly as friend becomes friendship, so citizenship is the condition of being a citizen.
senses.whyCN: 本族后缀 -ship 把「人」变成「状态」，正如 friend 变 friendship，因此这个词就是「作为公民的状态」。

senses.title: The rights and duties that come with it
senses.titleCN: 随身份而来的权利与义务
senses.definition: the whole bundle of voting, taxation, obedience to law and claim on public services attached to membership
senses.definitionCN: 与成员身份相连的一整套权利与义务：投票、纳税、守法以及享有公共服务
senses.example: Citizenship brings the duty to pay tax as well as the right to vote.
senses.exampleCN: 公民身份既带来投票权，也带来纳税的义务。
senses.why: A status is not a badge but a two-sided contract, and English uses the same noun for both sides of it.
senses.whyCN: 这种身份不是一枚徽章，而是一份双面契约，英语用同一个名词同时指这两面。

senses.title: Taking part in public life
senses.definition: the practice of joining public decisions and shared work rather than only holding the paper
senses.definitionCN: 参与公共决策与共同事务的实际行动，而不只是持有一纸身份
senses.example: For her, citizenship meant showing up at council meetings, not just carrying a passport.
senses.exampleCN: 对她来说，公民身份意味着出席市政会议，而不只是带着一本护照。
senses.why: The noun was stretched from the legal tie to the activity that keeps the tie alive, because a right that nobody uses slowly disappears.
senses.whyCN: 这个词从法律纽带扩展到维持纽带的行动，因为无人行使的权利会慢慢消失。

senses.title: Good conduct as a member
senses.definition: the quality of behaving responsibly toward neighbours and shared places
senses.definitionCN: 对邻里与公共空间负责任地行事的品质
senses.example: The school praised his citizenship after he organised a clean-up of the riverbank.
senses.exampleCN: 他组织了一次河岸清理，学校称赞了他的公民品德。
senses.why: -ship names a quality as well as a status, so the word can mean the virtue of a good member and not only the fact of membership.
senses.whyCN: -ship 既能指状态，也能指品质，因此这个词可指好成员的德行，而不只是成员这一事实。

senses.title: The school subject
senses.definition: a school subject that teaches how laws, elections and public services work
senses.definitionCN: 一门讲解法律、选举与公共服务如何运作的学校课程
senses.example: Citizenship is taught in year nine alongside history and geography.
senses.exampleCN: 九年级与历史、地理并行开设公民课。
senses.why: Modern curricula turned an abstract idea into a named subject, and the subject kept the plain noun rather than inventing a new one.
senses.whyCN: 现代课程把一个抽象理念变成有名目的科目，而这个科目沿用了朴素的原名词，没有另造新词。

senses.title: Corporate citizenship
senses.definition: the idea that a company owes duties to the society it operates in
senses.definitionCN: 认为企业对其所在社会负有责任的主张
senses.example: The bank advertises its corporate citizenship in every annual report.
senses.exampleCN: 这家银行在每份年报里宣传自己的企业公民责任。
senses.why: The metaphor treats a company as a member with duties, which lets moral language be applied to a firm.
senses.whyCN: 这个比喻把公司当作负有责任的成员，从而把道德语言用到企业身上。

senses.title: Global citizenship
senses.definition: a sense of belonging to humanity as a whole rather than to one state
senses.definitionCN: 认为自己属于全人类而非某一国家的归属感
senses.example: Climate campaigns appeal to global citizenship rather than to national loyalty.
senses.exampleCN: 气候运动诉诸世界公民意识，而不是国家忠诚。
senses.why: The same membership idea is stretched to a borderless community, and the stretch is marked by the adjective global.
senses.whyCN: 同一个成员身份观念被拉伸到一个没有国界的共同体，global 这个形容词标出了这一拉伸。

senses.title: Belonging to a town
senses.definition: membership in a town or neighbourhood, shown by daily involvement rather than by papers
senses.definitionCN: 对城镇或街区的成员感，靠日常参与而非证件来体现
senses.example: Her citizenship of the old quarter was a matter of daily errands, not papers.
senses.exampleCN: 她对老城区的归属感体现在每天的琐事里，而不是证件上。
senses.why: The oldest layer of the word is the city: Latin civitas named the body of townspeople before it named a state.
senses.whyCN: 这个词最古老的一层是「城市」：拉丁语 civitas 先指城镇居民全体，后来才指国家。

intro.en: Citizenship is citizen plus the native suffix -ship, which turns a person into a state or a quality. Citizen itself reaches English through Old French from Latin civitas 'the body of citizens', built on civis 'citizen'. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: citizenship 由 citizen 加本族后缀 -ship 构成，这个后缀把「人」变成「状态」或「品质」。citizen 本身经古法语来自拉丁 civitas「公民全体」，其词根为 civis「公民」。年代均为约数。

items.en: Civis meant 'citizen, townsman'. Its deeper origin is not established; the link sometimes proposed to a root meaning 'to settle' remains a hypothesis, not a demonstrated derivation.
items.cn: civis 意为「公民、城里人」。其更深来源未得到证明；有人提出的与「定居」词根的联系仍属假说，并非已证实的派生。

items.en: Civitas first named the condition of being a citizen, then the whole body of citizens and their commonwealth; the abstract and the collective readings existed side by side.
items.cn: civitas 先指「身为公民的状态」，再指「公民全体及其共同体」；抽象义与集合义长期并存。

items.en: Old French cité came from civitas but narrowed to 'city, town', losing the political sense. English city follows this line, which is why city and citizen look alike but name different things.
items.cn: 古法语 cité 出自 civitas，却收窄为「城市、城镇」，丢掉了政治含义。英语 city 沿这条线发展，所以 city 与 citizen 形近却指不同事物。

items.en: The person-word entered English around 1300 as citisein, 'inhabitant of a city'. The older English word for a townsman was burgess, and citizen gradually replaced it.
items.cn: 指人的这个词约在 1300 年以 citisein 进入英语，意为「城市居民」。英语里更早表示市民的词是 burgess，citizen 逐渐取代了它。

items.en: The native suffix -ship, historically related to shape, first named a condition or an office, as in friendship and lordship. From the sixteenth century it formed citizenship, 'the state of being a citizen'.
items.cn: 本族后缀 -ship 在历史上与 shape 相关，先表示「状态」或「职位」，如 friendship 与 lordship。到十六世纪构成 citizenship，即「身为公民的状态」。

items.en: From the nineteenth century the word also named school instruction and good conduct; the corporate and global uses are twentieth-century extensions. Source uncertain (first date): no exact first citation is recorded for either extension.
items.cn: 从十九世纪起，这个词也指学校课程与端正品行；企业义与世界公民义是二十世纪的扩展。首见年代不确定：这两种扩展都没有确切的最早书证。

note.en: Group one holds words built on the same Latin civis stock, easy to confuse at sight; group two holds near neighbours that also name a tie between a person and a state or place.
note.cn: 第一组是同出拉丁 civis 词族、容易看错的词；第二组是同样表示「人与国家或地方的联系」的近义词。

entries.definition: The countable person-word: one who holds the status. Citizenship is the status itself and cannot be counted the same way.
entries.definitionCN: 可数的「人」：持有该身份的个人。citizenship 是身份本身，不能同样计数。

entries.definition: A large town. It comes from the same Latin source but through a branch that narrowed to the place, so it never means a person.
entries.definitionCN: 指大城市。同出拉丁来源，但走的是收窄为「地方」的那条支线，因此从不指人。

entries.definition: The adjective for things belonging to a town or to citizens' duties. It describes the field, while citizenship names the status.
entries.definitionCN: 指「属于城镇或公民义务」的形容词，描述领域，而 citizenship 指身份本身。

entries.definition: A society and its culture at a developed stage. The ending -ization names a process, not a membership, and the word is not a synonym.
entries.definitionCN: 指发展到较高阶段的社会及其文化。-ization 结尾表示过程，而非成员身份，二者并非同义。

entries.definition: The legal tie to a state, often used when passports and immigration are discussed; it stresses the state's side, while citizenship stresses the member's rights and duties.
entries.definitionCN: 与国家之间的法律纽带，常用于护照与移民语境；它强调国家一侧，而 citizenship 强调成员的权利与义务。

entries.definition: The right to live in a country without full political membership; a resident may pay tax and still be unable to vote.
entries.definitionCN: 在一国居住的权利，但不含完整政治成员身份；居民可能纳税却无法投票。

entries.definition: The condition of being a subject of a crown rather than a citizen of a republic; the duties run upward to a ruler.
entries.definitionCN: 指身为君主臣民而非共和国公民的状态；义务朝上指向统治者。

entries.definition: The official process by which a foreigner acquires citizenship; it names the step, not the resulting status.
entries.definitionCN: 外国人取得公民身份的官方程序；它指这一步过程，而非取得后的身份。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: a real native suffix, a real Latin root and real fixed phrases.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的本族后缀、真实的拉丁词根与真实的固定搭配。

normal.en: -ship turns a person into a condition: citizen gives citizenship, friend gives friendship.
normal.cn: -ship 把「人」变成「状态」：citizen 得 citizenship，friend 得 friendship。

normal.en: The family runs citizen, citizenship, city, civic, civil and civilian.
normal.cn: 同族词包括 citizen、citizenship、city、civic、civil 与 civilian。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark the legal field: grant citizenship, dual citizenship, citizenship ceremony.
normal.cn: 固定搭配标出法律领域：授予公民身份、双重国籍、入籍仪式。

normal.en: Latin civis also lies inside civitas, the source of both city and citizen.
normal.cn: 拉丁 civis 也在 civitas 之中，而 civitas 同时是 city 与 citizen 的来源。

normal.en: The word always pairs a right with a duty: the vote and the tax return.
normal.cn: 这个词总把权利与义务配成一对：选票与报税单。

abstract.en: Picture a key that opens a town hall but carries a list of chores on the same ring.
abstract.cn: 想象一把能打开市政厅的钥匙，钥匙圈上同时挂着一串必须完成的杂事。

abstract.en: Picture a membership card that grows warmer the more often it is used.
abstract.cn: 想象一张会员卡，用得越频繁，摸起来越温热。

abstract.en: Picture a passport that is also a rota, saying when you must show up.
abstract.cn: 想象一本护照同时是一张值班表，写明你何时必须到场。

examples.en: Dual citizenship forced him to choose which passport to renew.
examples.cn: 双重国籍逼他选择续办哪一本护照。

examples.en: The council treats clean streets as a test of citizenship.
examples.cn: 市政会把街道整洁当作公民意识的一种检验。

examples.en: Citizenship classes cover voting, taxation and local services.
examples.cn: 公民课涵盖投票、纳税与地方公共服务。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「公民」加「船」：同坐一条船的人，才有身份、权利与义务——注意这只是谐音联想，并非词源

root: 拉丁 civis「公民」→ civitas「公民身份、公民全体」→ 古法语 cité「城市」→ 中古英语 citisein「市民」；英语 citizen 加本族后缀 -ship（状态、身份）构成 citizenship。civis 的更深来源不确定。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses move from a paper to a practice: the legal status first, then the two sides of its contract, then participation, conduct, the school subject, the company, the planet and finally the old town.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项从一纸身份走向实际践行：先讲法定身份，再讲契约的两面，然后依次是参与、品行、学校科目、企业、全球，最后回到古老的城镇。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a folded booklet that names one person as a member of a body, with rights printed on one page and duties on the other.
core.cn: 核心意象：一本折起的小册子把一个人写进某个共同体，一页印权利，另一页印义务。

branches.en: The booklet is the legal tie, and the tie runs both ways: a passport on one page, a tax form on the other.
branches.cn: 小册子是法律纽带，而纽带走双向：一页是护照，另一页是报税表。

branches.en: Belonging is practised where one lives: council meetings in the present, the old quarter in the past.
branches.cn: 归属在日常所在地被实践：当下的市政会议，以及过去的老城区。

branches.en: Conduct becomes teachable: the virtue of a good member is turned into a school subject with a syllabus.
branches.cn: 品行变成可教之物：好成员的德行被整理成有教学大纲的一门课。

branches.en: The metaphor makes a firm a member, so that moral duties can be asked of a company.
branches.cn: 比喻把企业当作成员，于是可以向公司追问道德责任。

branches.en: The border of the body is removed, leaving humanity as the only remaining community.
branches.cn: 共同体的边界被撤掉，只剩全人类作为唯一剩下的社群。

intro.en: Citizenship is a native suffix laid on a borrowed noun, so the word can be read as one person-noun plus one state-suffix.
intro.cn: citizenship 是把本族后缀加在借来的名词上，因此可按「一个指人的名词＋一个表状态的后缀」来读。

latinIntro.en: Latin supplies the noun civis and its abstract civitas, but has no suffix matching -ship; the state-suffix is native English and historically related to shape.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语提供名词 civis 及其抽象形式 civitas，但没有与 -ship 对应的后缀；这个表状态的后缀是本族英语成分，历史上与 shape 相关。

items.example: Civis is the root that carries the idea of membership.
items.exampleCN: 这个词根承载「成员身份」的观念。

items.example: Civitas adds the abstract ending to civis.
