items.example: The place branch narrowed away from the political sense.
items.exampleCN: 指地方的这条支线从政治含义中收窄出来。

items.example: The suffix makes a status out of a person-noun.
items.exampleCN: 这个后缀把指人的名词变成一种身份。

items.meaning: a member of a city or state
items.exampleCN: 这个指人的词约在 1300 年进入英语。

items.meaning: the status or virtue of a citizen
items.example: The suffix adds the abstract reading to the person-word.
items.exampleCN: 后缀为指人的词添上抽象含义。

items.meaning: belonging to a town or its citizens
items.example: The adjective describes the field rather than the person.
items.exampleCN: 这个形容词描述领域，而非指人。

items.meaning: a person not in the armed forces
items.example: The word contrasts the private person with the uniformed state.
items.exampleCN: 这个词把私人身份的平民与穿制服的公权力对立起来。

items.meaning: the citizens taken as a group

items.exampleCN: 集合后缀把许多持有该身份的人聚为一体。

definition_zh: 生物多样性；生物多样性水平
definition_en: the variety of living organisms and the ecological systems they form, measured at genetic, species, and ecosystem levels
core_image: 同一片森林里，每一层都长着不同的生命
scene: 这座岛与大陆隔开千万年，物种因此自成一套。 The island's isolation has produced remarkable biodiversity, with species found nowhere else on Earth.
sceneCN: 这里 biodiversity 是「生物多样性」（第 1 个义项：一个地区的物种多样性）；句意：这座岛屿的与世隔绝造就了非凡的生物多样性，有些物种在地球上别处都找不到。场景要点：海岛、多层的热带植被、不同种类的鸟与昆虫、记录表、望远镜。

pos.zh: 生物多样性；生物多样性水平

collocations.zh: 生物多样性补偿（生态补偿机制）

senses.title: Species diversity in a place
senses.titleCN: 物种多样性：一个地区有多少种生物
senses.definition: the variety and number of species living in a given area
senses.definitionCN: 某一地区内物种的多样程度和数量
senses.example: The island's isolation has produced remarkable biodiversity.
senses.exampleCN: 这座岛屿的与世隔绝造就了非凡的生物多样性。
senses.why: bio- supplies 'life' and diversity supplies 'turned different ways'. The first sense counts how many kinds of living thing share a place: difference among organisms is the core of the word, and species are the easiest differences to see.
senses.whyCN: bio- 提供“生命”，diversity 提供“转向各方”。第一个义项数的是一个地方共享着多少种生物：生物之间的差异是这个词的核心，而物种是最容易看见的差异。

senses.title: Genetic diversity within a species
senses.titleCN: 遗传多样性：同一物种内部的基因差异
senses.definition: the variation in genes among individuals of the same species
senses.definitionCN: 同一物种个体之间的基因差异
senses.example: Small populations lose biodiversity at the genetic level even before species disappear.
senses.exampleCN: 小种群在物种消失之前，就已经在遗传层面失去生物多样性。
senses.why: The 1992 Convention on Biological Diversity defined the term at three levels, and the first extension went inward: variety does not stop between species, it continues among individuals and their genes. A species is itself a pool of differences.
senses.whyCN: 1992 年《生物多样性公约》把该词定义为三个层次，第一次延伸是向内走：多样性并不止于物种之间，它继续存在于个体及其基因之间。一个物种本身就是一池差异。

senses.title: Ecosystem and habitat diversity
senses.titleCN: 生态系统与生境多样性
senses.definition: the variety of ecosystems, habitats, and ecological communities in a region
senses.definitionCN: 一个地区内生态系统、生境与生态群落的多样程度
senses.example: Wetlands, forest and coral reef add ecosystem biodiversity to the same region.
senses.exampleCN: 湿地、森林与珊瑚礁为同一地区增加了生态系统多样性。
senses.why: The third level steps outward: not the organisms but the kinds of place and the communities they form. Difference now applies to habitats, so the same word covers a forest, a marsh and a reef.
senses.whyCN: 第三个层次向外走：不是生物本身，而是地方的类型以及它们形成的群落。差异这时适用于生境，于是同一个词覆盖森林、沼泽与珊瑚礁。

senses.title: The measured level: high or low
senses.titleCN: 多样性水平：可高可低的量
senses.definition: the measured degree of variety in a place, which can be high, low, or declining
senses.definitionCN: 一个地方多样性的可测程度，可高、可低或正在下降
senses.example: The survey recorded low biodiversity in the polluted stretch of the river.
senses.exampleCN: 调查记录到河流受污染河段的生物多样性很低。
senses.why: Once a quantity can be counted, it can be compared. Diversity stops being a bare fact and becomes a scale — high, low, rich, poor — which is what field surveys actually report.
senses.whyCN: 一旦可以计数，就可以比较。多样性不再是单纯的事实，而变成一把刻度——高、低、丰富、贫乏——这正是野外调查实际报告的内容。

senses.title: Loss of biodiversity
senses.definition: the decline or disappearance of biological variety, usually through human pressure
senses.definitionCN: 生物多样性程度的下降或消失，通常由人类压力造成
senses.example: Habitat clearance is the leading cause of biodiversity loss worldwide.
senses.exampleCN: 栖息地清除是世界范围内生物多样性丧失的首要原因。
senses.why: A scale that can fall invites the noun 'loss'. The word now names a public problem, not only a property of a place; conservation supplies the negative frame, and loss becomes the standard collocation.
senses.whyCN: 一个会下跌的刻度自然引出“丧失”这个名词。这个词现在命名的是一种公共问题，而不只是某地的属性；保护话语提供了负面框架，loss 于是成为标准搭配。

senses.title: Conservation hotspot
senses.titleCN: 保护热点：多样性极高又受威胁的地区
senses.definition: a region with exceptionally high biodiversity that is under serious threat
senses.definitionCN: 生物多样性异常高、同时面临严重威胁的地区
senses.example: The mountain range is recognised as a global biodiversity hotspot.
senses.exampleCN: 这条山脉被认定为全球生物多样性热点地区。
senses.why: Where diversity is high and threatened, attention concentrates. Hotspot is the spatial form of that concentration: a place worth naming, mapping and funding, so the word becomes an argument for protection.
senses.whyCN: 在多样性高又受威胁的地方，注意力会集中。hotspot 就是这种集中的空间形态：一个值得命名、绘图和投入资金的地方，于是这个词本身成了一种保护理由。

senses.title: Agricultural biodiversity
senses.titleCN: 农业生物多样性：作物与家畜品种的多样
senses.definition: the variety of crops, livestock breeds, and associated organisms used in farming
senses.definitionCN: 农业中使用的作物、家畜品种及相关生物的多样性
senses.example: Traditional farms preserve agricultural biodiversity that monocultures lose.
senses.exampleCN: 传统农场保存着单一种植所丧失的农业生物多样性。
senses.why: Humans select plants and animals, so variety also exists among breeds and crop varieties. The compound widens 'life' from wild organisms to cultivated ones, and the word becomes a measure of food-system resilience.
senses.whyCN: 人类对动植物进行选择，所以品种与作物之间也存在多样性。这个复合词把“生命”从野生生物扩展到栽培生物，于是该词成为衡量食物系统韧性的一项指标。

senses.title: Biodiversity as a global commons
senses.titleCN: 作为全球公共资源的生物多样性
senses.definition: biodiversity treated as a shared resource and a subject of international law and policy
senses.definitionCN: 被当作共享资源、并成为国际法与政策对象的生物多样性
senses.example: The treaty treats biodiversity as a common concern of humankind.
senses.exampleCN: 该条约把生物多样性视为人类的共同关切。
senses.why: Because genes, species and habitats cross borders, the noun was lifted from ecology into international law. The 1992 Convention made it the name of a shared resource, and the word acquired a political subject as well as an ecological one.
senses.whyCN: 由于基因、物种与生境都跨越国界，这个名词从生态学被提升到国际法。1992 年公约使它成为一种共享资源的名称，这个词于是既有生态学主体，也有政治主体。

senses.title: Diversity in managed or urban land
senses.titleCN: 城市与人工生境中的生物多样性
senses.definition: biological variety measured in cities, restored land, and other human-managed landscapes
senses.definitionCN: 在城市、修复地及其他人类管理景观中测得的生物多样性
senses.example: Green roofs and city parks can raise urban biodiversity.
senses.exampleCN: 绿色屋顶与城市公园可以提升城市生物多样性。
senses.why: The last extension drops the wilderness assumption: diversity is measured wherever life persists, including cities and restored land. The word becomes a planning target rather than a description of untouched nature.
senses.whyCN: 最后一次延伸丢掉了“荒野”预设：凡有生命存续之处都可测多样性，包括城市与修复地。这个词于是从“未受触及的自然之描述”变成一项规划目标。

intro.en: Biodiversity is not an inherited word. It is a 20th-century scientific compound, clipped from the phrase biological diversity: bio- is Greek, diversity is Latin, and the two were joined in modern English. The earliest written record is disputed.
intro.cn: biodiversity 不是承袭来的词，而是 20 世纪的科学复合词，由短语 biological diversity 截短而成：bio- 是希腊语，diversity 是拉丁语，两者在现代英语里被拼在一起。最早的书面记录存疑。

items.en: bios means 'one's life, course or way of living, lifetime', as opposed to zoē 'animal life'. It comes from PIE *gwei- 'to live'. In English bio- has been used in scientific compounds since about 1800 for 'organic life', though biography keeps the older 'life-story' sense.
items.cn: bios 意为“一个人的生命、生活历程、寿命”，与 zoē“动物生命”相对，来自原始印欧语 *gwei-“活”。英语自约 1800 年起用 bio- 构成科学复合词，表示“有机生命”，但 biography 仍保留更古老的“生平故事”义。

items.en: divertere 'to turn apart' is dis- 'apart' + vertere 'to turn'. Its past participle diversus means 'turned different ways', and diversitas gives 'difference, variety'. English diversity (mid-14c) came through Old French diversete.
items.cn: divertere“转开”是 dis-“分开”+ vertere“转”。其过去分词 diversus 意为“转向各方的”，名词 diversitas 表示“差异、多样”。英语 diversity（14 世纪中）经由古法语 diversete 而来。

items.en: The full phrase was used in ecology and conservation from the 1970s–80s for variety at genetic, species and ecosystem levels. It is a descriptive phrase built from existing words, not a classical term with an ancient pedigree.
items.cn: 完整短语 biological diversity 在 20 世纪 70—80 年代的生态学与保护生物学中用来指基因、物种、生态系统三个层次的多样性。它是由现有词构成的描述性短语，不是有古老传承的经典术语。

items.en: Etymonline dates biodiversity 'by 1988'. The clipped form is often credited to W. G. Rosen in conference material around 1985–86, later printed in 1988; the exact first written use and the first coiner are disputed, and sources differ. Treat the date as approximate.
items.cn: Etymonline 把 biodiversity 记作“by 1988”。这个截短形式常被归到 W. G. Rosen 在 1985—86 年前后的会议材料，后来于 1988 年付印；最早的书面使用与首创者都有争议，各家资料不一。年代只能作大致估计。

items.era: WHY IT IS NOT AN OLD WORD
items.en: There is no Latin biodiversitas and no Greek compound of this shape. The word was built from a living prefix and a living noun to fill a gap in ecology, so its structure stays transparent in a way inherited words are not.
items.cn: 并不存在拉丁语 biodiversitas，也没有这种形状的希腊语复合词。这个词是用活的前缀加活的名词造出来填补生态学的空缺，因此它的结构保持着承袭词所没有的透明性。

items.en: The 1992 Convention on Biological Diversity fixed the three-level definition and turned the word into a legal and policy term. Later compounds — hotspot, offset, agrobiodiversity — extend it outward from ecology into planning, finance and agriculture.
items.cn: 1992 年《生物多样性公约》确定了三层定义，把这个词变成法律与政策术语。后来的复合词——hotspot、offset、agrobiodiversity——又把它从生态学向外扩展到规划、金融与农业。

note.en: The first group contains the words and phrases most often mistaken for biodiversity itself; the second contains measures of living variety that differ in what they actually count.
note.cn: 第一组是最容易被误当成 biodiversity 本身的词与短语；第二组是衡量生命多样性的指标，但各自实际计数的对象不同。

entries.definition: Variety or difference in general. It can describe people, ideas, or tastes; only the bio- prefix makes it about living organisms.
entries.definitionCN: 泛指多样或差异，可指人、想法、口味；只有加上 bio- 才专指生物。

entries.definition: The longer, formal phrase from which biodiversity was clipped. It is the safer term in legal and scientific writing and covers the same three levels.
entries.definitionCN: biodiversity 由之截短而来的较长正式短语。在法律与科学写作中更稳妥，涵盖同样的三个层次。

entries.definition: The total mass of living matter. It shares bio- but measures amount, while biodiversity measures difference.
entries.definitionCN: 活物质的总质量。它共享 bio-，但衡量的是数量，而 biodiversity 衡量的是差异。

entries.definition: A written life of a person, from bio- + graphein 'to write'. It looks like a bio- word but has nothing to do with ecology.
entries.definitionCN: 人物传记，来自 bio- + graphein“书写”。它看起来像 bio- 词，却与生态学无关。

entries.definition: The quality of differing in form or type. Everyday and unmeasured, with no ecological definition behind it.
entries.definitionCN: 形式或类型上存在差异的性质。日常用语，不可量化，背后没有生态学定义。

entries.definition: The number of species in a place. It counts only species, whereas biodiversity also includes genetic and ecosystem variety.
entries.definitionCN: 一个地方的物种数目。它只数物种，而 biodiversity 还包括遗传与生态系统层面的多样。

entries.definition: The number of individuals of a species. More individuals is not more diversity; a field of one crop can have high abundance and low biodiversity.
entries.definitionCN: 某一物种的个体数量。个体多并不等于多样性高；一块单一种植的田可以个体数量很高而生物多样性很低。

entries.definition: Unevenness in composition or structure across space. It is a measurement of pattern, not the variety of life itself.
entries.definitionCN: 组成或结构在空间上的不均匀。它是格局的度量，而不是生命本身的多样。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: the real Greek prefix, the real Latin noun, and the real three-level definition.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的希腊前缀、真实的拉丁名词，以及真实的三层定义。

normal.en: bio- 'life' + diversity 'turned apart': life turned into many different forms.
normal.cn: bio-“生命”+ diversity“转向各方”：生命被分成许多不同的形态。

normal.en: Three levels: genes → species → ecosystems. The word covers all three, and most exam questions test only the first.
normal.cn: 三个层次：基因 → 物种 → 生态系统。这个词覆盖三层，而多数考题只考第一层。

normal.en: Contrast pair: biomass measures amount, biodiversity measures variety. The second half of each word tells you what is measured.
normal.cn: 对比记忆：biomass 量的是数量，biodiversity 量的是多样。两个词的后半部分告诉你衡量的对象。

normal.en: bio- means 'life story' in biography and 'life science' in biology; biodiversity belongs to the science side.
normal.cn: bio- 在 biography 里是“生平故事”，在 biology 里是“生命科学”；biodiversity 属于科学这一侧。

normal.en: The word usually travels with loss, hotspot and conservation, because it names something that can be measured, threatened and protected.
normal.cn: 这个词常与 loss、hotspot、conservation 同行，因为它命名的东西可以被测量、被威胁、被保护。

abstract.en: Picture a shelf with many different books; abundance would be many copies of one book, diversity is many different titles.
abstract.cn: 想象一个书架摆着许多不同的书；abundance 是同一本书有很多本，diversity 是有很多不同的书名。

abstract.en: Picture a forest where canopy, understory and soil each hold a different community of life.
abstract.cn: 想象一片森林，树冠层、林下层与土壤各自住着不同的生命群落。

abstract.en: Picture three nested circles: genes inside species, species inside ecosystems. Biodiversity is the whole set of circles, not just the middle one.
abstract.cn: 想象三个同心圆：基因在物种之内，物种在生态系统之内。biodiversity 是整套圆，而不只是中间那一圈。

examples.en: The rainforest supports biodiversity that no plantation can replace.
examples.cn: 雨林所支撑的生物多样性是任何单一林场都无法替代的。

examples.en: Scientists measure biodiversity at the genetic, species and ecosystem levels.
examples.cn: 科学家在遗传、物种和生态系统三个层次上测量生物多样性。

examples.en: The report links biodiversity loss to the draining of local wetlands.
examples.cn: 报告把生物多样性丧失与当地湿地被排干联系起来。

dict_mnemonic.text: 拜（bio）生命所赐，大（dai）家各有伟（ver）色，提（ti）供多样 → biodiversity 生物多样性

root: 希腊 bios“生命”+ 拉丁 diversus“转向各方”构成的 diversity“多样性”；20 世纪仿 biological diversity 截短而成的新造复合词。

sensesIntro.en: Nine senses share one core: difference among living things. The word then widens inward to genes, outward to ecosystems, sideways to measurement and loss, and finally into law and city planning.
sensesIntro.cn: 九个义项共享同一个核心：生物之间的差异。这个词随后向内扩展到基因，向外扩展到生态系统，再横向扩展到测量与丧失，最后进入法律与城市规划。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: life turned into many different forms in one place.
core.cn: 核心意象：同一片土地上的生命分成许多不同的形态。

branches.en: LEVELS OF VARIETY: species differ from one another, and individuals differ genetically inside a species.
branches.cn: 多样的层次：物种之间彼此不同，个体在同一物种内部也有基因差异。

branches.en: PLACES AND CULTIVATION: habitats differ from one another, and farming adds human-selected varieties.
branches.cn: 生境与栽培：生境彼此不同，农业又加入人类选育的品种。

branches.en: MEASUREMENT AND DECLINE: variety becomes a scale with high and low values, and a falling scale becomes loss.
branches.cn: 测量与下降：多样性变成有高低值的刻度，而刻度下跌就成了丧失。

branches.en: PROTECTION AND LAW: threatened richness concentrates attention, and cross-border variety becomes a global commons.
branches.cn: 保护与法律：受威胁的丰富度集中注意力，跨国界的多样性成为全球公共资源。

branches.en: BEYOND WILDNESS: managed and urban land also count, so the word becomes a planning target.
branches.cn: 超越荒野：人工管理与城市土地也计入，于是这个词成为规划目标。

intro.en: Biodiversity is a transparent modern compound: bio- + diversity. Both parts are free-standing or semi-free in English, which is why the word feels self-explaining even to a reader who knows no Latin or Greek.
intro.cn: biodiversity 是一个透明的现代复合词：bio- + diversity。两部分在英语中都能独立或半独立使用，所以即使不懂拉丁语或希腊语，读者也觉得它自我解释。

latinIntro.en: There is no single Latin word behind biodiversity. The prefix is Greek bios; the noun is Latin diversitas, from diversus, past participle of divertere. The compound itself is modern, so its 'etymology' is a join, not an inheritance.
latinIntro.cn: biodiversity 背后没有单个拉丁词。前缀是希腊语 bios；名词是拉丁语 diversitas，出自 divertere 的过去分词 diversus。复合词本身是现代造物，所以它的“词源”是一次拼接，而不是承袭。

items.meaning: the science of life and living things
items.example: She studied biology before turning to ecology.
items.exampleCN: 她在转向生态学之前学的是生物学。

items.meaning: the variety of life at several levels
items.meaningCN: 生物多样性（bio-“生命”+ diversity“多样”）
items.example: The survey mapped biodiversity across the valley.
items.exampleCN: 这项调查绘制了山谷各处的生物多样性。

items.meaning: having a high variety of living things
items.meaningCN: 生物多样的；生物种类丰富的
items.example: The delta is one of the most biodiverse regions in Asia.
items.exampleCN: 这片三角洲是亚洲生物多样性最丰富的地区之一。

items.meaning: the diversity of crops and livestock
items.meaningCN: 农业生物多样性（agro-“农田”+ biodiversity）
items.exampleCN: 种子库保护农业生物多样性。

items.meaning: a place of intense activity or concentration
items.meaningCN: 热点（活动或集中程度极高的地点）
items.example: The region is a biodiversity hotspot.
items.exampleCN: 该地区是一个生物多样性热点。

items.meaning: the zone of life on Earth
a large ecological community shaped by climate
items.exampleCN: 苔原是寒冷的生物群系。

items.meaningCN: 多样性；差异（-ity 构成状态名词）
items.example: The region is known for its cultural diversity.
items.exampleCN: 该地区以文化多样性著称。

items.meaning: to make or become more varied
items.meaningCN: 使多样化；分散（-ify 表示“使……化”）

items.meaning: compensation for damage to habitats, usually by restoring or protecting an equivalent area
items.meaningCN: 生物多样性补偿：通过修复或保护等面积生境来弥补损害
items.example: The company funded a biodiversity offset near the mine.
items.exampleCN: 公司出资在矿区附近实施生物多样性补偿。

latinEntries.meaningCN: 转向各方的；各种各样的

definition_zh: 敏锐的；精明的；狡黠的
definition_en: clever and quick at seeing how to gain an advantage or understand a situation
core_image: 棋手在对手落子前已看穿整条路
scene: 会议室里众人还在翻资料，他已从一句话的措辞里看穿了对方的底价。 Her astute reading of the offer saved the company millions.
sceneCN: 这里 astute 是「敏锐的、精明的」（第 1 个义项：洞察局势并善用之）；句意为她对报价的敏锐解读为公司省下数百万。

pos.zh: 敏锐的；洞察力强的
精明的；善谋利的

senses.title: Quick to see and understand
senses.definition: able to notice details and grasp situations quickly and accurately
senses.definitionCN: 能迅速而准确地察觉细节、把握局势
senses.example: The astute critic spotted the flaw at once.
senses.exampleCN: 敏锐的评论家一眼看出破绽。
senses.why: From Latin astus, cleverness or craft; the mind moves like a skilled hand.
senses.whyCN: 源自拉丁语 astus（机巧）；头脑如巧手般灵活穿行。

senses.title: Clever in gaining advantage
senses.definition: shrewd in turning insight to practical benefit
senses.definitionCN: 善于把洞察化为实际利益
senses.example: An astute bargain doubled his holdings.
senses.exampleCN: 一笔精明的交易使他的资产翻倍。
senses.why: Craft is cunning applied; astuteness shades into shrewd self-interest.
senses.whyCN: 机巧运用于谋利便是狡黠；astute 因此带有精于算计的色彩。

intro.en: Astute comes from Latin astutus, shrewd, from astus, craft or cunning, of uncertain older origin.
intro.cn: astute 源自拉丁语 astutus（精明的），出自 astus（机巧、狡黠），更早来源不确定。

items.en: Astus meant craft, cunning, clever maneuver.
items.cn: 拉丁语 astus 意为机巧、狡黠的运作。

items.en: Astutus described a cunning, crafty mind.
items.cn: astutus 形容机敏狡黠的心智。

items.en: The word stayed alive in scholarly Latin.
items.cn: 该词在学术拉丁语中沿用。

items.en: English adopted astute in the seventeenth century, first often with a sly shade.
items.cn: 十七世纪英语借入 astute，早期常带狡黠意味。

items.en: It is now usually praise for sharp judgment.
items.cn: 如今它多为对敏锐判断的褒扬。

note.en: Astute pairs sharp eyes with sharp dealing: see it, then use it.
note.cn: astute 兼具慧眼与手腕：先看穿，再利用。

abstract.cn: 想象棋王在对方落子前已读盘全局。

abstract.en: See a trader pausing one second before signing.

examples.en: She remained astute even under pressure.
examples.cn: 即便重压之下她依然敏锐。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「额识途」——额是识途老马，一眼看穿全局，正是 astute 的精明。

root: 拉丁语 astus（机巧、狡黠，来源不确定）→ astutus（精明的）→ 英语 astute（敏锐的；精明的）。

sensesIntro.en: Craft of mind becomes both penetrating insight and sharp dealing.
sensesIntro.cn: 心智的机巧既化作穿透性的洞察，也化作精明的算计。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: eyes reading the whole board in one glance
core.cn: 核心意象：一眼读穿全局的目光

branches.en: penetrating observation
branches.cn: 穿透性的观察

branches.en: turning insight to gain
branches.cn: 把洞察化为利益

branches.en: the astus craft at work
branches.cn: astus 机巧的两种落点

branches.en: accurate reading of situations
branches.cn: 对局势的精准研判

branches.en: canny negotiation
branches.cn: 精明的周旋

intro.en: Astute keeps a single Latin root: craft of mind made into a word.
intro.cn: astute 保留单一拉丁词根：心智机巧凝成的词。

latinIntro.en: Latin astus, craft, is the whole family in one noun.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 astus（机巧）一词即整个词族。

definition_zh: 潟湖；礁湖（被沙洲、沙坝或珊瑚礁隔开的浅水水域）
definition_en: a shallow body of water separated from the open sea by a sandbar, spit or reef
core_image: 一道沙洲把外海的浪挡在外面，里面是一片浅浅的、几乎不动的水
scene: 沙洲把海湾隔出一片浅水，风浪进不来，水面平静得能映出云。 The lagoon behind the reef stays calm even in a storm.
sceneCN: 这里 lagoon 指「被礁或沙洲隔开的浅水区」（第 1 个义项：作为水体的潟湖整体）；句意为礁后的潟湖即使在风暴中也保持平静。

pos.zh: 潟湖；礁湖（可数，复数 lagoons）

derivatives.zh: lagoon + -al（形容词后缀）→ 潟湖的：属于潟湖环境的
lacuna（拉丁「水池、空隙」）→ 英语借词：空白、缺失（与 lagoon 同出拉丁 lacuna）
lake（拉丁 lacus「湖」经古法语进入英语）→ 湖（与 lagoon 共享 lacus 词根，但不是派生关系）
lagoon + side（复合名词）→ 潟湖一侧：朝向潟湖的岸段

senses.title: A shallow coastal water body
senses.titleCN: 海岸浅水：被隔开的水体
senses.definition: a shallow stretch of water cut off from the sea by a barrier
senses.definitionCN: 被障壁与海隔开的浅水区域
senses.example: The lagoon behind the reef stays calm even in a storm.
senses.exampleCN: 礁后的潟湖即使在风暴中也保持平静。
senses.why: the barrier is what defines the word: without something separating it from the open sea, shallow water is just shallow sea.
senses.whyCN: 障壁是这个词的定义要素：没有东西把它与外海隔开，浅水就只是浅海。

senses.title: The water inside an atoll
senses.definition: the water enclosed by a ring of coral reef
senses.definitionCN: 被环形珊瑚礁围住的水
senses.example: The atoll lagoon is green over white sand.
senses.exampleCN: 环礁潟湖在白色沙底上呈绿色。
senses.why: an atoll is a ring, and the water it holds is the clearest example of a lagoon.
senses.whyCN: 环礁是一个环，它围住的水正是潟湖最典型的例子。

senses.title: Water behind a sandbar
senses.definition: water trapped behind a beach ridge or spit
senses.definitionCN: 被海滩脊或沙嘴拦住的水
senses.example: Winter storms closed the lagoon mouth with sand.
senses.exampleCN: 冬季风暴用沙封住了潟湖口。
senses.why: a shifting sandbar can seal a river mouth or a bay, creating the still water the word names.
senses.whyCN: 移动的沙坝能封住河口或海湾，造出这个词所命名的静水。

senses.title: A water body with changing salinity
senses.definition: the water considered for its variable salt content and temperature
senses.definitionCN: 从盐度与温度变化角度考虑的水体
senses.example: The lagoon turns brackish after heavy rain.
senses.exampleCN: 大雨之后潟湖变成半咸水。
senses.why: limited exchange with the sea lets rain and evaporation change the water, so the word carries an implied chemistry.
senses.whyCN: 与海水的交换有限，雨水与蒸发因此能改变水质，这个词便隐含了一套化学特征。

senses.title: A nursery habitat
senses.definition: the sheltered water used by juvenile fish and seagrass
senses.definitionCN: 幼鱼与海草利用的受护水域
senses.example: Juvenile fish grow in the lagoon before moving offshore.
senses.exampleCN: 幼鱼在潟湖中长大，再游向外海。
senses.why: calm shallow water with plants is a nursery, so ecology uses the word for that function.
senses.whyCN: 平静的浅水与植物构成育幼场，因此生态学用这个词指那种功能。

senses.title: A stage in coastal infilling
senses.definition: the water body as a stage before it silts up into marsh or land
senses.definitionCN: 在淤积成沼泽或陆地之前的水体阶段
senses.example: The lagoon will become salt marsh within a century.
senses.exampleCN: 这个潟湖在一个世纪内会变成盐沼。
senses.why: sediment always arrives, so a lagoon is geologically temporary and the word can name that stage.
senses.whyCN: 沉积总会到来，因此潟湖在地质上只是暂时，词也可命名那个阶段。

senses.title: An artificial lagoon
senses.definition: a constructed shallow basin used for treatment, storage or recreation
senses.definitionCN: 为处理、储存或休闲而建的浅水池
senses.example: The plant settles solids in an artificial lagoon.
senses.exampleCN: 工厂在人工潟湖中沉降固体。
senses.why: the physical form, shallow still water behind a barrier, is easy to build, so the word extends to engineered basins.
senses.whyCN: 这种形态——障壁后的浅静水——容易建造，因此这个词扩展到工程池。

senses.title: A city built on water
senses.definition: the sheltered water around a historic canal city
senses.definitionCN: 围绕着历史运河城市的受护水域
senses.example: Venice stands on islands inside its lagoon.
senses.exampleCN: 威尼斯建在潟湖中的岛屿上。
senses.why: the Venetian lagoon is the best-known named example, so the word also evokes that urban water setting.
senses.whyCN: 威尼斯潟湖是最著名的专名例子，因此这个词也唤起那种城市水域场景。

intro.en: Lagoon came into English from Italian laguna, which goes back to Latin lacuna 'pool, hollow', a noun built on lacus 'lake'. The Latin root is secure; the chain through Italian is well documented. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: lagoon 从意大利语 laguna 进入英语，后者上溯拉丁 lacuna「水池、凹处」，该名词由 lacus「湖」构成。拉丁词根可靠，经意大利语的链条记载清楚。年代均为约数。

items.en: Lacus meant 'lake, basin' and is the source of Italian lago and French lac.
items.cn: lacus 意为「湖、盆地」，是意大利语 lago 与法语 lac 的来源。

items.en: Lacuna, a derivative of lacus, meant a hollow or a pool; it also gave English lacuna 'a gap'.
items.cn: lacuna 是 lacus 的派生词，意为凹处或水池；它也给出英语 lacuna「空白」。

items.en: Venetian and Italian laguna named the shallow protected water around Venice.
items.cn: 威尼斯方言与意大利语 laguna 指威尼斯周围受护的浅水。

items.en: English borrowed the word in the seventeenth century, first spelling it lagune and later lagoon.
items.cn: 英语于十七世纪借入这个词，先拼作 lagune，后作 lagoon。

items.en: Nineteenth-century geography extended lagoon from Venice to any shallow water behind a reef or bar.
items.cn: 十九世纪地理学把 lagoon 从威尼斯扩展到任何礁或沙坝后的浅水。

items.en: Source uncertain (derivation detail only): whether lacuna is a direct derivative of lacus or an independent formation is debated, so the link is best described as probable rather than proven.
items.cn: 来源不确定（仅派生细节存疑）：lacuna 究竟是 lacus 的直接派生还是独立构成，学界有争议，因此两者联系宜说成「可能」而非「已证」。

note.en: Group one holds the coastal water bodies most often confused with a lagoon; group two holds the general words for still inland water.
note.cn: 第一组是常与潟湖混淆的海岸水体；第二组是泛指静水的内陆水体词。

entries.definition: The ring of coral reef itself; a lagoon is the water inside such a ring.
entries.definitionCN: 指珊瑚礁环本身；潟湖是环里的水。

entries.definition: The tidal mouth of a river where fresh and salt water mix; it has an open connection to the sea, unlike a lagoon.
entries.definitionCN: 河流入海的潮汐河口，淡咸水混合；与潟湖不同，它向海敞开。

entries.definition: A broad inlet of the sea into the land; it remains connected to open water and is not cut off by a bar.
entries.definitionCN: 海伸入陆地的宽阔水域；与开阔水域相连，不被沙坝隔断。

entries.definition: Grass-covered muddy ground flooded by tides; it is often the later stage of a lagoon that has silted up.
entries.definitionCN: 受潮水淹没、长满草的泥地；常是潟湖淤积后的后期阶段。

entries.definition: A large body of water surrounded by land; it is usually fresh and inland, not coastal.
entries.definitionCN: 被陆地围绕的大片水域；通常为淡水且在内陆，而非海岸。

entries.definition: A small body of still water, often artificial; it has no connection to the sea.
entries.definitionCN: 小型静水，常为人工；与海没有联系。

entries.definition: A narrow arm of water reaching into land; it stresses the opening rather than the enclosed body.
entries.definitionCN: 伸入陆地的狭窄水域；强调开口，而非被围的水体。

entries.definition: Water cut off from the main flow, often by a bend or a barrier; it need not be coastal or saline.
entries.definitionCN: 与主流隔开的水，常由河湾或障壁造成；不必是海岸或咸水。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real Latin roots, real coastal terms and real stages, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的拉丁词根、真实的海岸术语与真实阶段，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: lacus is lake, lacuna is pool: lagoon is the little pool left behind the barrier.
normal.cn: lacus 是湖，lacuna 是水池：潟湖就是障壁后留下的小水池。

normal.en: The barrier decides the word: reef, sandbar or spit must separate it from the open sea.
normal.cn: 障壁决定这个词：必须有礁、沙坝或沙嘴把它与外海隔开。

normal.en: Atoll is the ring, lagoon is the water: the two words fit together like rim and cup.
normal.cn: 环礁是环，潟湖是水：两个词像杯沿与杯中水一样配套。

normal.en: Still water changes chemistry: rain dilutes it, sun concentrates it, exchange with the sea limits both.
normal.cn: 静水会改变化学：雨稀释它，太阳浓缩它，与海的交换又限制两者。

normal.en: A lagoon is temporary: sediment fills it and marsh follows.
normal.cn: 潟湖是暂时的：沉积填满它，沼泽随后而来。

abstract.en: A lagoon is the sea resting behind a door it cannot open.
abstract.cn: 潟湖是停在一扇它打不开的门后的海。

abstract.en: It is a shallow memory of the ocean, kept by sand.
abstract.cn: 它是海洋一段浅浅的记忆，由沙保存。

abstract.en: Calm here is borrowed time: the barrier will move.
abstract.cn: 这里的平静是借来的时间：障壁终会移动。

examples.en: The lagoon supports seagrass beds and juvenile fish.
examples.cn: 这片潟湖供养着海草床与幼鱼。

examples.en: Sand closed the lagoon mouth during the dry season.
examples.cn: 旱季时沙封住了潟湖口。

examples.en: The lagoon water warmed to thirty degrees in summer.
examples.cn: 夏季潟湖水温升到三十度。

dict_mnemonic.text: lagoon（潟湖）来自意大利 laguna，上溯拉丁 lacuna「水池」；记成「沙坝或礁后的一池浅水」，静、浅、盐度多变。

root: 意大利语 laguna ← 拉丁 lacuna「水池、凹处」← lacus「湖」；经法语或意大利语于十七世纪进入英语。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one sheltered water body: the coastal basin, the atoll's inner sea, the bar behind sand, its shifting chemistry, its nursery role, its silting stage, its artificial copy and its city setting.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项沿同一片受护水域展开：海岸盆地、环礁内海、沙坝后的水、变化的化学、育幼功能、淤积阶段、人工复制与城市水域。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: waves stop at a sandbar while the water behind it lies almost flat.
core.cn: 核心意象：浪停在沙洲外，沙洲后的水几乎不动。

branches.en: THREE BARRIERS: coast, coral ring and sandbar each enclose the same kind of water.
branches.cn: 三种障壁：海岸、珊瑚环与沙坝各自围出同一类水。

branches.en: CHEMISTRY: restricted exchange lets salinity and temperature drift.
branches.cn: 化学：交换受限使盐度与温度漂移。

branches.en: NURSERY: calm shallow water becomes a shelter for the young.
branches.cn: 育幼场：平静浅水成为幼体的庇护所。

branches.en: TEMPORARY AND BUILT: silt ends it, engineering copies it.
branches.cn: 暂时与仿建：淤积终结它，工程复制它。

branches.en: CITY WATER: a historic city makes the lagoon its ground.
branches.cn: 城市水域：一座历史城市把潟湖当作地基。

intro.en: Lagoon is a borrowed noun whose Latin ancestry is clear but whose English form carries no productive affix except the adjective ending -al.
intro.cn: lagoon 是借入名词，拉丁来源清楚，但英语形式除形容词后缀 -al 外不带能产词缀。

latinIntro.en: Lacus and lacuna are the Latin entries; Italian laguna is the intermediate form, not a Latin word.
latinIntro.cn: lacus 与 lacuna 是拉丁条目；意大利语 laguna 是中间形式，并非拉丁词。

items.structure: lacus, lacus (Latin noun, masculine, fourth declension)
items.example: Lacus is the source of Italian lago.
items.exampleCN: lacus 是意大利语 lago 的来源。

items.structure: lacuna, lacunae (Latin noun, feminine, first declension)
items.example: Lacuna passed into English as a word for a gap.
items.exampleCN: lacuna 作为「空白」义进入英语。

items.example: The Venetian laguna surrounds the old city.
items.exampleCN: 威尼斯潟湖环绕着老城。

items.example: The lagoon lies behind the barrier island.

items.meaning: of or belonging to a lagoon
items.exampleCN: 潟湖泥保存着细密的层理。

items.meaning: the opening where lagoon water meets the sea
items.meaningCN: 潟湖水与海相接的开口

items.meaning: a ridge of sand built by waves
items.example: A sandbar seals the lagoon in summer.
The estuary opens freely to the sea.

definition_zh: adj. 利他的；无私的；为他人利益着想的
definition_en: Showing a selfless concern for the welfare of others; motivated by the good of other people rather than by personal gain.
core_image: 把好处推给别人，自己退到后面
scene: 他把奖金全捐给了病房里的孩子，自己一分没留。 His altruistic gesture surprised the whole office.
sceneCN: 第 1 个义项：他把奖金捐出去，不为自己留任何好处。这种把他人利益放在前面的做法，就是 altruistic 所说的利他。

pos.zh: 利他的；无私的

forms.label: 无 -er/-est 形式（多音节形容词，用 more/most）

senses.title: Putting others first
senses.definition: motivated by the good of other people rather than by any benefit to oneself
senses.definitionCN: 以他人的好处而非自身所得为出发点的
senses.example: Her altruistic choice cost her a year of savings.
senses.exampleCN: 她这个利他的选择让她损失了一年的积蓄。
senses.why: The base is Latin alter, the other of two, so the word literally points away from the self and toward the other person.
senses.whyCN: 词根是拉丁语 alter「两者中的另一个」，所以这个词字面上就把手从自己指向了他人。

senses.title: In biology and ethics
senses.titleCN: 生物学与伦理学中的利他
senses.definition: describing behaviour that lowers the fitness or payoff of the actor while raising that of another
senses.definitionCN: 用于描述降低行动者自身适合度或收益、却提高他人收益的行为
senses.example: Altruistic grooming is common among related bats.
senses.exampleCN: 利他性的相互梳理在亲缘蝙蝠中很常见。
senses.why: Comte coined the noun as the opposite of egoism, and the sciences kept that strict sense: a real cost to the giver, a real gain to the receiver.
senses.whyCN: 孔德把这个名词造出来作为利己主义的反面，各门学科保留了这一严格含义：给予者确有损失，接受者确有收益。

intro.en: Altruistic is the adjective of altruism, a word Auguste Comte coined in French around 1830 from autrui, other people, which descends from Latin alter, the other of two.
intro.cn: altruistic 是 altruism 的形容词，而 altruism 是孔德约 1830 年在法语中造的词，来自 autrui「他人」，后者又源自拉丁语 alter「两者中的另一个」。

items.en: Latin alter meant the other of two. It is the base of the whole family: alternate, alternative and the phrase alter ego.
items.cn: 拉丁语 alter 意为「两者中的另一个」。它是整个词族的底座：alternate、alternative 以及短语 alter ego。

items.en: Old French autrui, other people, grew out of a Latin form built on alter, with the l turning into a u sound on the way.
items.cn: 古法语 autrui「他人」由建立在 alter 之上的拉丁语形式发展而来，途中 l 变成了 u 音。

items.en: Auguste Comte coined French altruisme around 1830 from autrui, pairing it against egoisme to name the principle of living for others.
items.cn: 孔德约 1830 年由 autrui 造出法语 altruisme，与 egoisme 相对，用来命名「为他人而活」的原则。

items.en: English took altruism in the mid nineteenth century, and George Henry Lewes spread it through his writing on Comte and positivism.
items.cn: 英语在 19 世纪中期借入 altruism，刘易斯通过介绍孔德与实证主义的著作把它推广开来。

items.en: Altruistic is the adjective built with -istic, now standard in ethics, psychology, evolutionary biology and ordinary praise of a generous act.
items.cn: altruistic 是用 -istic 构成的形容词，如今在伦理学、心理学、演化生物学以及对慷慨行为的日常称赞中都是标准用词。

note.en: The look-alike group keeps the altru- family and the -istic ending; the near-meaning group lists other words for putting others first.
note.cn: 形近组保留 altru- 词族与 -istic 词尾；近义组列出其他表示「把他人放在前面」的词。

entries.definition: The principle of living for others.
entries.definitionCN: 为他人而活的原则。

entries.definition: A person who acts for the good of others.
entries.definitionCN: 为他人利益行事的人。

entries.definition: Genuine and not copied.
entries.definitionCN: 真实的，非仿造的。

entries.definition: Showing skill in the arts.
entries.definitionCN: 在艺术方面有技巧的。

entries.definition: Caring more for others than for oneself.
entries.definitionCN: 关心他人多于关心自己。

entries.definition: Not putting oneself first.
entries.definitionCN: 不把自己放在第一位。

entries.definition: Giving help or money to good causes.
entries.definitionCN: 向公益提供帮助或金钱。

entries.definition: Kindly and wishing to do good.
entries.definitionCN: 仁慈并希望行善。

normalIntro.en: Altruistic hides alter, the other: the word literally turns you toward the other person.
normalIntro.cn: altruistic 里藏着 alter「他人」：这个词字面上就是把你转向另一个人。

normal.en: Alter means other, so altruistic means other-first.
normal.cn: alter 意为「他人」，所以 altruistic 就是「他人优先」。

normal.en: It is the opposite of egoistic, and Comte designed the pair.
normal.cn: 它是 egoistic 的反面，这一对是孔德有意设计的。

normal.en: Use more altruistic, not altruisticer: the word is too long for -er.
normal.cn: 用 more altruistic，不用 altruisticer：这个词太长，不加 -er。

normal.en: The noun is altruism, the person is an altruist.
normal.cn: 名词是 altruism，人是 altruist。

normal.en: Do not confuse altruistic with authentic: one is about others, one about truth.
normal.cn: 别把 altruistic 与 authentic 混淆：一个讲他人，一个讲真实。

abstract.en: Picture someone pushing the last chair at the table toward a stranger.
abstract.cn: 想象有人把桌边最后一把椅子推给陌生人。

abstract.en: Imagine a hand giving away the whole loaf and keeping the crumbs.
abstract.cn: 想象一只手把整条面包送出去，只留下碎屑。

abstract.en: Think of a bat grooming a cousin it will never see again.
abstract.cn: 想象一只蝙蝠为再也见不到的表亲梳理毛发。

examples.en: His altruistic motives were never in doubt.
examples.cn: 他的利他动机从未受到怀疑。

examples.en: The donation was purely altruistic, with no tax benefit.
examples.cn: 这笔捐赠纯粹是利他的，没有任何税收好处。

examples.en: She acted altruistically and asked for nothing back.
examples.cn: 她无私地行事，不求任何回报。

dict_mnemonic.text: 谐音「爱他如实」——爱他（altru）如实（istic）：实实在在地爱别人、不图回报，就是利他的、无私的。

root: 拉丁语 alter「两者中的另一个」经古法语 autrui「他人」，由孔德造出 altruisme，英语借为 altruism「利他主义」，再加 -istic 构成形容词 altruistic，字面即「把他人放在自己之前」。

sensesIntro.en: Both senses are the same outward turn: everyday praise for a generous motive, and the technical label for behaviour that costs the giver.
sensesIntro.cn: 两个义项是同一次向外的转身：日常里对慷慨动机的称赞，以及学术上对「给予者付出代价」的行为的标注。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: pushing the benefit to others and stepping back
core.cn: 核心意象：把好处推给别人，自己退到后面

branches.en: Giving away a bonus without a second thought.
branches.cn: 毫不犹豫地把奖金送出去。

branches.en: Choosing the harder road so a friend gains.
branches.cn: 选更难走的路，好让朋友获益。

branches.en: A worker bee that never breeds.
branches.cn: 一只从不繁殖的工蜂。

branches.en: Grooming that costs time and buys kinship.
branches.cn: 花时间梳理，换来亲缘关系。

branches.en: Both put the other before the self.
branches.cn: 两者都把他人放在自己之前。

intro.en: Altruistic is alter plus -ism plus -ist plus -istic, a chain that turns other into a description of character.
intro.cn: altruistic 是 alter 加 -ism 加 -ist 加 -istic，这条链把「他人」变成了对品格的描述。

latinIntro.en: Latin alter, the other of two, became Old French autrui; Comte built altruisme on it and English added the adjective ending.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 alter「两者中的另一个」变成古法语 autrui；孔德在其上造出 altruisme，英语再加形容词词尾。
